# Accessibility (A11y) (/docs/guide/accessibility)



What DiaX Guarantees [#what-diax-guarantees]

DiaX keeps node content in the DOM. Your headings, links, buttons, form controls and text therefore
remain available to browsers and assistive technology instead of being flattened into Canvas or one
opaque image.

The built-in adapters also provide 3 narrow guarantees:

* node wrappers receive stable DOM IDs and valid `aria-flowto` ID references;
* hover-only nodes and relations do not enter the tab order;
* a relation with `events.onClick` becomes a named SVG button with visible focus and Enter/Space
  activation.

DiaX does not infer a complete text alternative from graph geometry. The semantics, contrast and
accessible names of the DOM you render inside each node remain application responsibilities.

Start With a Named Region [#start-with-a-named-region]

Give each important diagram a visible heading and a short summary. This lets people find the diagram
by landmark or heading even when its spatial layout is not useful to them.

```tsx
<section aria-labelledby="deployment-heading">
  <h2 id="deployment-heading">Deployment Pipeline</h2>
  <p>Commits pass through build and review before production deployment.</p>

  <FlowDiagram nodes={nodes} relations={relations} />
</section>
```

If every relationship is necessary to understand the page, add an adjacent ordered list, table or
paragraph as the non-spatial explanation. Do not rely on arrow position, color or `aria-flowto` as the
only source of meaning.

Supplemental Relationship Metadata [#supplemental-relationship-metadata]

DiaX maps relations by injecting `aria-flowto` into each source node wrapper. Every referenced value
is also the target wrapper's DOM `id`, so the IDREF resolves inside the current diagram.

Support for `aria-flowto` varies across screen readers and browser combinations. Treat it as
supplemental metadata, not as a portable navigation command or a replacement for meaningful DOM
order.

When using `<FlowDiagram>` or `<Mindmap>`, the adapter binds this automatically. When composing a
headless renderer, preserve both the target `id` and the relationship metadata.

**React / Vue:**

```tsx
<div {...node.bindProps}>{node.data.content}</div>
```

**Solid:**

```tsx
<div
  id={node.resolvedId}
  data-diax-node={node.resolvedId}
  aria-flowto={node.ariaFlowTo}
  style={node.style}
>
  {node.data.content}
</div>
```

**Svelte:**

```svelte
<div
  id={node.resolvedId}
  data-diax-node={node.resolvedId}
  aria-flowto={node.ariaFlowTo}
  style={node.style}
>
  {node.data.content}
</div>
```

Namespaces & DOM IDs [#namespaces--dom-ids]

Use `namespace` when multiple diagrams can repeat local node IDs such as `api` or `database` on one
page. DiaX resolves both the wrapper `id` and every `aria-flowto` target with the same namespace.
Do not replace the generated `id` while retaining `aria-flowto`, or the relationship becomes a broken
ID reference.

Reading Order & Group Boundaries [#reading-order--group-boundaries]

Assistive technology follows DOM order, not arrow coordinates. Built-in Diagram adapters emit a
deterministic layout order; a two-dimensional graph still has no universally correct linear reading
order. Put the intended narrative before the diagram when sequence matters.

Node wrappers are semantic-transparent `<div>` elements. DiaX does not add `role="group"` to every
node because repeated anonymous groups create navigation noise. Render a native heading, list,
button or link inside a node when that meaning exists.

Nested group boundaries are derived visual surfaces. Their visible labels remain text, but the CSS
boundary does not claim to contain distant node DOM in the accessibility tree. Explain essential
containment in the region summary or in ordinary semantic HTML.

Interactive Edges [#interactive-edges]

A relation with `events.onClick` becomes an SVG control with `role="button"`, a deterministic
accessible name, a visible focus treatment and Enter/Space activation. The SVG drawing surface is
presentation-only, so it does not become an “image containing a button” in the accessibility tree.
Hover-only relations remain outside the tab order because visual emphasis is not an action.

Provide an explicit, localized `ariaLabel`. The fallback `Connection from {from} to {to}` is useful
for development but rarely matches product language, and visible rich-label content is not a
substitute for the control's name.

```tsx
const relations = [
  {
    from: 'review',
    to: 'evidence',
    label: '3 findings',
    ariaLabel: 'Open the 3 review findings',
    events: { onClick: openFindings },
  },
];
```

The default transparent pointer path is 24 CSS px wide. Increase `hitSlop` when the product requires
a more forgiving pointer target; keyboard focus and activation do not depend on that width.

High Contrast & Focus [#high-contrast--focus]

DiaX uses the system `Highlight` color for a focused edge while forced colors are active. Node cards,
icons and controls are authored DOM, so test their borders, text and focus states in the Windows High
Contrast themes your product supports.

Prefer system colors and allow the browser to adapt authored content:

```css
@media (forced-colors: active) {
  .service-card {
    color: CanvasText;
    background: Canvas;
    border: 1px solid CanvasText;
  }
}
```

Avoid `forced-color-adjust: none` unless preserving a specific color is essential and you have tested
the resulting contrast. `highlightOnHover` is visual emphasis only; put real actions on native
controls with their own `:focus-visible` treatment.

Reduced Motion & Zoom [#reduced-motion--zoom]

DiaX edge animations and the React/Solid stagger reveal respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Apply the
same policy to authored node animation:

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .my-diagram-animation {
    animation: none;
    transition: none;
  }
}
```

At 200% zoom, keep authored node text reflowable and avoid fixed canvas heights that clip the Grid or
edge labels.

Evidence Boundaries [#evidence-boundaries]

Different checks answer different questions:

| Evidence                                      | What it can establish                                            | What it cannot establish                        |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| DOM and accessibility-tree automation         | valid IDREFs, semantic roles, names, order and keyboard behavior | announcement quality or screen-reader shortcuts |
| Chromium forced-colors emulation              | CSS media-query coverage and obvious system-color regressions    | real Windows High Contrast rendering            |
| Firefox/WebKit automation                     | engine behavior, accessibility-tree and focus parity             | macOS Safari hardware behavior                  |
| VoiceOver, NVDA or JAWS on supported hardware | actual announcements and navigation                              | every user's assistive-technology configuration |

Do not report emulation as real assistive-technology or hardware acceptance.

Manual Acceptance Checklist [#manual-acceptance-checklist]

1. Navigate the page by headings and regions before entering the diagram.
2. Confirm the authored node controls have useful names and a logical Tab order.
3. Confirm each clickable edge announces the explicit `ariaLabel` and activates once with Enter and
   Space.
4. Confirm hover-only edges and node wrappers do not add tab stops or repeated anonymous groups.
5. Read the non-spatial summary without looking at the diagram and verify that no essential meaning
   is missing.
6. Repeat at 200% zoom, with reduced motion, in real Windows High Contrast and with the supported
   Safari + VoiceOver and Edge + NVDA combinations.


# Agent-first Workflow (/docs/guide/agent-workflow)



Start with the explanation the reader needs, not with a package or diagram family. DiaX gives an
agent a bounded path from intent to a reproducible web artifact while the application keeps control
of trust, presentation and delivery.

```text
question
  -> choose layout owner and trust boundary
  -> generate one bounded first artifact
  -> validate the exact authoring path
  -> repair diagnosed subjects only
  -> inspect the exact built preview
  -> review at the final use size
  -> export or share with artifact truth
```

This is one handoff journey across existing interfaces. It is not a new mode, workflow API or DiaX
CLI.

1\. State the communication job [#1-state-the-communication-job]

Give the agent the audience, the question the visual must answer and the destination. "Explain why
the launch decision is supported" is actionable. "Make an architecture diagram" leaves hierarchy,
evidence and reading order unspecified.

Then choose one existing recipe in the [AI Cookbook](/docs/guide/ai-cookbook). Reuse an existing
semantic Presentation role only when it matches the content; do not invent a component type for each
noun in the prompt.

2\. Choose layout owner and trust boundary [#2-choose-layout-owner-and-trust-boundary]

These are separate decisions:

| Source and job                                     | Layout owner            | Trust boundary               | Generate                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Topology is data                                   | DiaX Diagram            | Untrusted runtime input      | Constrained JSON with object relations      |
| Reviewed report, comparison or product composition | Application CSS         | Trusted repository source    | Connect JSX/HTML with centralized relations |
| Existing supported Mermaid source                  | DiaX after import       | Text parser diagnostics      | Mermaid text, then import                   |
| Reviewed Markdown build                            | Host MDX/build pipeline | Executable repository source | MDX plus build diagnostics                  |

Do not add manual positions to Diagram output or ask generated data to repair bend points. Do not
compile arbitrary model-produced JSX or MDX at an untrusted runtime boundary. The
[AI Integration guide](/docs/guide/ai-integration) contains the complete parsing and allowlist
contract.

3\. Bound the first artifact [#3-bound-the-first-artifact]

A useful first candidate normally has one primary reading path, 8–12 primary items or fewer, and
only branches that explain the question. This is authoring guidance, not a runtime limit. Start
smaller when the answer is smaller.

Require stable, short semantic IDs. Keep relation data centralized. Ask for a complete candidate,
but not for a complete universe: ornamental clusters, vendor identity, edge styling and secondary
metadata can follow after the structure proves useful.

4\. Validate the path that will ship [#4-validate-the-path-that-will-ship]

Validation depends on the authoring boundary:

* JSON: validate the parsed `unknown` value against an application schema, then run
  `validateDiagram()` for graph diagnostics.
* Connect JSX or trusted MDX: type-check and build the real host, then verify every relation target is
  present in the rendered DOM.
* Mermaid: keep importer diagnostics and reject unsupported families or syntax instead of guessing.
* Remark: surface structured VFile diagnostics in live preview and fail the production build under
  the host's selected strict policy.

This small boundary is safe to reuse after application-level structural validation:

```ts contract
import {
  DiaxValidationError,
  type DiaxEdge,
  type DiaxNode,
  validateDiagram,
} from 'diax';

export interface AcceptedDiagram {
  nodes: DiaxNode<string>[];
  relations: DiaxEdge<string>[];
}

export function acceptDiagram(candidate: AcceptedDiagram): AcceptedDiagram {
  const diagnostics = validateDiagram(candidate.nodes, candidate.relations);
  if (diagnostics.some(diagnostic => diagnostic.severity === 'error')) {
    throw new DiaxValidationError(diagnostics);
  }
  return candidate;
}
```

Do not pass arbitrary parsed JSON directly to this function. Structural limits, allowlists and
resource policy remain application responsibilities.

5\. Repair only diagnosed subjects [#5-repair-only-diagnosed-subjects]

Return diagnostic `code`, `path`, `message` and `hint` to the agent. Preserve valid IDs and content,
change the smallest invalid subject, then run the same validation again with a small retry limit.

DiaX's Playground and first-success benchmark derive a private repair protocol from those same
public diagnostics. For each diagnostic code it records four product-level facts: what valid work
must be preserved, the exact repair scope, one supported action and the validation stage to retry.
This keeps interactive guidance and agent evaluation consistent without adding repair policy to the
public `DiaxDiagnostic` interface. Applications can follow the same discipline with their own domain
rules; they should continue treating `hint` as the portable public suggestion.

Do not replace a graph because one endpoint is missing. Do not expose dummy nodes, waypoints or
routing knobs as repair controls. If the composition is wrong rather than invalid, revise the
communication structure or choose the correct layout owner.

Repair in dependency order so a later visual symptom is not patched over an earlier structural
cause:

1. schema, IDs, missing endpoints and unsupported input;
2. node or group overlap and the wrong layout owner;
3. paths through unrelated nodes and backward endpoint direction;
4. crossings, shared corridors, group-border runs and cramped route rhythm;
5. label clearance, clipping and final reading-size legibility.

The last three stages are maintainer/golden-artifact evidence from the private browser receipt, not
runtime authoring options. An agent should revise topology or composition and rerender; it should not
invent a bend point merely to silence one visual finding.

6\. Inspect the exact built preview [#6-inspect-the-exact-built-preview]

Source that compiles is not yet the artifact. Preview the package entries, fonts, CSS and framework
host that will actually render it. The Playground's **Live**, **Updating** and **Last good** states
make this distinction explicit: only **Live** represents the current source revision committed and
painted in the preview iframe.

[Open the Playground →](/playground)

When the artifact depends on a consumer application, build that application. A fixture rendered
from workspace source cannot prove that a packed package, remote chunk or production CSS path works.

7\. Review at the final use size [#7-review-at-the-final-use-size]

Use the [Visual Constitution](/docs/guide/visual-constitution) as the shared review contract. Check
reading order, long content, edge and group labels, narrow width, keyboard access, dark and forced
color behavior, reduced motion and the intended destination size.

A Showcase thumbnail proves selection-scale recognition. It does not prove that body text is
readable. A Playwright engine proves its captured browser facts. It does not prove hardware Safari,
screen-reader comprehension, a projector or print.

8\. Export or share with truth [#8-export-or-share-with-truth]

Prefer live DOM when the destination supports it. Use PNG for portable snapshots, browser print/PDF
for documents and SVG with `<foreignObject>` only for compatible web-aware destinations.

Export the current **Live** artifact, not an older successful preview under a newer source identity.
Keep its source/artifact hashes and human-review status with the receipt. A receipt proves identity
and named checks; it does not certify correctness or taste. See
[Export DOM Visuals](/docs/guide/exporting) for the complete capture contract.

Handoff definition of done [#handoff-definition-of-done]

| Stage      | Evidence to hand off                                                               |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Intent     | Audience, question and destination                                                 |
| Ownership  | Diagram or Connect decision plus executable/untrusted boundary                     |
| Candidate  | Bounded source with stable IDs and centralized relations                           |
| Validation | Structural/build result plus intact DiaX diagnostics                               |
| Preview    | Exact current revision rendered by the intended host                               |
| Review     | Named viewport, interaction, accessibility and destination checks                  |
| Delivery   | Live link or artifact bytes tied to source identity; remaining human review stated |

Reuse the existing context [#reuse-the-existing-context]

* [AI Authoring Context](/docs/guide/skills) — the checked-in Skill router and evidence boundary
* [AI Integration](/docs/guide/ai-integration) — untrusted JSON, validation and repair
* [AI Cookbook](/docs/guide/ai-cookbook) — question-first Diagram and Connect recipes
* [Playground](/playground) — current-revision preview, diagnostics and export
* [Export DOM Visuals](/docs/guide/exporting) — artifact and receipt truth
* [Package Entry Points](/docs/reference/package-entry-points) — exact loading boundaries


# AI Cookbook (/docs/guide/ai-cookbook)



Classify the visual before generating code [#classify-the-visual-before-generating-code]

The most important AI decision is not color or arrow style. It is who owns layout.

| User intent                       | Generate                    | Why                                                       |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| System architecture or call graph | Diagram JSON                | Topology should determine placement                       |
| Organization tree or mind map     | Diagram JSON                | Hierarchy is the visual structure                         |
| Existing Mermaid content          | Mermaid source, then import | Preserve portable text input                              |
| Decision with evidence cards      | Reviewed Connect JSX        | Report composition should remain authored DOM             |
| KPI cards with causal arrows      | Reviewed Connect JSX        | Metrics need responsive CSS and semantic HTML             |
| Before / After comparison         | Reviewed Connect JSX        | Columns and annotations own the story                     |
| Promotion timeline or roadmap     | Reviewed Connect JSX        | Time, prose and milestones need deliberate composition    |
| Reusable application graph        | Diagram data + `nodeTypes`  | Data remains serializable; presentation stays allowlisted |

Use JSON at an untrusted runtime boundary. Generate JSX only in a trusted repository workflow where
the result is reviewed like application code.

This page supplies question-first recipes. Use the
[Agent-first Workflow](/docs/guide/agent-workflow) to carry the selected recipe through validation,
the exact built preview, final-use-size review and truthful export or sharing.

<ScenarioCorpus />

Prompt: choose the interface first [#prompt-choose-the-interface-first]

Give an agent this policy before asking for implementation:

```text
Classify the requested visual before writing code:

1. If topology should decide placement, output a DiaX Diagram Definition as JSON.
2. If JSX/CSS should decide placement, output reviewed React code using
   @diax/react/connect with centralized relations.
3. Do not invent a mode prop or mix Diagram nodes with Connect targets.
4. Keep every semantic ID stable, short, and unique.
5. Prefer object relations in generated output.
6. Explain the selected layout owner in one sentence, then output the artifact.
```

Recipe: system architecture [#recipe-system-architecture]

Generate a serializable Diagram Definition. Keep framework content and styling out of the model:

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "web", "content": "Web App", "type": "client" },
    { "id": "gateway", "content": "API Gateway", "type": "service" },
    { "id": "orders", "content": "Order Service", "type": "service" },
    { "id": "db", "content": "PostgreSQL", "type": "database" }
  ],
  "relations": [
    { "from": "web", "to": "gateway", "label": "HTTPS" },
    { "from": "gateway", "to": "orders", "label": "gRPC" },
    { "from": "orders", "to": "db", "label": "SQL" }
  ]
}
```

The application validates the JSON and owns the visual allowlist:

```tsx contract
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react';

const nodeTypes = {
  client: ({ content }: { content: React.ReactNode }) => <article>{content}</article>,
  service: ({ content }: { content: React.ReactNode }) => <section>{content}</section>,
  database: ({ content }: { content: React.ReactNode }) => <code>{content}</code>,
};

export function Architecture({ nodes, relations }: {
  nodes: Array<{ id: string; content: string; type: keyof typeof nodeTypes }>;
  relations: Array<{ from: string; to: string; label?: string }>;
}) {
  return <FlowDiagram nodes={nodes} relations={relations} nodeTypes={nodeTypes} />;
}
```

Recipe: grounded RAG architecture [#recipe-grounded-rag-architecture]

Treat retrieval as an architecture question, not as a new DiaX mode. Start from two independently
owned paths:

* the **online question path** authorizes intent, checks a policy-aware cache, retrieves and reranks
  evidence, then preserves citation identity in the answer;
* the **versioned knowledge path** chunks reviewed sources, records revisions and access metadata,
  then updates the durable index consumed by retrieval.

Use ordinary Diagram nodes and relations because the topology should determine placement. Semantic
groups can name the two paths and their shared parent system; `SystemNode`, `DataStoreNode` and
`EvidenceNode` remain replaceable DOM presentation. A cache return or reranker feedback relation is
an ordinary stable edge, not a hand-authored bend point.

Before generating the artifact, require the authorization boundary, cache key, index revision,
retrieval contract and citation identity as verified facts. Do not invent `RagDiagram`, retriever
node types in Core, coordinates or a vendor-logo registry.

At narrow reading widths, keep node metadata, group titles and relation labels at their intended
size and make the wide canvas explicitly horizontally scrollable. Do not scale thirteen rich nodes
down until the topology fits 320px: that produces a recognizable thumbnail, not a readable system
review.

[Study the complete automatic RAG specimen →](/showcase/rag-grounding-system)

Recipe: decision and evidence [#recipe-decision-and-evidence]

The author controls a responsive report grid; DiaX only connects the semantic cards:

```tsx contract
import { ConnectionSurface, connectionTarget } from '@diax/react/connect';

const relations = [
  { from: 'problem', to: 'evidence', label: 'measured by' },
  { from: 'evidence', to: 'decision', label: 'supports' },
];

export function DecisionStory() {
  return (
    <ConnectionSurface relations={relations} className="grid gap-16 lg:grid-cols-3">
      <article {...connectionTarget('problem')}><h2>Problem</h2><p>Checkout latency</p></article>
      <article {...connectionTarget('evidence')}><h2>Evidence</h2><strong>-38%</strong></article>
      <article {...connectionTarget('decision')}><h2>Decision</h2><p>Expand rollout</p></article>
    </ConnectionSurface>
  );
}
```

Keep relation data near the surface. Do not hide outgoing arrows inside individual cards.

Recipe: promotion timeline [#recipe-promotion-timeline]

Use CSS for the timeline and Connect for cross-milestone causality:

```tsx contract
import { ConnectionSurface, connectionTarget } from '@diax/react/connect';

const milestones = [
  { id: 'baseline', quarter: 'Q1', title: 'Established baseline' },
  { id: 'platform', quarter: 'Q2', title: 'Shipped platform' },
  { id: 'impact', quarter: 'Q3', title: 'Scaled impact' },
];

export function PromotionTimeline() {
  return (
    <ConnectionSurface
      relations={[
        { from: 'baseline', to: 'platform' },
        { from: 'platform', to: 'impact', label: 'enabled' },
      ]}
      className="grid gap-12 md:grid-cols-3"
    >
      {milestones.map(item => (
        <article key={item.id} {...connectionTarget(item.id)}>
          <small>{item.quarter}</small><h2>{item.title}</h2>
        </article>
      ))}
    </ConnectionSurface>
  );
}
```

This is the right place for an array-to-DOM map: the array describes authored cards, while the
centralized relations describe connections. It is not the noisy `DiaxNode` / `DiaxEdge` marker loop.

Recipe: Mermaid enhancement [#recipe-mermaid-enhancement]

Keep Mermaid when portable text is valuable. Import the supported topology, then apply DiaX DOM
renderers or migrate selected nodes into richer presentation primitives. Do not claim that DiaX can
import Mermaid `sequenceDiagram`, Gantt or timeline syntax. A React sequence-style protocol is a
separate Connect recipe built from measured message rows and an ordered transcript.

[See supported Mermaid families →](/docs/guide/mermaid)

[See the DOM-native sequence recipe →](/docs/react/connect#sequence-style-protocols-without-a-sequence-mode)

Recipe: repository-grounded architecture evidence [#recipe-repository-grounded-architecture-evidence]

For source-code architecture reviews, citations are authored facts—not inferred graph metadata.
Resolve and verify them in an agent or build workflow before rendering:

```ts
const repositoryEvidence = {
  repository: 'https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify',
  revision: '3e0f4d8382c500c286fe5d5d29ec28597ed58c7c',
  sources: [
    {
      path: 'archify/SKILL.md',
      line: 15,
      endLine: 37,
      label: 'Bounded authoring contract',
    },
  ],
};
```

The authoring step must verify the public HTTPS repository, full 40-character commit, blob, and
line range before producing a stable link. Missing evidence fails closed. After that check, pass the
trusted link into `EvidenceNode` and use Connect only for a declared relation such as “supports this
decision.” DiaX Core and framework adapters do not need Git, filesystem, GitHub, or network access.

Do not turn file proximity or dependency reachability into an unverified runtime-impact claim.

[Inspect the complete repository-evidence specimen →](/showcase/repository-evidence-map)

Repeatability checklist [#repeatability-checklist]

* Stable IDs survive prompt retries and content edits.
* Object relations make repair paths explicit.
* Generated JSON has product-specific size and type limits.
* JSX generation happens only in a reviewed code workflow.
* One surface has exactly one layout owner.
* The result uses semantic HTML before decorative wrappers.
* Long text, empty content, mobile width and dark mode are part of acceptance.
* Export is deterministic; screenshots are outputs, not the source of truth.

<Callout type="info">
  The goal is not to make AI draw pixels more creatively. It is to give AI a constrained,
  inspectable web-native language whose output can be repaired and reproduced.
</Callout>


# AI Integration (/docs/guide/ai-integration)



Choose the Trust Boundary First [#choose-the-trust-boundary-first]

DiaX gives an AI two useful output modes with different security properties:

* **Untrusted or automated output:** generate JSON with string content and object-form edges, validate
  it, then pass the validated fields to DiaX.
* **Trusted authored output:** generate or edit MDX/JSX in a reviewed code workflow, where normal React
  components and Tailwind classes can provide richer presentation.

<Callout type="warn">
  MDX and JSX are executable code, not a safe serialization format. Never compile, import or evaluate
  model-generated MDX/JSX from an untrusted request inside your application process. Use JSON for that
  boundary, or run code generation in a reviewed and appropriately sandboxed workflow.
</Callout>

***

LLM JSON → FlowDiagram [#llm-json--flowdiagram]

Ask the model for a constrained JSON object. Prefer object-form edges: `from`, `to` and `label` remain
separate fields, so a validator and a repair loop can identify the exact failure without reparsing a
compact string.

```json title="LLM Output"
{
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "browser", "content": "Browser" },
    { "id": "api", "content": "API Server" },
    { "id": "db", "content": "Database" }
  ],
  "relations": [
    { "from": "browser", "to": "api", "label": "HTTPS" },
    { "from": "api", "to": "db", "label": "SQL" }
  ]
}
```

Treat parsed JSON as `unknown`. Validate its structure with an application-owned JSON Schema, Zod,
Valibot or equivalent, then use DiaX validation for graph-level problems such as duplicate IDs and
missing endpoints:

DiaX publishes a baseline schema at `diax/schemas/diax.json`. An AI-facing schema should usually be
narrower—for example, require object-form edges and a small allowlist of node types.

```tsx contract
import {
  DiaxValidationError,
  type DiaxEdge,
  type DiaxNode,
  validateDiagram,
} from 'diax';
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react';

interface GeneratedDiagram {
  nodes: DiaxNode<string>[];
  relations: DiaxEdge<string>[];
}

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null;
}

function parseGeneratedDiagram(modelText: string): GeneratedDiagram {
  const candidate: unknown = JSON.parse(modelText);
  if (!isRecord(candidate) || !Array.isArray(candidate.nodes) || !Array.isArray(candidate.relations)) {
    throw new Error('Expected an object with nodes and relations arrays.');
  }
  if (candidate.nodes.length > 50 || candidate.relations.length > 100) {
    throw new Error('Generated diagram exceeds the 50-node or 100-relation limit.');
  }

  const nodes = candidate.nodes.map((node, index): DiaxNode<string> => {
    if (!isRecord(node) || typeof node.id !== 'string' || typeof node.content !== 'string') {
      throw new Error(`nodes[${index}] requires string id and content fields.`);
    }
    return { id: node.id, content: node.content };
  });

  const relations = candidate.relations.map((relation, index): DiaxEdge<string> => {
    if (!isRecord(relation) || typeof relation.from !== 'string' || typeof relation.to !== 'string') {
      throw new Error(`relations[${index}] requires string from and to fields.`);
    }
    if (relation.label !== undefined && typeof relation.label !== 'string') {
      throw new Error(`relations[${index}].label must be a string when present.`);
    }
    return {
      from: relation.from,
      to: relation.to,
      ...(relation.label === undefined ? {} : { label: relation.label }),
    };
  });

  return { nodes, relations };
}

export function GeneratedFlow({ modelText }: { modelText: string }) {
  const diagram = parseGeneratedDiagram(modelText);
  const diagnostics = validateDiagram(diagram.nodes, diagram.relations);

  if (diagnostics.some(diagnostic => diagnostic.severity === 'error')) {
    throw new DiaxValidationError(diagnostics);
  }

  return <FlowDiagram nodes={diagram.nodes} relations={diagram.relations} />;
}
```

The example deliberately implements a narrow product schema so it runs without a hidden validator.
In a larger application, replace `parseGeneratedDiagram()` with Ajv, Zod, Valibot or an equivalent
runtime validator. Keep the same product-specific limits and allowlists. React escapes string
content, but validation is still required for correctness, resource limits and application policy.

***

Trusted MDX + Tailwind + DiaX [#trusted-mdx--tailwind--diax]

For repository content that is code-reviewed and built like the rest of the application, AI can draft
complete MDX pages with embedded DiaX diagrams styled with Tailwind:

```mdx title="ai-generated-page.mdx"
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react';

# System Architecture

<FlowDiagram
  nodes={[
    {
      id: 'api',
      content: (
        <div className="px-4 py-2 bg-blue-500/10 rounded-xl border border-blue-500/20 text-blue-300">
          API Gateway
        </div>
      ),
    },
    { id: 'auth', content: 'Auth Service' },
    { id: 'db', content: 'PostgreSQL' },
  ]}
  relations={[
    { from: 'api', to: 'auth', label: 'gRPC' },
    { from: 'auth', to: 'db', label: 'Query' },
  ]}
  theme="light"
  density="spacious"
/>
```

This pattern works because:

* **DiaX topology is data-driven** — IDs, nodes and object edges are easy to validate and repair.
* **Tailwind classes are composable** — trusted source can use an existing design system.
* **MDX combines prose and JSX** — useful in a reviewed authoring pipeline, not as an untrusted runtime payload.

***

AI Agent Best Practices [#ai-agent-best-practices]

1\. Default to object edges [#1-default-to-object-edges]

Object edges cost a few more tokens but produce better diagnostics and avoid escaping or delimiter
ambiguity. Reserve the string shorthand for trusted, hand-authored diagrams where terseness matters.

```ts
// Preferred AI output: explicit fields are easy to validate and repair.
relations: [
  { from: 'a', to: 'b' },
  { from: 'b', to: 'c' },
  { from: 'c', to: 'd', label: 'output' },
]; // [!code highlight]

// Concise shorthand remains available for trusted source.
relations: ['a->b', 'b->c', 'c->|output|d'];
```

2\. Keep rendering choices application-owned [#2-keep-rendering-choices-application-owned]

Register a small allowlist of `nodeTypes` and themes in application code. Let the model select a known
type or preset; do not let untrusted JSON inject arbitrary JSX, imports or component names.

```tsx
<FlowDiagram theme="notion" nodes={nodes} relations={relations} />
```

3\. Do not let the model invent vendor identity [#3-do-not-let-the-model-invent-vendor-identity]

Treat a provider or product mark as optional presentation, not graph semantics. The model may select
an application-approved provider ID only when the source text names it unambiguously. Application
code maps that ID to a trusted `NodeCard.icon`, `ActorNode.avatar` or `nodeTypes` renderer.

Use these generation rules:

```text
Allowed provider IDs: sourceHost, cloudPrimary.
Emit a provider ID only when the request names an exact allowlisted provider.
If identity is missing or uncertain, omit the provider ID.
Never emit an icon import, SVG payload, data URL or remote logo URL.
Keep the visible node name and semantic type meaningful without the mark.
```

Icons and avatars should normally be decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`); the visible node name owns
the accessible identity. The application owns the asset source, license/trademark review, targeted
import and bundle cost. DiaX does not fetch logos or ship a vendor catalogue. See the
[vendor identity recipe](/docs/ui-react/presentation-recipes#vendor-identity-decorates-a-semantic-role)
for a compiled `nodeTypes` example with an explicit fallback.

4\. Choose one layout owner [#4-choose-one-layout-owner]

When the model is explaining topology, generate a Diagram Definition and let DiaX place it. Do not
smuggle manual positions into an automatic Diagram:

```tsx
// Good — let DiaX compute positions
<FlowDiagram nodes={nodes} relations={relations} density="spacious" /> // [!code highlight]

// Avoid — manual positioning is fragile
<FlowDiagram nodes={nodes.map(n => ({ ...n, position: { col: 1, row: 1 } }))} /> // [!code --]
```

When the expression is a report, comparison, code walkthrough, mock UI or other authored
composition, let JSX/CSS own layout and use the isolated Connect leaf for geometry:

```tsx
import { ConnectionSurface, connectionTarget } from '@diax/react/connect';

<ConnectionSurface relations={[{ from: 'claim', to: 'evidence', label: 'because' }]}>
  <section {...connectionTarget('claim')} className="rounded-2xl border p-6">
    <h3>Claim</h3>
    <MetricCard />
  </section>
  <aside {...connectionTarget('evidence')} className="rounded-xl bg-slate-50 p-4">
    <EvidenceTable />
  </aside>
</ConnectionSurface>
```

Do not combine these into a generated `mode` prop. The model should decide from the job: topology
data → Diagram; authored DOM composition → Connect. Keep relations centralized in both cases.

5\. Feed diagnostics back to the model [#5-feed-diagnostics-back-to-the-model]

Keep `code`, `path`, `message` and `hint` intact when asking an agent to repair invalid output. Do not
reduce diagnostics to one generic "diagram failed" string: field-level feedback is what makes an AI
loop predictable.

```ts contract
import type { DiaxDiagnostic } from 'diax';

export function createRepairPrompt(
  invalidJson: string,
  diagnostics: readonly DiaxDiagnostic[],
): string {
  return `Repair this DiaX Diagram JSON.

Rules:
- Return JSON only.
- Preserve valid node IDs and content.
- Change only fields required by the diagnostics.
- Every relation endpoint must reference an existing node ID.

Diagnostics:
${JSON.stringify(diagnostics, null, 2)}

Invalid JSON:
${invalidJson}`;
}
```

Run the repaired response through the same structural and graph validation again. Set a small retry
limit and show the final diagnostics to the author instead of silently rendering a partial graph.

The Playground's JSON and Mermaid editors use the same focused policy for interactive authoring:
validate before render, preserve the first diagnostic subject and show one supported next edit. The
projection remains private to the product surface—it is not a second public diagnostic interface,
and it never exposes routing coordinates as an AI repair control.

Internally, the Playground and Agent first-success verifier share one versioned repair catalog for
Core diagnostic codes. It binds **preserve policy → repair scope → supported action → retry stage**
and includes the catalog hash in verifier identity. This is evidence that DiaX's own product paths do
not drift; it is not a catalog export, a schema extension or a requirement for application agents.

***

LLM-Friendly Documentation [#llm-friendly-documentation]

DiaX documentation is designed for AI consumption:

* **`/llms.txt`** — Machine-readable index of all documentation pages
* **`/llms-full.txt`** — Full processed text of all pages
* **`/docs/*.mdx`** — Per-page Markdown content via the `.mdx` extension
* **Page Actions** — Copy Markdown and Open in AI buttons on every doc page

***

Next Steps [#next-steps]

* [Agent-first Workflow](/docs/guide/agent-workflow) — Carry the task through built preview, visual review and artifact delivery
* [AI Cookbook](/docs/guide/ai-cookbook) — Choose Diagram or Connect for architecture, promotion, KPI, roadmap, and comparison stories
* [MDX Guide](/docs/guide/mdx-guide) — Complete guide to using DiaX in MDX files

# Comparison (/docs/guide/comparison)





Feature Comparison [#feature-comparison]

| Capability                   | DiaX                                                                      | React Flow                                       | Mermaid                                                         | D2                                       |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| **Primary job**              | DOM-native application diagrams                                           | Interactive React node editors                   | Portable text-to-SVG diagrams                                   | Text compiled to static diagrams         |
| **Node presentation**        | Application-owned DOM/components                                          | Custom React nodes                               | Renderer-controlled SVG/HTML labels                             | Renderer-controlled SVG with rich labels |
| **Layout ownership**         | Automatic Diagram mode; public React Connect leaf for authored DOM        | Positioned canvas nodes with layout integrations | Diagram-family renderer                                         | Compiler and selected layout engine      |
| **Authoring input**          | Typed objects with JSX content, supported Mermaid import                  | Application data and React components            | Mermaid DSL                                                     | D2 DSL                                   |
| **Framework story**          | Framework-agnostic Core; five Alpha adapters with disclosed parity limits | React                                            | Embeddable rendered output                                      | CLI/embedded rendered output             |
| **Drag/pan/zoom editor**     | Outside the 1.0 goal                                                      | Core product capability                          | Not the primary job                                             | Not the primary job                      |
| **Server rendering**         | Topology/Grid markup on server; pixel edges after client measurement      | Depends on integration                           | Commonly rendered client-side or pre-rendered by an integration | Static output is a primary workflow      |
| **Generated-input boundary** | JSON schema + graph diagnostics; reviewed JSX/MDX only                    | Application-defined                              | Text parser diagnostics                                         | Text parser diagnostics                  |

***

When to Use What [#when-to-use-what]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Use DiaX when you need...">
    * **Diagram-as-code** in a web app — define diagrams with JSON or JSX, not a visual editor
    * **Dependency-light core** — no runtime dependencies, with package size tracked in the repository
    * **Full styling control** — every node is a real DOM element you can style with Tailwind, CSS modules, or any CSS-in-JS
    * **Framework flexibility** — a framework-agnostic Core with Alpha adapters that are converging on a shared contract
    * **AI-generated diagrams** — validated JSON or a supported Mermaid subset, with explicit diagnostics
    * **SSR-aware output** — topology and Grid markup can render on the server; measured SVG edges complete on the client
  </Card>

  <Card title="Use React Flow when you need...">
    * **Interactive node editing** — users drag, connect, and rearrange nodes in real time
    * **Visual programming** — workflow builders, pipeline editors, node-based UIs
    * **Built-in controls** — minimap, zoom controls, background grid out of the box
    * **Large graph handling** — virtualized rendering for hundreds of nodes
  </Card>

  <Card title="Use Mermaid when you need...">
    * **Quick diagrams from text** — write a few lines of Mermaid DSL, get a diagram
    * **Markdown integration** — many Markdown renderers support Mermaid natively
    * **No framework dependency** — works anywhere you can embed an SVG
    * **Portable sequence or Gantt text** — Mermaid has mature DSLs for families DiaX does not import;
      DiaX can compose a DOM-native React sequence with Connect, but it is not Mermaid-compatible text
  </Card>

  <Card title="Use D2 when you need...">
    * **Standalone diagram files** — compile `.d2` files into SVG/PNG in CI/CD
    * **Rich text labels** — D2 supports Markdown inside node labels
    * **Automatic layout engines** — ELK, dagre built-in with fine-grained control
    * **No web dependency** — runs as a CLI binary, no browser required
  </Card>
</Cards>

***

Positioning Summary [#positioning-summary]

<DiagramPreview
  title="Where DiaX fits in the ecosystem"
  code="`<Mindmap
nodes={[
  { id: 'diax', content: 'DiaX' },
  { id: 'mermaid', content: 'Mermaid' },
  { id: 'd2', content: 'D2' },
  { id: 'reactflow', content: 'React Flow' },
  { id: 'headless', content: 'Headless' },
  { id: 'static', content: 'Static' },
  { id: 'code', content: 'Code-defined' },
]}
relations={[
  'diax->headless', 'diax->code', 'diax->static',
  'mermaid->static', 'mermaid->code',
  'd2->static', 'd2->code',
  'reactflow->headless',
]}
density=&#x22;comfortable&#x22;
/>`"
>
  <Mindmap
    nodes="[
    { id: 'diax', content: 'DiaX' },
    { id: 'mermaid', content: 'Mermaid' },
    { id: 'd2', content: 'D2' },
    { id: 'reactflow', content: 'React Flow' },
    { id: 'headless', content: 'Headless' },
    { id: 'static', content: 'Static' },
    { id: 'code', content: 'Code-defined' },
  ]"
    relations="[
    'diax->headless',
    'diax->code',
    'diax->static',
    'mermaid->static',
    'mermaid->code',
    'd2->static',
    'd2->code',
    'reactflow->headless',
  ]"
    density="comfortable"
  />
</DiagramPreview>

DiaX occupies a focused space: **DOM-native, code-defined application diagrams**. Choose it when a
node must remain part of your application UI and automatic layout or DOM connection removes real
graph mechanics. Choose Mermaid for broad portable text coverage, React Flow for an interactive
canvas editor, and D2 for a compiler-first static diagram workflow.


# DSL Syntax (/docs/guide/dsl)





String DSL [#string-dsl]

DiaX supports a mermaid-like string DSL for defining relations between nodes:

```text title="DSL Quick Reference"
a->b          Solid arrow
a-->b         Dashed arrow
a<->b         Bidirectional solid
a<-->b        Bidirectional dashed
a->|label|b   Arrow with label
a-->|label|b  Dashed arrow with label
```

<DiagramPreview
  title="String DSL — All arrow types"
  code="`<FlowDiagram
nodes={[
  { id: 'a', content: 'A' },
  { id: 'b', content: 'B' },
  { id: 'c', content: 'C' },
  { id: 'd', content: 'D' },
  { id: 'e', content: 'E' },
  { id: 'f', content: 'F' },
]}
relations={[
  'a->b',             // solid
  'b-->c',            // dashed
  'c<->d',            // bidirectional
  'd->|label|e',      // labeled
  'e-->|dashed|f',    // dashed + labeled
]}
density=&#x22;spacious&#x22;
/>`"
>
  <FlowDiagram
    nodes="[
    { id: 'a', content: 'A' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'B' },
    { id: 'c', content: 'C' },
    { id: 'd', content: 'D' },
    { id: 'e', content: 'E' },
    { id: 'f', content: 'F' },
  ]"
    relations="['a->b', 'b-->c', 'c<->d', 'd->|label|e', 'e-->|dashed|f']"
    density="spacious"
  />
</DiagramPreview>

Examples [#examples]

```ts
const relations = [
  'src->build', // solid arrow
  'build-->test', // dashed arrow
  'api<->db', // bidirectional
  'gw->|gRPC|auth', // labeled arrow
];
```

***

Object Form [#object-form]

For full control over edge styling, use typed objects:

```ts
const relations = [
  { from: 'a', to: 'b', style: 'dashed', color: '#5E6AD2', animate: 'flow' },
  { from: 'b', to: 'c', label: 'next', bidirectional: true },
];
```

Object Properties [#object-properties]

| Property        | Type                  | Description                     |
| --------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `from`          | `string`              | Source node ID (required)       |
| `to`            | `string`              | Target node ID (required)       |
| `label`         | `string`              | Edge label text                 |
| `style`         | `'solid' \| 'dashed'` | Line style (default: `'solid'`) |
| `color`         | `string`              | Edge color (CSS color value)    |
| `animate`       | `string`              | Animation preset name           |
| `bidirectional` | `boolean`             | Show arrows on both ends        |

***

Mixing Styles [#mixing-styles]

You can mix string DSL and object form in the same `relations` array:

```ts
const relations = [
  'a->b', // string DSL
  { from: 'b', to: 'c', animate: 'flow' }, // object form
  'c->|deploy|d', // string with label
  { from: 'd', to: 'e', style: 'dashed', color: '#4CAF50' },
];
```

The parser automatically detects the format and handles both transparently.

<DiagramPreview
  title="Mixed styles — string DSL + object form"
  code="`<FlowDiagram
nodes={[
  { id: 'a', content: 'Source' },
  { id: 'b', content: 'Build' },
  { id: 'c', content: 'Test' },
  { id: 'd', content: 'Stage' },
  { id: 'e', content: 'Prod' },
]}
relations={[
  'a->b',
  { from: 'b', to: 'c', animate: 'flow' },
  'c->|deploy|d',
  { from: 'd', to: 'e', style: 'dashed', color: '#4CAF50' },
]}
centered density=&#x22;spacious&#x22;
/>`"
>
  <FlowDiagram
    nodes="[
    { id: 'a', content: 'Source' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'Build' },
    { id: 'c', content: 'Test' },
    { id: 'd', content: 'Stage' },
    { id: 'e', content: 'Prod' },
  ]"
    relations="[
    'a->b',
    { from: 'b', to: 'c', animate: 'flow' },
    'c->|deploy|d',
    { from: 'd', to: 'e', style: 'dashed', color: '#4CAF50' },
  ]"
    density="spacious"
  />
</DiagramPreview>

  <Card title="Edge Types" href="/docs/guide/edge-types" description="Animation presets, path types, and custom labels" />

  <Card title="Themes" href="/docs/guide/themes" description="Built-in themes and CSS variable customization" />

# Edge Types (/docs/guide/edge-types)





Animation Presets [#animation-presets]

DiaX includes 5 built-in edge animation presets that bring your diagrams to life:

| Preset            | Effect                      | Best for                       |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `flow`            | Flowing dots along the path | Data flow, pipelines           |
| `pulse`           | Pulsing glow effect         | Active connections, heartbeats |
| `shimmer`         | Shimmering highlight        | Loading states, processing     |
| `reverse-flow`    | Dots flowing in reverse     | Feedback loops, returns        |
| `reverse-shimmer` | Reverse shimmer effect      | Reverse processing             |

<DiagramPreview
  name="animated-edges"
  title="Animation presets"
  code="`<FlowDiagram
nodes={[
  { id: 'a', content: 'flow' },
  { id: 'b', content: 'pulse' },
  { id: 'c', content: 'shimmer' },
  { id: 'd', content: 'reverse-flow' },
  { id: 'e', content: 'target' },
]}
relations={[
  { from: 'a', to: 'e', animate: 'flow' },
  { from: 'b', to: 'e', animate: 'pulse' },
  { from: 'c', to: 'e', animate: 'shimmer' },
  { from: 'd', to: 'e', animate: 'reverse-flow' },
]}
centered density=&#x22;spacious&#x22;
/>`"
>
  <FlowDiagram
    nodes="[
    { id: 'a', content: 'flow' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'pulse' },
    { id: 'c', content: 'shimmer' },
    { id: 'd', content: 'reverse-flow' },
    { id: 'e', content: 'target' },
  ]"
    relations="[
    { from: 'a', to: 'e', animate: 'flow' },
    { from: 'b', to: 'e', animate: 'pulse' },
    { from: 'c', to: 'e', animate: 'shimmer' },
    { from: 'd', to: 'e', animate: 'reverse-flow' },
  ]"
    density="spacious"
  />
</DiagramPreview>

Usage [#usage]

Apply animations via the string DSL or object form:

```ts
// [!code word:animate]
// Object form — animate property
const relations = [
  { from: 'a', to: 'b', animate: 'flow' },
  { from: 'b', to: 'c', animate: 'pulse', color: '#4CAF50' },
  { from: 'c', to: 'd', animate: 'shimmer' },
];
```

<Callout type="info">
  Edge animations are powered by CSS and injected via `injectEdgeStyles()` from
  the core engine. Framework bindings handle this automatically.
</Callout>

***

Path Types [#path-types]

DiaX supports 3 edge path algorithms:

Bezier (default) [#bezier-default]

Smooth curved paths — the default and most visually appealing option:

```ts
// Default — no need to specify
<FlowDiagram nodes={nodes} relations={relations} />

// Explicit
// [!code word:pathType]
<FlowDiagram nodes={nodes} relations={relations} pathType="bezier" />
```

Straight [#straight]

Direct straight lines between nodes — clean and minimal:

```ts
// [!code word:pathType]
<FlowDiagram nodes={nodes} relations={relations} pathType="straight" />
```

Orthogonal [#orthogonal]

Right-angle paths that follow a grid — ideal for technical/architectural diagrams:

```ts
// [!code word:pathType]
<FlowDiagram nodes={nodes} relations={relations} pathType="orthogonal" />
```

A rich relation can override the Diagram default. This is useful when one authored view combines a
straight primary pipeline with a curved feedback relation:

```tsx
<FlowDiagram
  nodes={nodes}
  pathType="straight"
  relations={[
    { from: 'build', to: 'deploy' },
    { from: 'deploy', to: 'review', pathType: 'bezier' },
  ]}
/>
```

<DiagramPreview
  title="Path type: orthogonal"
  code="`<FlowDiagram
nodes={[
  { id: 'a', content: 'API' },
  { id: 'b', content: 'Auth' },
  { id: 'c', content: 'DB' },
]}
relations={['a->b', 'b->c']}
pathType=&#x22;orthogonal&#x22;
centered density=&#x22;spacious&#x22;
/>`"
>
  <FlowDiagram
    nodes="[
    { id: 'a', content: 'API' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'Auth' },
    { id: 'c', content: 'DB' },
  ]"
    relations="['a->b', 'b->c']"
    pathType="orthogonal"
    density="spacious"
  />
</DiagramPreview>

***

Custom Edge Labels [#custom-edge-labels]

Edge labels are rendered automatically when you provide a `label` in the relation:

```ts
const relations = [
  'gw->|gRPC|auth', // string DSL with label
  { from: 'auth', to: 'db', label: 'SQL' }, // object form with label
];
```

For framework-specific custom label rendering (custom JSX/template for labels), see:

* [React Edge Types](/docs/react/edges)
* [Vue Edge Types](/docs/vue/edges)
* [Svelte Edge Types](/docs/svelte/edges)
* [Solid Edge Types](/docs/solid/edges)

***

Edge Styling [#edge-styling]

Customize edge appearance with these properties:

| Property      | Type     | Default       | Description                      |
| ------------- | -------- | ------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `strokeColor` | `string` | Theme default | Color of the edge line           |
| `strokeWidth` | `number` | `1.5`         | Width of the edge line           |
| `arrowSize`   | `number` | `6`           | Size of the arrowhead            |
| `curvature`   | `number` | `0.25`        | Bezier curve strength (0.01–2.0) |

These can be set as props on the diagram component (applies to all edges) or per-edge via the object form.

Curvature [#curvature]

The `curvature` property controls how curved bezier edge paths are:

```tsx
relations={[
  { from: 'a', to: 'b', curvature: 0.1 },  // Nearly straight
  { from: 'a', to: 'c', curvature: 0.5 },  // Moderate curve
  { from: 'a', to: 'd', curvature: 1.5 },  // Very curved
]}
```

Values range from `0.01` (nearly straight) to `2.0` (extreme curve). Default is `0.25`.

***

Marker Shapes [#marker-shapes]

DiaX supports **14 marker shapes** for edge endpoints. Set markers per-edge using `sourceMarker` and `targetMarker`:

```tsx
relations={[
  { from: 'a', to: 'b', targetMarker: 'triangle' },                     // Default filled marker
  { from: 'b', to: 'c', sourceMarker: 'circle', targetMarker: 'diamond' },
  { from: 'c', to: 'd', sourceMarker: 'crowfoot-many', targetMarker: 'crowfoot-one' }, // ER-style
]}
```

Standard Markers [#standard-markers]

| Shape             | Description                              |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `"arrow"`         | Open chevron formed by two stroked lines |
| `"triangle"`      | Filled triangle — default target marker  |
| `"triangle-open"` | Open/unfilled triangle                   |
| `"diamond"`       | Filled diamond                           |
| `"diamond-open"`  | Open diamond                             |
| `"circle"`        | Filled circle                            |
| `"circle-open"`   | Open circle                              |
| `"cross"`         | Cross/plus mark                          |
| `"bar"`           | Vertical bar                             |
| `"none"`          | No marker                                |

Crow's Foot Markers (ER Diagrams) [#crows-foot-markers-er-diagrams]

| Shape                     | Meaning      | Usage                    |
| ------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------ |
| `"crowfoot-one"`          | Exactly one  | 1:1 relationships        |
| `"crowfoot-many"`         | Many         | 1:N relationships        |
| `"crowfoot-one-or-zero"`  | Zero or one  | Optional relationships   |
| `"crowfoot-many-or-zero"` | Zero or many | Optional N relationships |

Use crow's foot markers for ER (entity-relationship) diagrams to visually represent cardinality.

***

Next Steps [#next-steps]

* [DSL Syntax](/docs/guide/dsl) — Complete relation DSL reference
* [Themes](/docs/guide/themes) — Built-in themes and CSS variables

Interactive Edges [#interactive-edges]

> **Framework Specifics**: See how custom edge rendering works in [React](/docs/react/edges), [Vue](/docs/vue/edges), [Solid](/docs/solid/edges), and [Svelte](/docs/svelte/edges).

Diagram edges are often too thin (e.g., 1px to 2px wide) to reliably hover or interact with using a mouse.

Invisible Hitboxes [#invisible-hitboxes]

When a rich relation provides edge event handlers, DiaX adds a 24px transparent **hitbox** beside the
visible path. Clickable edges are keyboard focusable and respond to Enter and Space. Give every
clickable edge a localized `ariaLabel`; otherwise DiaX falls back to `Connection from {from} to {to}`.

```tsx
const relations = [{
  from: 'build',
  to: 'deploy',
  ariaLabel: 'Open deployment details',
  events: { onClick: () => openDeployment() },
}];
```

Highlight on Hover [#highlight-on-hover]

`highlightOnHover` is node-driven: hovering a node dims unrelated nodes and edges while illuminating
its exact upstream and downstream relation occurrences. A shortcut between two highlighted nodes
does not light up unless traversal actually reaches it from or toward the hovered node. Edge events
are independent and opt-in.

Just pass the prop:

```tsx
// [!code word:highlightOnHover]
<FlowDiagram nodes={nodes} relations={relations} highlightOnHover={true} />
```

***

<Cards>

# Export DOM Visuals (/docs/guide/exporting)





DiaX nodes are real DOM and its relation layer is SVG. An export is complete only when it captures
both. Serializing the first `<svg>` produces arrows without the JSX, Tailwind, table, code or UI
content that made the visual useful.

Choose the destination first [#choose-the-destination-first]

| Destination                            | Recommended output         | Why                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Docs, apps and blogs                   | live DOM                   | Keeps accessibility, links, selection, responsive CSS and interaction    |
| Chat, slides and issue trackers        | PNG                        | Most portable snapshot of the complete composed visual                   |
| A web-aware design or archive workflow | SVG with `<foreignObject>` | Keeps DOM text and vector edges, but requires a compatible viewer        |
| Review packet or handout               | browser print / PDF        | Uses page size, margins, font loading and pagination owned by the report |

There is intentionally no Core `export` mode. Page size, brand fonts, remote assets and download
policy belong to the host workflow, not graph semantics.

Export from the Playground [#export-from-the-playground]

The Playground's Export action is an opt-in product feature:

1. Wait until the preview reports **Live**.
2. Open **Export**.
3. Prefer **PNG** when the artifact will leave the browser.
4. Choose **SVG** only when the destination supports HTML inside SVG `<foreignObject>`.

The MDX preview distinguishes the source revision from the accepted artifact. While a new revision
is compiling, the previous successful preview remains visible as **Updating**. If compilation fails,
it becomes **Last good** and the current file diagnostics stay visible beside it. Export is available
only from **Live**, so an older valid preview cannot be downloaded under the identity of the current
source revision. Compilation alone does not produce **Live**: the current Sandpack revision must
commit and paint in the iframe before its private runtime receipt is accepted.

The sandbox waits for fonts and layout, clones the complete preview root, inlines computed
presentation styles, `<img>` sources and every export-visible CSS `url(...)`, and retains nested
SVG edge layers. Fragment references such as `url(#marker)` remain local to the artifact. A remote,
blob or computed-style resource that cannot be embedded fails the export with its context and an
actionable CORS/vendor-local message; DiaX never silently leaves a mutable URL in a successful SVG.
PNG output is bounded to 32 megapixels; if that limit is exceeded, lower the export scale instead
of risking a tab crash. Requests are correlated with the exact iframe and report an actionable
error when the preview is unavailable, rasterization fails or browser clipboard policy denies
access.

After a successful export, the dialog creates a separate
`*.diax-receipt.json` file. It binds the frozen source and presentation settings to the exact PNG
or SVG bytes with SHA-256, records the painted MDX revision when one exists, and identifies the
canonical static capture policy. Its `asset-closure` check records discovered, embedded and
unresolved resource counts. A failed later attempt leaves the previous successful receipt visible;
failure cannot relabel old bytes as a new artifact. The receipt timestamp is UTC and the review
status remains `pending` until a person inspects the exported file.

Canonical capture suppresses focus, hover targeting, carets, transitions and animations before the
browser snapshots computed presentation. This keeps a button that happened to be focused or a card
that was mid-transition from changing the archival artifact. Authored content, form values and
theme choices remain part of the export.

The receipt proves byte identity and request correlation. It does not prove that the diagram is
correct, attractive or accessible in its destination, and it is currently a Playground product
artifact rather than a Core or framework package interface.

<Callout type="warning">
  SVG `<foreignObject>` is a web interchange format, not a universal office-document format.
  Applications that strip embedded HTML will lose node content. Use PNG or PDF for those targets.
</Callout>

Capture in an application [#capture-in-an-application]

`@diax/react`, Vue, Solid and Svelte do not add a framework export hook. Own one wrapper around the
complete visual and integrate a DOM-capture tool at that seam:

```tsx
const visual = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-report-visual]');
if (!visual) throw new Error('Missing report visual');

await document.fonts.ready;
await Promise.all(
  [...visual.querySelectorAll('img')].map(image =>
    image.complete ? Promise.resolve() : image.decode(),
  ),
);

const { snapdom } = await import('@zumer/snapdom');
const snapshot = await snapdom(visual, {
  backgroundColor: '#fff',
  scale: 2,
});
await snapshot.download({ type: 'png', filename: 'architecture.png' });
```

Keep the capture dependency behind the interaction that needs it. A static Diagram or Connect page
should not load image-export code during initial rendering.

Print and PDF contract [#print-and-pdf-contract]

Use print CSS to remove interaction affordances and preserve document semantics:

```css
@media print {
  [data-report-visual] {
    break-inside: avoid;
    color-scheme: light;
    background: #fff;
    color: #111;
    box-shadow: none;
  }

  [data-report-visual] :is([data-diax-edge-action], .screen-only) {
    display: none;
  }
}
```

Test the actual destination ratio. A 16:9 slide, article column and A4 page have different line
lengths. Pin or embed the intended fonts, give remote images usable CORS headers, keep text
meaningful without color, and verify that tables scroll on screen but fit or deliberately paginate
on paper.

Evidence boundary [#evidence-boundary]

DiaX's browser contract exports one fixture containing an authored DOM block and an SVG edge layer
to both SVG and PNG in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. The Presentation preflight also generates a
four-page A4 PDF and checks one bounded recipe per page; its rendered macOS Chromium artifact is
reviewed for clipping, overlap and legibility.

The same browser contract verifies that MDX export responses match the currently painted revision,
that source and artifact hashes are present, and that the downloadable receipt still reports human
review as pending. Playwright WebKit is rendering-engine evidence, not macOS Safari evidence.

That evidence does not replace hardware Safari, Windows High Contrast, installed corporate fonts,
projector output or a physical printer. Those environments remain destination-specific acceptance,
not claims that can be manufactured by another library option.
