# JSX Authoring (/docs/react/jsx-composition)





Choose the authoring shape from the source [#choose-the-authoring-shape-from-the-source]

JSX markers and `nodes` / `relations` are two authoring adapters for the same Diagram Definition.
They share validation, layout, measurement and edge rendering; neither is a separate runtime mode.

| Source                                                                 | Recommended interface    | Why                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| Hand-authored architecture, report or teaching diagram                 | `@diax/react/jsx`        | Content and topology stay locally readable |
| API response, state, generated collection or frequently changing graph | `@diax/react` data props | The data is already the definition         |
| Existing JSX/Tailwind layout whose placement must not change           | `@diax/react/connect`    | Your DOM/CSS remains the layout owner      |

<Callout type="warn">
  Do not map an existing node array back into `<DiaxNode>` and an edge array back into
  `<DiaxEdge>`. That only repeats the same structure in a noisier form. Pass the arrays directly.
</Callout>

```tsx
// Dynamic data: keep it as data.
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react';

<FlowDiagram nodes={services} relations={links} />;
```

Static JSX definitions [#static-jsx-definitions]

Use sibling declarations when the diagram itself is authored as a visual story. Node children stay
ordinary React DOM, while edges remain first-class relations instead of being hidden inside a node.

```tsx contract
'use client';

import { DiaxEdge, DiaxNode, FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react/jsx';

function CheckoutArchitecture() {
  return (
    <FlowDiagram direction="horizontal" density="spacious">
      <DiaxNode id="browser">
        <article className="rounded-2xl border p-4">
          <small>Client</small>
          <strong>Checkout</strong>
        </article>
      </DiaxNode>

      <DiaxNode id="payments">
        <article><small>Service</small><strong>Payments</strong></article>
      </DiaxNode>

      <DiaxNode id="ledger">
        <article><small>Database</small><strong>PostgreSQL</strong></article>
      </DiaxNode>

      <DiaxEdge
        from="browser"
        to="payments"
        label={<span>HTTPS</span>}
        targetMarker="triangle"
      />
      <DiaxEdge
        from="payments"
        to="ledger"
        label="commit"
        pathType="orthogonal"
        style="dashed"
      />
    </FlowDiagram>
  );
}
```

<DiagramPreview
  title="Static JSX definition"
  code="`'use client';

import { DiaxEdge, DiaxNode, FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react/jsx';

<FlowDiagram density=&#x22;spacious&#x22;>
<DiaxNode id=&#x22;gateway&#x22;>
  <div className=&#x22;rounded-xl border border-indigo-400/20 bg-indigo-500/10 px-4 py-3&#x22;>
    <span className=&#x22;text-xs text-indigo-300&#x22;>EDGE</span>
    <strong className=&#x22;block&#x22;>API Gateway</strong>
  </div>
</DiaxNode>
<DiaxNode id=&#x22;auth&#x22;><strong>Auth Service</strong></DiaxNode>
<DiaxNode id=&#x22;db&#x22;><code>PostgreSQL</code></DiaxNode>
<DiaxEdge from=&#x22;gateway&#x22; to=&#x22;auth&#x22; label=&#x22;gRPC&#x22; />
<DiaxEdge from=&#x22;auth&#x22; to=&#x22;db&#x22; pathType=&#x22;orthogonal&#x22; />
</FlowDiagram>`"
>
  <JSXAuthoringPreview />
</DiagramPreview>

`DiaxEdge` exposes the complete shared Relation vocabulary: labels, anchors, marker shapes,
animation, events, hit targets, path overrides and accessibility names. The old `dashed` boolean is
retained temporarily; new code uses `style="dashed"`.

Composition rules [#composition-rules]

* `DiaxNode` and `DiaxEdge` are siblings. A relation does not belong to either endpoint.
* A node's children are opaque presentation content; DiaX never scans inside them for topology.
* Fragments, conditions and small inline lists are supported, but arrays that already represent the
  whole graph should use data props directly.
* Unknown top-level JSX produces `UNSUPPORTED_DEFINITION_CHILD`; it is never silently discarded.
* A component that returns markers cannot be expanded safely because it may contain Hooks,
  Context, Suspense or side effects. Keep declarations visible at the Diagram call site.
* The data entry and JSX entry cannot be mixed. Choose one source for each Diagram.

Next.js and React Server Components [#nextjs-and-react-server-components]

Construct the complete marker tree inside one file marked `'use client'`. Do not create
`DiaxNode` / `DiaxEdge` elements in a Server Component and pass them through an RSC boundary; React
serializes component references across that boundary and the synchronous Definition Adapter cannot
inspect them. When topology originates on the server, pass a JSON-safe data Definition to
`@diax/react` instead.

Dynamic JSX content without marker loops [#dynamic-jsx-content-without-marker-loops]

Dynamic topology does not mean plain text nodes. Put any React content directly in the data:

```tsx
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react';

const nodes = services.map(service => ({
  id: service.id,
  content: <ServiceCard service={service} />,
}));

<FlowDiagram nodes={nodes} relations={links} />;
```

Use `nodeTypes` for allowlisted server or AI data, or `renderNode` when one renderer owns the full
presentation policy. Runtime AI output should remain JSON-safe and validated; only trusted,
code-reviewed generation should emit executable TSX.

Loading behavior [#loading-behavior]

`@diax/react/jsx` is a real build entry. It does not load Connect, Mermaid, Notebook or optional UI
presets. Conversely, `@diax/react` does not contain the JSX extractor. The two entries converge only
after authoring input has become the same `nodes + relations` definition.


# Props Reference (/docs/react/props)



Props Reference [#props-reference]

`<FlowDiagram>` / `<Mindmap>` Props [#flowdiagram--mindmap-props]

Import these data-driven components from `@diax/react`. Dynamic topology stays in `nodes` and
`relations`; this entry does not accept marker children.

<TypeTable
  type="{
  nodes: { description: 'Node definitions; content may be arbitrary JSX', type: 'readonly DiaxNode[]', default: '—' },
  relations: { description: 'Centralized relation definitions', type: 'readonly DiaxRelation[]', default: '—' },
  groups: { description: 'Semantic group boundaries; parentId enables nesting', type: 'readonly DiaxGroup[]', default: '—' },
  direction: { description: 'Layout direction', type: &#x22;'horizontal' | 'vertical' | 'horizontal-reverse' | 'vertical-reverse'&#x22;, default: &#x22;'horizontal'&#x22; },
  density: { description: 'Spacing', type: &#x22;'compact' | 'comfortable' | 'spacious'&#x22;, default: &#x22;'comfortable'&#x22; },
  centered: { description: 'Center nodes in cells', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
  align: { description: 'Align nodes within grid cells', type: &#x22;'start' | 'center' | 'end'&#x22;, default: &#x22;'start'&#x22; },
  highlightOnHover: { description: 'Highlight path on hover', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
  stagger: { description: 'Stagger entrance animation', type: 'boolean | number', default: 'false' },
  measureMode: { description: 'DOM measurement strategy', type: &#x22;'resize' | 'auto' | 'continuous'&#x22;, default: &#x22;'resize'&#x22; },
  theme: { description: 'Theme preset or object', type: &#x22;'linear' | 'light' | 'notion' | 'github' | DiaxTheme&#x22;, default: '—' },
  namespace: { description: 'Resolved DOM ID namespace', type: 'string', default: '—' },
  nodeTypes: { description: 'Node type registry', type: 'Record<string, (node, state) => ReactNode>', default: '—' },
  renderNode: { description: 'Custom node renderer', type: '(node, state) => ReactNode', default: '—' },
  renderEdgeLabel: { description: 'Custom edge label renderer', type: '(label) => ReactNode', default: '—' },
  pathType: { description: 'Edge path type', type: &#x22;'bezier' | 'straight' | 'orthogonal'&#x22;, default: &#x22;'bezier'&#x22; },
  strokeColor: { description: 'Edge color; inherits currentColor when unthemed', type: 'string', default: &#x22;'var(--diax-edge-color, currentColor)'&#x22; },
  strokeWidth: { description: 'Edge width', type: 'number', default: '1' },
  arrowSize: { description: 'Arrow marker size', type: 'number', default: '6' },
}"
/>

Definitions are treated as immutable authoring values. Arrays created with `as const`, memoized
selectors or readonly application state can be passed directly; DiaX does not require callers to
clone them into mutable arrays.

`<DiaxNode>` Props [#diaxnode-props]

Import the JSX-authored `FlowDiagram`, `Mindmap`, `DiaxNode` and `DiaxEdge` from
`@diax/react/jsx`. Use this form for static visual stories; pass existing arrays to the root data
entry instead of mapping them into marker components.

<TypeTable
  type="{
  id: { description: 'Unique node ID (required)', type: 'string', default: '—' },
  type: { description: 'Node type for nodeTypes registry', type: 'string', default: '—' },
  position: { description: 'Override auto-layout position', type: '{ col?: number; row?: number }', default: '—' },
  children: { description: 'Node content', type: 'ReactNode', default: '—' },
}"
/>

`<DiaxEdge>` Props [#diaxedge-props]

`DiaxEdgeProps` is derived from the shared Core `DiaxEdge<ReactNode>` type. JSX and data definitions
therefore expose the same rich Relation controls.

<TypeTable
  type="{
  from: { description: 'Source node ID (required)', type: 'string', default: '—' },
  to: { description: 'Target node ID (required)', type: 'string', default: '—' },
  label: { description: 'Edge label', type: 'ReactNode', default: '—' },
  style: { description: 'Line style', type: &#x22;'solid' | 'dashed'&#x22;, default: &#x22;'solid'&#x22; },
  color: { description: 'Edge color', type: 'string', default: '—' },
  bidirectional: { description: 'Bidirectional arrow', type: 'boolean', default: '—' },
  animate: { description: 'Animation preset', type: 'AnimationPreset', default: '—' },
  sourceAnchor: { description: 'Override source attachment side', type: 'Anchor', default: 'auto' },
  targetAnchor: { description: 'Override target attachment side', type: 'Anchor', default: 'auto' },
  sourceMarker: { description: 'Source marker shape or config', type: 'MarkerShape | MarkerConfig', default: &#x22;'none'&#x22; },
  targetMarker: { description: 'Target marker shape or config', type: 'MarkerShape | MarkerConfig', default: &#x22;'triangle'&#x22; },
  pathType: { description: 'Per-edge path override', type: &#x22;'bezier' | 'straight' | 'orthogonal'&#x22;, default: 'diagram default' },
  strokeWidth: { description: 'Per-edge stroke width', type: 'number', default: 'diagram default' },
  strokeDasharray: { description: 'Custom SVG dash pattern', type: 'string', default: '—' },
  className: { description: 'Class name on the visible SVG path', type: 'string', default: '—' },
  gap: { description: 'Gap between path and node borders', type: 'number', default: '0' },
  curvature: { description: 'Bezier curvature factor', type: 'number', default: '0.4' },
  order: { description: 'SVG rendering order', type: 'number', default: 'source order' },
  hitSlop: { description: 'Interactive hit-target width', type: 'number', default: '24' },
  events: { description: 'Click, hover and context-menu handlers', type: 'DiaxEdgeEvents', default: '—' },
  ariaLabel: { description: 'Accessible name for an interactive edge', type: 'string', default: 'generated fallback' },
  dashed: { description: 'Deprecated compatibility alias; use style=&#x22;dashed&#x22;', type: 'boolean', default: '—' },
}"
/>


# Next.js & SSR (/docs/react/ssr)



Put the renderer behind a client boundary [#put-the-renderer-behind-a-client-boundary]

DiaX can validate, parse, and plan pure data on the server, but the React renderer measures real DOM
after hydration to place its SVG edge layer. In Next.js App Router, put the file that imports
`@diax/react` behind a `'use client'` boundary:

```tsx title="app/dashboard/my-diagram.tsx" contract
'use client';

import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react';

export function MyDiagram() {
  return (
    <FlowDiagram
      nodes={[
        { id: 'gateway', content: 'Gateway' },
        { id: 'service', content: 'Service' },
        { id: 'database', content: 'Database' },
      ]}
      relations={['gateway->service', 'service->database']}
    />
  );
}
```

The Server Component can render that client boundary normally:

```tsx title="app/dashboard/page.tsx"
import { MyDiagram } from './my-diagram';

export default function DashboardPage() {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Architecture</h1>
      <MyDiagram />
    </main>
  );
}
```

The page block is a two-file Next.js project fragment; the client module above is the standalone
TypeScript contract. A Client Component can still contribute prerendered HTML. The important
boundary is that DOM measurement and interaction start in the browser after hydration—not that the
entire route must return an empty server response.

Cross the RSC boundary with data [#cross-the-rsc-boundary-with-data]

Prefer a small serializable definition across Server and Client Components:

```ts title="diagram-definition.ts" contract
export interface DiagramDefinition {
  nodes: Array<{ id: string; content: string }>;
  relations: Array<{
    from: string;
    to: string;
    label?: string;
    style?: 'solid' | 'dashed';
  }>;
}
```

Server code may fetch or validate that definition, or parse supported Mermaid source through
`@diax/mermaid`. Pass only JSON-safe node fields and relations to the client renderer. Do not cross
the boundary with React nodes, event handlers, parser diagnostics, layout worker state, or generated
unreviewed JSX.

The release gate includes a real Next production fixture that proves Mermaid parsing remains in the
Server Component graph while `@diax/react` remains in the client graph:

```bash
pnpm smoke:rsc
```

Lazy load an optional diagram [#lazy-load-an-optional-diagram]

Use `next/dynamic` when the feature itself is optional or below the fold. In the App Router,
`ssr: false` must be declared from a Client Component:

```tsx title="app/dashboard/lazy-diagram.tsx" contract
'use client';

import dynamic from 'next/dynamic';

const LazyFlowDiagram = dynamic(
  () => import('@diax/react').then((module) => module.FlowDiagram),
  {
    ssr: false,
    loading: () => <p role="status">Loading diagram…</p>,
  },
);

export function LazyDiagram() {
  return (
    <LazyFlowDiagram
      nodes={[
        { id: 'author', content: 'Author' },
        { id: 'reader', content: 'Reader' },
      ]}
      relations={['author->reader']}
    />
  );
}
```

This is a loading decision, not a correctness requirement. The normal client-boundary example is
preferred when the diagram is primary page content. Keep the dynamic declaration at module scope so
React and Next can retain its identity and cached import.

Avoid hydration drift [#avoid-hydration-drift]

* Keep the initial serializable definition deterministic between server render and hydration.
* Do not branch node content on `window`, viewport width, random IDs, or local time during render.
* Let responsive CSS change presentation; do not produce a different topology for the first client
  render.
* Reserve meaningful loading space for lazily loaded diagrams to reduce layout shift.
* When node content changes after hydration, let the adapter's measurement lifecycle recompute edge
  geometry rather than caching DOM rectangles in application state.

Server-safe and browser-only leaves [#server-safe-and-browser-only-leaves]

| Job                                                     | Entry                 | Runtime                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Validate and compute a basic definition                 | `diax`                | Server-safe for pure APIs                    |
| Plan measured automatic routes from supplied rectangles | `diax/layout-plan`    | Server-safe                                  |
| Parse supported Mermaid source                          | `@diax/mermaid`       | Server-safe, ESM-only                        |
| Render and measure a React Diagram                      | `@diax/react`         | Client boundary; measurement after hydration |
| Connect already-positioned DOM                          | `@diax/react/connect` | Browser-only client entry                    |

See [Package Entry Points](/docs/reference/package-entry-points) for the complete loading and SSR
contract.


# Authoring Model (/docs/reference/authoring-model)



**Audience:** most users, AI pipelines, and adapter authors.\
&#x2A;*Runtime:** server-safe; no DOM dependency.\
&#x2A;*Import:** `diax`.

Nodes and relations [#nodes-and-relations]

```ts
interface DiaxNode<Content = unknown> {
  id: string;
  content: Content;
  type?: string;
  position?: { col?: number; row?: number };
}

type DiaxRelation<Label = unknown> = string | DiaxEdge<Label>;
```

Independent payload types [#independent-payload-types]

Node content, object edge labels, and group labels are independent payload channels. Most users do
not write generic arguments: TypeScript infers them from the three input arrays. Custom headless
renderers can make the separation explicit in the order
`<NodeContent, EdgeLabel, GroupLabel>`:

```ts contract
import { computeLayout } from 'diax';

interface NodePayload { title: string }
interface EdgePayload { protocol: string }
interface GroupPayload { badge: string }

const layout = computeLayout<NodePayload, EdgePayload, GroupPayload>({
  nodes: [
    { id: 'browser', content: { title: 'Browser' } },
    { id: 'api', content: { title: 'API' } },
  ],
  relations: [{ from: 'browser', to: 'api', label: { protocol: 'HTTPS' } }],
  groups: [{ id: 'backend', label: { badge: 'Internal' }, nodeIds: ['api'] }],
});

layout.nodeBindings[0].data.content.title;
layout.parsedEdges[0].label;
layout.groupBindings[0].data.label?.badge;
```

String relation shorthand can always create a string label, so parsed edge labels are typed as
`EdgePayload | string | undefined`. AI and JSON workflows normally use serializable values and can
continue to rely on inference.

`position` is an optional rank/order hint, not a pixel coordinate or a way to author internal
routing bends. `col` and `row` must be integers from 0 through 255. This generous safety bound
prevents accidental million-rank dummy chains while leaving ordinary reports and architecture
diagrams unconstrained in practice.

Object relations are the canonical format for generated or dynamic content:

```ts contract
import type { DiaxNode, DiaxRelation } from 'diax';

const nodes: DiaxNode<string>[] = [
  { id: 'claim', content: 'Conversion improved' },
  { id: 'evidence', content: 'A/B test: +12%' },
];

const relations: DiaxRelation<string>[] = [
  {
    from: 'claim',
    to: 'evidence',
    label: 'supported by',
    pathType: 'orthogonal',
    targetMarker: 'arrow',
  },
];
```

String relations are concise authoring sugar for trusted, static definitions:

```ts
'a->b'
'a-->|label|b'
'a<->b'
```

Use `parseRelation()` or `parseRelations()` to normalize either form into
`ParsedRelation`. Prefer objects in agent output because fields and repair paths remain explicit.

Semantic groups [#semantic-groups]

Use one optional group list when a Diagram needs nested system or subgraph boundaries:

```ts contract
import type { DiaxGroup } from 'diax';

const groups: DiaxGroup<string>[] = [
  { id: 'system', label: 'System', nodeIds: ['browser'] },
  {
    id: 'backend',
    label: 'Backend services',
    nodeIds: ['api', 'db'],
    parentId: 'system',
  },
];
```

`nodeIds` contains direct members. `parentId` nests one group inside another; parent bounds include
all descendant nodes automatically. Do not calculate group rectangles or add synthetic nodes.
Cross-group relations remain ordinary relations.

All official Diagram adapters render these boundaries from the same Core binding; Mermaid flowchart
subgraphs lower to the same model. Built-in flow packing and ELK preserve compound containment.
Group-aware ports and collapse behavior remain experimental follow-up work.

Rich edge fields [#rich-edge-fields]

`DiaxEdge` includes:

* `from`, `to`, `label`, `style`, `color`, and `bidirectional`
* `sourceAnchor`, `targetAnchor`, `pathType`, `curvature`, and `gap`
* `sourceMarker`, `targetMarker`, `strokeWidth`, and `strokeDasharray`
* `events`, `ariaLabel`, `hitSlop`, `className`, and `animate`

The same relation vocabulary is shared by Core, Diagram, Connect, and JSX authoring. Do not create
a second application-specific edge shape unless you are intentionally translating a domain model.

Runtime validation [#runtime-validation]

`validateDiagram(nodes, relations)` returns structured diagnostics and never requires parsing
human-readable error text:

```ts contract
import { validateDiagram } from 'diax';

const diagnostics = validateDiagram(
  [{ id: 'source', content: 'Source' }],
  [{ from: 'source', to: 'missing' }],
);

for (const diagnostic of diagnostics) {
  console.log(diagnostic.code, diagnostic.path, diagnostic.hint);
}
```

Every `DiaxDiagnostic` has a stable `code`, `severity`, and `message`, plus optional `path`,
`location`, and repair `hint`.

| Code                           | Meaning                                                             |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MIXED_MODE`                   | Data props and JSX definition children were mixed                   |
| `UNSUPPORTED_DEFINITION_CHILD` | JSX definition input contained an unsupported child                 |
| `INVALID_NODE_ID`              | A node ID is empty or invalid                                       |
| `INVALID_NODE_POSITION`        | A grid hint is fractional, negative, or exceeds the safe rank bound |
| `DUPLICATE_NODE_ID`            | More than one node uses the same ID                                 |
| `DUPLICATE_GROUP_ID`           | More than one group uses the same ID                                |
| `GROUP_ID_COLLISION`           | A group ID collides with a node ID                                  |
| `UNKNOWN_GROUP_NODE`           | A group references a missing node                                   |
| `UNKNOWN_PARENT_GROUP`         | A group references a missing parent                                 |
| `DUPLICATE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP`   | A node is assigned to two direct groups                             |
| `CYCLIC_GROUP`                 | Parent references form a cycle                                      |
| `MALFORMED_RELATION`           | A relation cannot be parsed                                         |
| `ORPHAN_RELATION`              | An endpoint does not exist in the surface                           |
| `SELF_LOOP`                    | A node points to itself; currently a warning                        |
| `UNSUPPORTED_CROSS_SURFACE`    | A relation crosses an unsupported measurement boundary              |

`computeLayout()` throws `DiaxValidationError` for error-severity diagnostics and keeps the
original list on `error.diagnostics`.

Type-safe builder [#type-safe-builder]

`defineDiagram(nodes)` constrains relation endpoints to literal node IDs:

```ts contract
import { defineDiagram } from 'diax';

const checkout = defineDiagram([
  { id: 'cart' as const, content: 'Cart' },
  { id: 'payment' as const, content: 'Payment' },
] as const)
  .relation('cart', 'payment', { label: 'checkout' })
  .build();
```

The builder is optional compile-time sugar. Arrays remain the serialization boundary and the
recommended AI output.

AST conversion [#ast-conversion]

`createAST(nodes, relations, options?)` parses relations into a normalized
`DiaxAST<NodeContent, EdgeLabel, GroupLabel>`.
`createASTFromEdges(nodes, edges, options?)` accepts edges that are already parsed. Adapter options
may retain `direction`, `layout`, `centered`, and `groups` without introducing another model.

AST is an interchange value for adapters such as Mermaid. It is not a second required authoring
mode, and framework users do not need to construct it before rendering.

Related [#related]

* [Core Interface](/docs/reference/core-interface)
* [AI validation and repair](/docs/guide/ai-integration)
* [React JSX authoring](/docs/react/jsx-composition)


# Core Interface (/docs/reference/core-interface)



**Audience:** custom renderer authors, validation services, and framework adapter authors.\
&#x2A;*Runtime:** server-safe and framework-agnostic.\
&#x2A;*Import:** `diax`.

`computeLayout(input)` [#computelayoutinput]

This is the primary Core interface. It validates input, normalizes relations, partitions qualified
edges, runs the selected layout, and produces CSS Grid bindings.

```ts contract
import { computeLayout } from 'diax';

const layout = computeLayout({
  nodes: [
    { id: 'web', content: 'Web' },
    { id: 'api', content: 'API' },
    { id: 'db', content: 'Database' },
  ],
  relations: ['web->api', 'api->db'],
  layout: 'flow',
  direction: 'horizontal',
  centered: true,
});
```

Input [#input]

| Field           | Type                      | Default        | Notes                                            |                    |
| --------------- | ------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ |
| `nodes`         | `readonly DiaxNode[]`     | required       | Stable unique IDs                                |                    |
| `relations`     | `readonly DiaxRelation[]` | required       | String or object form                            |                    |
| `groups`        | `readonly DiaxGroup[]`    | `[]`           | Semantic containment from direct node membership |                    |
| `layout`        | \`'flow' \\               | 'mindmap'\`    | `'flow'`                                         | Built-in algorithm |
| `direction`     | `Direction`               | `'horizontal'` | Includes reverse directions                      |                    |
| `namespace`     | `string`                  | —              | Qualifies DOM IDs                                |                    |
| `centered`      | `boolean`                 | `false`        | Centers nodes in grid tracks                     |                    |
| `autoRelations` | `boolean`                 | `false`        | Creates sequential edges only when none exist    |                    |

Output [#output]

| Field            | Purpose                                                     |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `nodeBindings`   | Node data, resolved IDs, ARIA flow targets, and grid styles |
| `groupBindings`  | Outermost-first group data and derived CSS Grid boundaries  |
| `parsedEdges`    | Normalized relations for measurement and edge rendering     |
| `containerStyle` | Framework-neutral CSS Grid properties                       |
| `layoutResult`   | Raw layout nodes, rows, and columns                         |
| `layoutMap`      | Node ID to layout-position lookup                           |
| `cols` / `rows`  | Grid dimensions                                             |

The function does not read the DOM and does not compute hover state. A renderer still owns DOM
creation, measurement, edge overlay lifecycle, and cleanup.

`LayoutInput<NodeContent, EdgeLabel, GroupLabel>` and the matching output keep all three payload
channels independent. TypeScript normally infers them; use explicit arguments only when a custom
renderer or an empty input array prevents useful inference. See [Authoring Model](/docs/reference/authoring-model#independent-payload-types).

Failure contract [#failure-contract]

Invalid definitions throw `DiaxValidationError` before layout:

```ts contract
import { computeLayout, DiaxValidationError } from 'diax';

try {
  computeLayout({
    nodes: [{ id: 'only', content: 'Only node' }],
    relations: [{ from: 'only', to: 'missing' }],
  });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof DiaxValidationError) {
    error.diagnostics.forEach(item => console.error(item.code, item.path));
  } else {
    throw error;
  }
}
```

Do not catch and replace this error with a blank diagram. Show an actionable error state or pass
the diagnostics into an AI repair loop.

`computeHighlight(hoveredId, nodes, parsedEdges)` [#computehighlighthoveredid-nodes-parsededges]

Highlight state is deliberately separate so hover does not rerun layout:

```ts contract
import { computeHighlight, computeLayout } from 'diax';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'a', content: 'A' },
  { id: 'b', content: 'B' },
];
const computed = computeLayout({ nodes, relations: ['a->b'] });
const highlight = computeHighlight('a', nodes, computed.parsedEdges);

highlight.highlightedNodes;
highlight.highlightedEdgeIds;
highlight.nodeStates;
```

Pass `null` as the hovered ID to return the idle state. Official adapters use
`getNodeDisplayOpacity()` and edge render helpers so the visual policy stays consistent.
`highlightedEdgeIds` contains exact stable relation occurrences, not every edge whose endpoints
happen to be highlighted. For `a → focus → b` plus a bypass `a → b`, hovering `focus` selects the
incoming and outgoing relations while the bypass remains dimmed. Parallel relations, cycles and
self-loops remain deterministic; authored `from → to` direction is never reversed by inspection.

When not to call Core directly [#when-not-to-call-core-directly]

Use a framework `FlowDiagram` when you do not need to own rendering lifecycle. Use React
[Connect](/docs/react/connect) when CSS already owns placement. Calling `computeLayout` does not
turn Connect into an automatic-layout surface.

Related [#related]

* [Graph & Layout Primitives](/docs/reference/graph-layout)
* [Edge Rendering Primitives](/docs/reference/edge-rendering)
* [Measurement](/docs/reference/measurement)


# Edge Rendering Primitives (/docs/reference/edge-rendering)



**Audience:** custom renderer and framework adapter authors.\
&#x2A;*Runtime:** geometry is server-safe; DOM event helpers require browser events.\
&#x2A;*Imports:** `diax/layout-plan` for Diagram-aware routing; `diax/edge-geometry` for direct geometry.

Official adapters already compose these functions. Use them directly when you are building a
different SVG overlay, exporting geometry, or implementing another framework binding.

Geometry pipeline [#geometry-pipeline]

| Stage                        | Functions                                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Anchors                      | `anchorPoint`, `computeAnchors`, `applyGap`                                     |
| Path shape                   | `cubicBezierPath`, `straightPath`, `orthogonalPath`, `selfLoopPath`             |
| Diagram batch computation    | `computeEdgePaths`                                                              |
| Engine-neutral planning      | `planLayeredLayout`, `withGroupBoundaryPorts`, `computeEdgePathsFromLayoutPlan` |
| Direct DOM-owned computation | `computeDirectEdgePaths` from `diax/edge-geometry`                              |
| Labels and dash              | `bezierLabelPoint`, `resolveDashArray`                                          |

```ts contract
import { computeAnchors, cubicBezierPath, straightPath } from 'diax';

const anchors = computeAnchors(
  { id: 'a', col: 0, row: 0 },
  { id: 'b', col: 1, row: 0 },
  'horizontal',
);

straightPath(0, 20, 120, 20);
cubicBezierPath(0, 20, anchors.sourceAnchor, 120, 20, anchors.targetAnchor);
```

`computeEdgePaths(edges, rects, layoutMap, direction, pathType?, routingOptions?)` combines measured
node rectangles with layout positions. Internally it creates a `LayoutPlan` with stable edge IDs,
fan-in/out ports, one section per crossed rank, parallel lanes, a feedback gutter, and measured label
tracks. Self-loops use the same port, section, label, and bounds contract instead of a renderer-only
special path. Its `ComputedEdgePath` output includes path data, endpoints, label position, resolved
dash style, order, and hit-slop metadata.

Advanced engines and custom renderers can use the structured seam directly:

```ts contract
import type { LayoutNode } from 'diax';
import {
  computeEdgePathsFromLayoutPlan,
  planLayeredLayout,
  type NodeRect,
} from 'diax/layout-plan';

const rects = new Map<string, NodeRect>();
const layoutMap = new Map<string, LayoutNode>();
const plan = planLayeredLayout({ edges: [], rects, layoutMap });
const paths = computeEdgePathsFromLayoutPlan(plan, []);
```

`LayoutPlan` contains only authored nodes plus final pixels, optional engine-derived group bounds,
node ports, ordered group entry/exit ports, route sections, labels, overall bounds, and diagnostics.
Dummy items remain an engine implementation detail. Custom layout adapters can call
`withGroupBoundaryPorts(plan)` after producing final group and route geometry; built-in and ELK
plans already do this.

`groupLabelRects` is a measured adapter fact, not authored diagram data. Official adapters obtain it
from `createDiagramMeasurementObserver` in `diax/diagram-measurement`. The planner projects a label
that intersects a group border into an exclusion interval, allocates the remaining side capacity,
and inserts a short boundary dogleg when a port moves. Rich JSX/Vue/Svelte labels therefore use their
actual rendered box without adding `labelWidth`, bend, gate, or port-offset authoring options.

Use the direct leaf when your application owns DOM placement and does not want Diagram routing:

```ts contract
import { computeDirectEdgePaths } from 'diax/edge-geometry';

const paths = computeDirectEdgePaths([], new Map(), new Map(), 'horizontal', 'bezier');
```

This is the primitive used by Connect. It includes anchors, stable `createEdgeIds`, self-loops, gap,
parallel-pair offsets, labels, and path interpolation, but it deliberately excludes obstacle routing
and graph layout. The separate package entry also keeps the automatic router out of native ESM and
federation consumers. Connect adds DOM-owned obstacle-aware anchor selection and automatic shared-side
port spreading privately; those policies are not extra direct-geometry modes.

`pathType` describes how a planned route is drawn. Explicit `straight` remains a direct escape hatch
and is not automatically rerouted around nodes. A self-loop still follows its planned outer route
because a direct line from a node to itself has no visible geometry. Semantic compound routes now
retain their actual group-boundary crossings; authored portals, collapse, and nested Connect
surfaces remain out of scope.

Markers [#markers]

| Function                              | Purpose                                                  |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `normalizeMarker(marker)`             | Expand a shape or config into normalized marker data     |
| `resolveEdgeMarkers(edge)`            | Resolve source/target markers and bidirectional defaults |
| `markerId(shape, color, size?)`       | Produce a stable CSS-safe marker ID                      |
| `markerUrl(shape, color, size?)`      | Produce an SVG `url(#id)` reference                      |
| `collectMarkers(edges, color, size?)` | Deduplicate marker definitions needed by a surface       |
| `MARKER_SHAPES`                       | Built-in SVG marker definitions                          |

`MarkerShape` supports arrows, triangles, diamonds, circles, cross, bar, crow's-foot variants, and
`none`. A renderer should emit one `<defs>` marker per `MarkerInstance`, not one per edge.

Render-ready data [#render-ready-data]

`prepareEdgeRenderData(edgePaths, options?)` centralizes marker resolution, highlighting,
accessibility, hit targets, and display colors:

```ts
const { markers, paths } = prepareEdgeRenderData(computedPaths, {
  strokeColor: '#64748b',
  arrowSize: 6,
  highlightedNodes,
  highlightedEdgeIds,
  accentColor: '#5e6ad2',
});
```

Each `RenderReadyPath` includes the final marker URLs, display color, `actionable` state,
`hitSlop`, and `ariaLabel`. Using this output prevents framework adapters from drifting on
keyboard or visual semantics.

Additional helpers:

* `isEdgeHighlighted(edge, highlightedNodes, highlightedEdgeIds?)`
* `getEdgeDisplayColor(edge, defaultColor, highlightedNodes, accentColor?, dimmedColor?)`
* `getNodeDisplayOpacity(nodeId, highlightedNodes)`

Pass both sets from `computeHighlight()` when relation identity matters. Omitting
`highlightedEdgeIds` preserves the legacy endpoint fallback for custom renderers that have not yet
carried stable `edgeId` values through their geometry pipeline.

Interaction contract [#interaction-contract]

`dispatchEdgeEvent(edge, handler, originalEvent)` forwards the shared
`{ from, to, originalEvent }` payload to a relation handler.

`activateEdgeOnKeyDown(event)` gives actionable SVG paths button-like Enter and Space behavior.
Only edges with click behavior should receive `role="button"`, focusability, and keyboard
activation. Hover-only edges must not pretend to be controls.

For reliable pointer interaction, draw a separate transparent hit path using the resolved
`hitSlop`; do not inflate the visible stroke.

Renderer responsibilities [#renderer-responsibilities]

A custom edge renderer must provide:

1. A surface-local SVG overlay and marker definitions.
2. Stable node measurement owned by the same surface.
3. Visible and pointer hit paths.
4. Accessible names and keyboard behavior for actionable edges.
5. Highlight consistency and cleanup on unmount.

If you do not need to own all five, use an official framework adapter.

Related [#related]

* [Measurement](/docs/reference/measurement)
* [Edge behavior guide](/docs/guide/edge-types)
* [Accessibility](/docs/guide/accessibility)


# Graph & Layout Primitives (/docs/reference/graph-layout)



**Audience:** adapter authors and advanced custom renderers.\
&#x2A;*Runtime:** server-safe pure TypeScript.\
&#x2A;*Import:** `diax`.

Most applications should use [`computeLayout`](/docs/reference/core-interface), which combines
these atoms with validation, relation parsing, namespace handling, and binding generation.

Built-in layout [#built-in-layout]

`simpleGridLayout(nodes, edges, groups?)` [#simplegridlayoutnodes-edges-groups]

Computes a grid layout for a directed graph. Authored `position.col` and `position.row` values pin an
axis before automatic placement fills the remaining positions. Long edges are normalized into an
internal dummy item at every crossed rank before crossing-minimization sweeps. Those items reserve
route rows but never appear in `LayoutResult.nodes`. Explicit grid hints are bounded to integer
indices from 0 through 255; callers never create dummy items themselves. Optional semantic groups
reserve nested, exclusive row bands so a rectangular boundary cannot capture unrelated nodes.

```ts contract
import { parseRelations, simpleGridLayout } from 'diax';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'a', content: 'A' },
  { id: 'b', content: 'B' },
  { id: 'c', content: 'C', position: { col: 2 } },
];

const result = simpleGridLayout(nodes, parseRelations(['a->b', 'b->c']));
result.nodes;
result.cols;
result.rows;
```

`mindmapLayout(nodes, edges)` [#mindmaplayoutnodes-edges]

Computes the built-in center-out hierarchy layout. Use `computeLayout({ layout: 'mindmap' })` in
application code so validation and binding behavior remain consistent.

`resolveLayout(mode)` and `LAYOUTS` [#resolvelayoutmode-and-layouts]

`resolveLayout('flow')` returns `simpleGridLayout`; `resolveLayout('mindmap')` returns
`mindmapLayout`. Unknown names throw. `LAYOUTS` exposes the same built-in registry for adapter
introspection.

<Callout type="warn">
  DiaX does not expose a global layout registry. The built-in engine and ELK both emit the same
  value-based `LayoutPlan`; import `@diax/layout-elk` explicitly instead of registering a mutable
  provider.
</Callout>

Graph traversal [#graph-traversal]

These helpers accept normalized `ParsedRelation[]`:

| Function                             | Result                      |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `buildChildMap(nodeIds, edges)`      | Forward adjacency map       |
| `buildParentMap(nodeIds, edges)`     | Reverse adjacency map       |
| `buildUndirectedMap(nodeIds, edges)` | Bidirectional adjacency map |
| `bfs(startId, adjacency)`            | Reachable node ID set       |
| `nodeIds(nodes)`                     | Node ID set                 |

```ts contract
import { bfs, buildChildMap, nodeIds, parseRelations } from 'diax';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'root', content: 'Root' },
  { id: 'child', content: 'Child' },
];
const children = buildChildMap(nodeIds(nodes), parseRelations(['root->child']));
const reachable = bfs('root', children);
```

These are useful for selection, dependency highlighting, and adapter-specific navigation. They do
not perform validation; normalize and validate untrusted input first.

Direction helpers [#direction-helpers]

```ts contract
import { isReversed, isVertical, toAxis } from 'diax';

toAxis('horizontal-reverse'); // 'horizontal'
isVertical('vertical-reverse'); // true
isReversed('horizontal-reverse'); // true
```

`Direction` is `'horizontal' | 'vertical' | 'horizontal-reverse' | 'vertical-reverse'`.
`Axis` is `'horizontal' | 'vertical'`.

Layout types [#layout-types]

```ts
interface LayoutResult {
  nodes: LayoutNode[];
  cols: number;
  rows: number;
}

type LayoutFn = (
  nodes: DiaxNode[],
  edges: ParsedRelation[],
  groups?: readonly DiaxGroup[],
) => LayoutResult;
```

`LayoutResult` is the lightweight CSS Grid placement result. `LayoutPlan` is the measured pixel
contract between a full layout engine and a renderer. See
[Edge Rendering Primitives](/docs/reference/edge-rendering) for its planning and rendering APIs.

Related [#related]

* [Core Interface](/docs/reference/core-interface)
* [ELK integration](/docs/guide/layout-elk)
* [Layout modes](/docs/guide/layout-modes)


# API Reference (/docs/reference)



Start at the right depth [#start-at-the-right-depth]

DiaX exposes low-level graph, geometry, measurement, and rendering atoms so framework adapters and
custom renderers do not need to fork the engine. Most applications should still begin with one
high-level framework interface.

| You are building                         | Start here                                                   | Runtime                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| A data-driven diagram                    | [Framework adapter](/docs/react)                             | DOM measurement in the browser   |
| Connections over existing JSX/CSS        | [React Connect](/docs/react/connect)                         | Browser-only edge surface        |
| An AI or server-side validation pipeline | [Authoring Model](/docs/reference/authoring-model)           | Server-safe                      |
| A custom renderer or framework adapter   | [Core Interface](/docs/reference/core-interface)             | Core is server-safe              |
| Custom paths, markers, or interaction    | [Edge Rendering](/docs/reference/edge-rendering)             | Geometry is pure; events use DOM |
| A custom measurement owner               | [Measurement](/docs/reference/measurement)                   | Browser-only                     |
| A bundle or federation integration       | [Package Entry Points](/docs/reference/package-entry-points) | Boundary-specific                |

<Callout type="info">
  **Progressive disclosure is intentional.** Public does not mean recommended for every
  application. Low-level interfaces are primarily for adapter authors and custom renderers.
</Callout>

Recommended Core interface [#recommended-core-interface]

`computeLayout` is the deepest general-purpose Core module: it validates definitions, resolves
namespaces, parses relations, runs layout, and returns framework-neutral bindings.

```ts contract
import { computeLayout } from 'diax';

const result = computeLayout({
  nodes: [
    { id: 'browser', content: 'Browser' },
    { id: 'api', content: 'API' },
  ],
  relations: [{ from: 'browser', to: 'api', label: 'HTTPS' }],
  layout: 'flow',
  direction: 'horizontal',
});

result.nodeBindings;
result.parsedEdges;
result.containerStyle;
```

Framework applications should normally let `FlowDiagram`, `Mindmap`, or the matching adapter call
this function. Call Core directly for validation pipelines, non-React adapters, or a custom
renderer.

Reference map [#reference-map]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Authoring Model" href="/docs/reference/authoring-model" description="Nodes, relations, parsing, AST, builder, validation, and diagnostics" />

  <Card title="Core Interface" href="/docs/reference/core-interface" description="computeLayout, computeHighlight, inputs, outputs, and failure behavior" />

  <Card title="Graph & Layout" href="/docs/reference/graph-layout" description="Built-in layout algorithms, traversal, registry, and direction helpers" />

  <Card title="Edge Rendering" href="/docs/reference/edge-rendering" description="Paths, anchors, markers, rendering data, interaction, and accessibility" />

  <Card title="Measurement" href="/docs/reference/measurement" description="Observers, DOM rectangles, bounds, and namespaces" />

  <Card title="Themes & Styles" href="/docs/reference/themes" description="Explicit visual entry points and style injection" />

  <Card title="Package Entry Points" href="/docs/reference/package-entry-points" description="Imports, audiences, SSR conditions, and tree-shaking boundaries" />
</Cards>

Stability vocabulary [#stability-vocabulary]

| Label               | Meaning                                                                 |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Most users**      | Recommended high-level interface with product-level contract coverage   |
| **Advanced**        | Stable atom for a real custom renderer or integration need              |
| **Adapter authors** | Framework-neutral primitive; expect to own lifecycle and rendering glue |
| **Browser-only**    | Reads DOM geometry or dispatches native events; do not call during SSR  |
| **Experimental**    | May change before 1.0; the page states the current limitation           |

DiaX is pre-1.0. The package boundary and maturity label are part of each interface contract; a
symbol being exported from Core does not imply that applications should assemble the entire
rendering pipeline themselves.


# Measurement (/docs/reference/measurement)



**Audience:** framework adapter and custom renderer authors.\
&#x2A;*Runtime:** browser-only in normal use; helpers return safe no-op results during SSR.\
&#x2A;*Import:** `diax`.

Measurement is a lifecycle seam, not a layout algorithm. Diagram computes placement first, then an
adapter measures the rendered nodes so edges can attach to their real boxes. Connect skips
automatic placement but uses the same surface-owned geometry principle.

Surface ownership [#surface-ownership]

Mark the measurement surface with `data-diax-canvas` and each endpoint with a stable
`data-diax-node` value. `findOwnedNodeElements(container)` excludes endpoints belonging to a
nested DiaX canvas.

This prevents a parent overlay from accidentally drawing edges for a child diagram. Cross-surface
geometry requires an explicit shared owner; a qualified ID alone does not create one.

`measureNodeRects(container)` [#measurenoderectscontainer]

Returns a `Map<string, NodeRect>` in the container's scrollable local coordinate space. It
compensates for borders, scroll offsets, and ancestor scale transforms.

```ts
import { measureNodeRects } from 'diax';

const rects = measureNodeRects(container);
const source = rects.get('source');
```

On the server it returns an empty map. Do not use an SSR result as evidence that browser geometry
is valid.

`createMeasurementObserver(container, config)` [#createmeasurementobservercontainer-config]

```ts
import { createMeasurementObserver } from 'diax';

const observer = createMeasurementObserver(container, {
  mode: 'auto',
  onMeasure(rects) {
    renderEdges(rects);
  },
});

observer.observe();
observer.measure();
observer.disconnect();
```

Always call `disconnect()` when the owning surface unmounts.

| Mode         | Watches                                                    | Use when                    |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `resize`     | Container and node `ResizeObserver`                        | Static content              |
| `auto`       | Resize, DOM mutation, animation/transition completion      | Default dynamic UI          |
| `continuous` | Auto plus animation-frame measurement during active motion | Edges must track moving DOM |

`continuous` is intentionally opt-in because it trades CPU for motion fidelity. Prefer reduced
motion and a settled final measurement for ordinary documentation.

Diagram routing obstacles [#diagram-routing-obstacles]

Automatic Diagram adapters also measure semantic-group labels because those labels sit on the group
border and can block entry or exit ports. Use the dedicated leaf instead of making Connect or a
server-only planner load this browser lifecycle:

```ts contract
import { createDiagramMeasurementObserver } from 'diax/diagram-measurement';
import { planLayeredLayout } from 'diax/layout-plan';
import type { LayoutNode, ParsedRelation } from 'diax';

const container = document.createElement('div');
const edges: ParsedRelation[] = [];
const layoutMap = new Map<string, LayoutNode>();

const observer = createDiagramMeasurementObserver(container, {
  onMeasure(nodeRects, { groupLabelRects }) {
    planLayeredLayout({ edges, rects: nodeRects, layoutMap, groupLabelRects });
  },
});
```

Labels must carry `data-diax-group-label-id` using the same resolved identity as their
`data-diax-group` surface. The shared observer watches nodes and labels in one lifecycle, preserves
local aliases for namespaced IDs, and excludes nested DiaX canvases. Application authors should not
estimate `labelWidth` or provide port offsets.

Bounds utilities [#bounds-utilities]

| Function                             | Purpose                           |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| `rectToBox(rect)` / `boxToRect(box)` | Convert rectangle representations |
| `getBoundsOfBoxes(a, b)`             | Union of two boxes                |
| `getOverlappingArea(a, b)`           | Intersection area, or zero        |
| `getNodesBounds(nodes)`              | Collective node bounds            |
| `clamp(value, min, max)`             | Numeric range clamp               |

These functions are pure and server-safe.

Namespaces [#namespaces]

| Function                       | Purpose                                          |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `resolveId(rawId, namespace?)` | Qualify a local ID as `namespace::id`            |
| `parseNamespacedId(id)`        | Split a qualified ID                             |
| `isCrossDiagramRef(id)`        | Detect an already-qualified reference            |
| `partitionEdges(edges)`        | Separate local layout edges from qualified edges |

`isCrossDiagramRef` is a historical name. Official renderers do not draw between independent
canvas elements. A cross-surface relation needs one shared measurement and overlay owner.

Measurement acceptance [#measurement-acceptance]

A custom adapter should verify resize, scroll, nested surfaces, transforms, dynamic content,
unmount cleanup, 200% zoom, and browser differences. Geometry unit tests alone are not sufficient.

Related [#related]

* [Edge Rendering](/docs/reference/edge-rendering)
* [React Connect](/docs/react/connect)
* [Browser accessibility contract](/docs/guide/accessibility)


# Package Entry Points (/docs/reference/package-entry-points)



**Audience:** application architects, library authors, and deployment owners.

Choose an entry point by responsibility. Do not import a broad product surface and rely on a
bundler to rediscover boundaries that the package already exposes.

Core [#core]

| Import                     | Contains                                                                                                    | Runtime                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `diax`                     | Validation, AST conversion, layout, geometry, measurement helpers                                           | Pure APIs are server-safe; measurement no-ops on SSR                       |
| `diax/layout-plan`         | Measured layered routing, stable node/group ports, route sections, label tracks, and `LayoutPlan` rendering | Pure and server-safe; opt-in for Diagram/custom renderer jobs              |
| `diax/diagram-measurement` | Node and group-label DOM measurement lifecycle for automatic Diagram routing                                | Browser-only adapter seam; excluded from pure planners and Connect         |
| `diax/edge-geometry`       | Direct anchors, stable edge identities, paths, labels, and endpoint geometry                                | Pure and server-safe; excludes graph layout and automatic obstacle routing |
| `diax/themes`              | Theme values and conversion/injection                                                                       | Conversion is server-safe; injection is browser-only                       |
| `diax/styles.css`          | Core CSS variables and edge styles                                                                          | CSS asset                                                                  |
| `diax/schemas/diax.json`   | Serializable DiaX schema                                                                                    | Build/server tooling                                                       |

React [#react]

| Import                | Use it for                                       | Does not include                                     |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `@diax/react`         | Data-first Diagram components and hooks          | Connect, JSX definition markers, Mermaid, UI presets |
| `@diax/react/connect` | Relations over already-positioned JSX/CSS        | Automatic node layout, Mermaid, UI presets           |
| `@diax/react/jsx`     | Static sibling `DiaxNode` / `DiaxEdge` authoring | Connect and Mermaid                                  |

Use exactly one topology source for a surface. A subpath is a semantic contract, not a `mode`
flag: importing Connect cannot accidentally pull the Diagram authoring adapter into the same
module graph.

Connect composes `diax/edge-geometry` rather than Diagram's smart router. Custom renderers whose
host CSS owns node placement should choose the same leaf. Official Diagram adapters compose
`diax/layout-plan`; custom Diagram renderers choose it explicitly so Core-only consumers and native
ESM never evaluate the measured planner by accident. Official adapters pair it with
`diax/diagram-measurement`; server-only planners and Connect consumers do not load that DOM seam.

Optional product layers [#optional-product-layers]

| Import                        | Responsibility                                                                            |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@diax/ui-react`              | Styled DOM node primitives and renderer registries                                        |
| `@diax/ui-react/presentation` | Parser-free semantic roles for reports, architecture and ordinary React DOM               |
| `@diax/ui-react/mermaid`      | React composition for the supported Mermaid subset                                        |
| `@diax/ui-react/styles.css`   | Optional primitive styles                                                                 |
| `@diax/mermaid`               | Mermaid detection, parsing, transformation, and diagnostics                               |
| `@diax/layout-elk`            | Experimental async ELK `LayoutPlan` adapter                                               |
| `@diax/notebook`              | Notebook surface                                                                          |
| `@diax/notebook/playground`   | Full multi-mode Playground product                                                        |
| `remark-diax`                 | Build-time Remark transformation plus VFile diagnostics for supported diagram code blocks |

`@diax/mermaid` depends on parser infrastructure and should not enter a normal Diagram or Connect
bundle. `@diax/notebook/playground` is a product boundary, not a component barrel for application
runtime code.

`remark-diax` leaves an invalid fence readable and reports the importer result through the current
VFile. Live previews can display those messages without stopping rendering; strict build hosts
collect the complete report before failing. See the [`remark-diax` Reference](/docs/reference/remark-diax)
for the message contract and host policy. The package is ESM-only because its importer and Unified
toolchain are ESM-only; configure it from an ESM build config rather than `require()`.

All DiaX-family peers of `@diax/ui-react` are optional at package-install time. Root and
`/presentation` consumers need only React; `/mermaid` consumers install `diax`, `@diax/react` and
`@diax/mermaid` explicitly.

Framework adapters [#framework-adapters]

`@diax/vue`, `@diax/svelte`, `@diax/solid`, and `@diax/vanilla` expose their framework's
high-level Diagram interface and lower-level bindings. Check
[Framework Parity](/docs/guide/feature-parity) before assuming a React-only authoring surface exists
in every adapter.

Tree-shaking checklist [#tree-shaking-checklist]

1. Import from the narrow documented subpath.
2. Keep Mermaid, UI primitives, ELK, and Notebook out of shared application barrels.
3. Use `import type` for types.
4. Load Playground and Mermaid composition with a literal dynamic import at the route or feature
   boundary.
5. Import CSS explicitly; do not depend on an unrelated component for global styles.
6. Test the built consumer artifact or sourcemap, not only the source import statement.

Package metadata marks JavaScript entries side-effect free where appropriate and lists CSS
explicitly. This supports tree-shaking, but a consumer barrel that eagerly re-exports every DiaX
package can still defeat the intended product boundary.

Module Federation [#module-federation]

Federated consumers should expose the smallest leaf they need, share `react` and `react-dom` as
compatible singletons, and keep Core versions aligned across host and remote. Do not federate the
Playground as a substitute for the React runtime.

Version mismatch, server/client condition selection, and eager shared dependencies can change the
actual graph. Validate a production host/remote build and interaction smoke test before release.

SSR and React Server Components [#ssr-and-react-server-components]

* Core validation, parsing, and layout can run on the server.
* Diagram and Connect edge surfaces measure DOM after hydration.
* `@diax/react/connect` is a client entry.
* Serializable Diagram definitions may cross an RSC boundary.
* Do not pass event handlers or unreviewed generated JSX across a serialization boundary.
* Import Mermaid parsing on the server when possible; keep its parser out of the client graph unless
  the browser editor needs it.

Related [#related]

* [React SSR](/docs/react/ssr)
* [Performance](/docs/guide/performance)
* [AI trust boundary](/docs/guide/ai-integration)


# remark-diax (/docs/reference/remark-diax)





**Audience:** documentation-platform maintainers and live-preview implementers.

`remark-diax` is an ESM-only Remark plugin for trusted Markdown/MDX builds. It transforms supported
Mermaid fences into an imported React component and reports importer diagnostics through the
current VFile. It is not a Markdown renderer, a runtime sandbox, or a second DiaX language.

For ordinary JSX in MDX, start with the [MDX Guide](/docs/guide/mdx-guide). You need this reference
only when the build should transform fenced source automatically.

Installation and runtime boundary [#installation-and-runtime-boundary]

<InstallTabs packages="['remark-diax', '@diax/ui-react', '@diax/react', '@diax/mermaid']" description="Plugin, DOM renderer, React binding, and supported-subset importer" />

Also import `@diax/ui-react/styles.css` once from the application's global stylesheet. The plugin
automatically emits this static component import when at least one fence is valid:

```js
import { SmartMermaidDiagram } from '@diax/ui-react/mermaid';
```

The host therefore needs to install and resolve the renderer packages, but does not register a
global component. `remark-diax` and its Mermaid importer are ESM-only; configure them from an ESM
file such as `next.config.mjs` or `docusaurus.config.mjs`, not through `require()`.

Minimal configuration [#minimal-configuration]

The plugin export and options below are compiled as part of the documentation contract:

```ts title="remark-diax-options.ts" contract
import { remarkDiax, type RemarkDiaxOptions } from 'remark-diax';

const options: RemarkDiaxOptions = {
  languages: ['mermaid', 'diax-mermaid'],
  theme: 'github',
};

export const diaxRemarkPlugin = [remarkDiax, options] as const;
```

Pass `remarkDiax` or the option tuple to the normal `remarkPlugins` array exposed by the host.
The snippets below are configuration fragments because each platform owns the surrounding config.

Evidence boundary [#evidence-boundary]

The documentation contract resolves `remark-diax` through its package manifest and built declaration
entry, so the export and option names above cannot drift silently. The package test suite also runs
a real `@mdx-js/mdx` compile with valid and invalid fences and verifies the resulting JSX import and
VFile messages:

```bash
pnpm --filter remark-diax test
```

This documentation site is the Fumadocs production fixture: its real `source.config.ts` registers
`remarkDiax`, the content build transforms the dedicated fence below, and the browser contract
verifies the injected renderer, nodes, and measured edges. Next MDX and Docusaurus do not yet have
equivalent production fixtures; their snippets remain host configuration fragments rather than an
independently verified support matrix.

`pnpm smoke:docs` also locks the fixture's workspace dependency, dedicated fence, generated import
source, application-owned Client Component bridge, and browser selector as one configuration
contract. A partial edit cannot leave the page looking documented while silently bypassing the
plugin.

Fumadocs [#fumadocs]

Fumadocs on Next.js compiles MDX as a Server Component. Keep the document server-renderable and
bridge only the hook-based diagram renderer into a Client Component:

```tsx title="components/mdx/smart-mermaid-diagram-client.tsx" contract
'use client';

export { SmartMermaidDiagram } from '@diax/ui-react/mermaid';
```

Then point the existing `importSource` option at that application-owned bridge:

```ts title="source.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from 'fumadocs-mdx/config';
import { remarkDiax } from 'remark-diax';

export default defineConfig({
  mdxOptions: {
    remarkPlugins: [
      [remarkDiax, {
        importSource: '@/components/mdx/smart-mermaid-diagram-client',
      }],
    ],
  },
});
```

Live Fumadocs host fixture [#live-fumadocs-host-fixture]

The following source is not a pre-authored React component. Fumadocs passes its custom fence through
the installed plugin during the real Docs build, which injects the client bridge and renders
`SmartMermaidDiagram` without turning the whole document into a Client Component:

<SmartMermaidDiagram
  chart="`flowchart LR
  source[MDX source] --> transform[remark-diax]
  transform --> dom[DiaX DOM]`"
  theme="github"
  className="remark-diax-fumadocs-fixture"
/>

Next.js with `@next/mdx` [#nextjs-with-nextmdx]

```js title="next.config.mjs"
import createMDX from '@next/mdx';
import { remarkDiax } from 'remark-diax';

const withMDX = createMDX({
  options: {
    remarkPlugins: [[remarkDiax, { theme: 'github' }]],
  },
});

export default withMDX({ pageExtensions: ['mdx', 'tsx'] });
```

Docusaurus [#docusaurus]

```js title="docusaurus.config.mjs"
import { remarkDiax } from 'remark-diax';

export default {
  presets: [
    ['classic', {
      docs: {
        remarkPlugins: [[remarkDiax, { theme: 'light' }]],
      },
    }],
  ],
};
```

Options [#options]

| Option         | Type       | Default                               | Meaning                                |
| -------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `languages`    | `string[]` | `['diax', 'diax-mermaid', 'mermaid']` | Fence languages to inspect             |
| `component`    | `string`   | `'SmartMermaidDiagram'`               | Named JSX component to emit            |
| `importSource` | `string`   | `'@diax/ui-react/mermaid'`            | Static import source for the component |
| `theme`        | `string`   | —                                     | Theme prop passed to the component     |
| `className`    | `string`   | —                                     | Class on the diagram wrapper           |

Changing `component` or `importSource` is an advanced renderer seam. The target module must export
that exact named component and accept the generated `chart`, `centered`, optional `theme`, and
optional `className` props.

Fence and diagram support [#fence-and-diagram-support]

The `mermaid`, `diax-mermaid`, and legacy `diax` fence aliases all contain Mermaid source. The
plugin uses the same supported subset as `@diax/mermaid`:

* `flowchart` / `graph`;
* `classDiagram`;
* `stateDiagram` / `stateDiagram-v2`;
* `erDiagram`;
* `requirementDiagram`;
* `mindmap`.

Sequence, Gantt, Pie, Timeline, Sankey and other families are not implied by the fence name. See the
[Mermaid Guide](/docs/guide/mermaid) for syntax and fidelity limits.

VFile diagnostics [#vfile-diagnostics]

Every matching fence is parsed through the public `parseMermaid()` importer. A valid fence becomes
JSX. An invalid or unsupported fence remains the original code node so the page never degrades into
a silent blank.

For each importer diagnostic, the plugin appends a standard VFile message:

| Field    | Value                                      |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `source` | `'remark-diax'`                            |
| `ruleId` | Original `MermaidDiagnosticCode`           |
| `reason` | Human-readable problem                     |
| `note`   | Suggested repair when available            |
| `place`  | Markdown-document-relative source location |
| `url`    | Mermaid import guide                       |

Messages are non-fatal by default because the original fence remains readable. The package does not
add a custom payload, reporter callback, global diagnostic provider, or `strict` option.

Strict build policy [#strict-build-policy]

Run the complete processor, then select messages by the standard `source` field. Apply failure only
after processing so a document with multiple bad fences produces one complete report:

```ts title="strict-build-policy.ts"
const file = await processor.process({ path: 'guide.mdx', value: source });
const errors = file.messages.filter((message) => message.source === 'remark-diax');

if (errors.length > 0) {
  throw new AggregateError(errors, 'DiaX fences failed validation');
}
```

This is a policy fragment: `processor` and `source` belong to the host's existing Unified pipeline.
When using `remark-cli`, its standard `--frail` option can fail the process on VFile messages.

Live-preview policy [#live-preview-policy]

Use the same configured processor and create a fresh VFile for every editor revision. If the host
imports `VFile` itself, declare `vfile` as a direct host dependency instead of relying on the
plugin's transitive graph.

```ts title="live-preview-policy.ts"
import { VFile } from 'vfile';

const file = new VFile({ path: activePath, value: source });
const tree = processor.parse(file);
const transformedTree = await processor.run(tree, file);
const markers = file.messages
  .filter((message) => message.source === 'remark-diax')
  .map((message) => ({
    code: message.ruleId,
    severity: 'error',
    message: message.reason,
    hint: message.note,
    line: message.line,
    column: message.column,
  }));
```

This is also a host fragment: `activePath`, `source`, and `processor` come from the editor. The
important lifecycle contract is one VFile per revision, which prevents stale messages from leaking
into the next preview. `transformedTree` contains JSX for valid diagrams and the original code node
for invalid ones.

Host checklist [#host-checklist]

1. Use an ESM build configuration.
2. Install the renderer companions and import `@diax/ui-react/styles.css` once.
3. Treat MDX as trusted executable source.
4. Preserve invalid fences and surface every VFile message.
5. Fail strict builds only after collecting the complete report.
6. Create a fresh VFile for each live-preview revision.
7. Keep `remark-diax` out of routes that do not compile Mermaid fences.

Related [#related]

* [MDX Integration](/docs/guide/mdx-guide)
* [Mermaid Import](/docs/guide/mermaid)
* [Package Entry Points](/docs/reference/package-entry-points)
* [Troubleshooting](/docs/guide/troubleshooting)


# Themes & Styles (/docs/reference/themes)



**Audience:** application authors and adapter authors.\
&#x2A;*Runtime:** theme conversion is server-safe; injection functions require the browser.\
&#x2A;*Imports:** `diax/themes`, `diax`, or `diax/styles.css`.

Visual code is an explicit dependency [#visual-code-is-an-explicit-dependency]

The headless `diax` root does not import built-in theme presets. Import them from the dedicated
entry so nonvisual consumers do not load theme data:

```ts contract
import { resolveTheme, themes, themeToCSS, themeToStyle } from 'diax/themes';

const github = resolveTheme('github');
const css = themeToCSS(themes.github);
const darkStyle = themeToStyle(themes.github, 'dark');
```

Built-in names are `linear`, `light`, `notion`, and `github`.

Custom theme values [#custom-theme-values]

```ts contract
import type { DiaxTheme } from 'diax/themes';

const midnight: DiaxTheme = {
  name: 'midnight',
  light: {
    '--diax-node-bg': '#f8fafc',
    '--diax-node-text': '#0f172a',
  },
  dark: {
    '--diax-node-bg': '#0f172a',
    '--diax-node-text': '#f8fafc',
  },
};
```

Custom themes are values passed to a component or helper. DiaX does not maintain a global mutable
theme registry.

Delivery choices [#delivery-choices]

Framework component [#framework-component]

Pass a built-in name or theme value through the adapter's `theme` prop. This is the normal
application path.

Static stylesheet [#static-stylesheet]

```css
@import 'diax/styles.css';
```

Use the stylesheet when your integration wants explicit CSS delivery instead of runtime injection.

Custom adapter [#custom-adapter]

```ts
import { injectThemeStyles, themes } from 'diax/themes';
import { injectEdgeStyles } from 'diax';

injectThemeStyles(themes.github);
injectEdgeStyles();
```

`injectThemeStyles()`, `injectEdgeStyles()`, and `injectStaggerStyles()` mutate the document
and must run only in the browser. Official adapters own the edge-style lifecycle; application code
should not call these functions a second time without a custom-renderer reason.

UI Primitives [#ui-primitives]

`@diax/ui-react/styles.css` styles the optional DOM presentation primitives with low-specificity
selectors and DiaX variables. It does not belong in Core and is not loaded by `@diax/react`.

```css
@import '@diax/ui-react/styles.css';
```

Related [#related]

* [UI Primitives](/docs/ui-react)
* [Theme guide](/docs/guide/themes)
* [Package Entry Points](/docs/reference/package-entry-points)


# ClassNode (/docs/ui-react/class-diagram)





Overview [#overview]

`ClassNode` renders UML class diagram nodes with three sections: header (name + stereotype),
attributes, and methods. Supports both compound composition and data-driven modes.

Compound Composition [#compound-composition]

<DiagramPreview
  title="ClassNode — compound composition"
  code="`import { ClassNode, ClassHeader, ClassAttributes, ClassMethods } from '@diax/ui-react';

<ClassNode>
<ClassHeader stereotype=&#x22;interface&#x22;>Animal</ClassHeader>
<ClassAttributes items={[&#x22;+name: string&#x22;, &#x22;-age: int&#x22;, &#x22;#id: uuid&#x22;]} />
<ClassMethods items={[&#x22;+eat(): void&#x22;, &#x22;+sleep(): void&#x22;, &#x22;-digest(): void&#x22;]} />
</ClassNode>`"
>
  <ClassNode>
    <ClassHeader stereotype="interface">
      Animal
    </ClassHeader>

    <ClassAttributes items="[&#x22;+name: string&#x22;, &#x22;-age: int&#x22;, &#x22;#id: uuid&#x22;]" />

    <ClassMethods items="[&#x22;+eat(): void&#x22;, &#x22;+sleep(): void&#x22;, &#x22;-digest(): void&#x22;]" />
  </ClassNode>
</DiagramPreview>

Data-driven [#data-driven]

<DiagramPreview
  title="ClassNode — data prop"
  code="`<ClassNode data={{
name: &#x22;UserService&#x22;,
stereotype: &#x22;service&#x22;,
attributes: [&#x22;-db: Database&#x22;, &#x22;-cache: Redis&#x22;],
methods: [&#x22;+getUser(id): User&#x22;, &#x22;+createUser(data): User&#x22;, &#x22;-validate(): bool&#x22;],
}} />`"
>
  <ClassNode
    data="{
  name: &#x22;UserService&#x22;,
  stereotype: &#x22;service&#x22;,
  attributes: [&#x22;-db: Database&#x22;, &#x22;-cache: Redis&#x22;],
  methods: [&#x22;+getUser(id): User&#x22;, &#x22;+createUser(data): User&#x22;, &#x22;-validate(): bool&#x22;],
}"
  />
</DiagramPreview>

Visibility Indicators [#visibility-indicators]

UML visibility symbols are color-coded:

| Symbol | Visibility | Color |
| ------ | ---------- | ----- |
| `+`    | public     | Green |
| `-`    | private    | Red   |
| `#`    | protected  | Amber |
| `~`    | package    | Blue  |

Interactive States [#interactive-states]

<DiagramPreview
  title="Highlighted & dimmed"
  code="`<div className=&#x22;flex gap-4&#x22;>

<ClassNode highlighted data={{ name: &#x22;Highlighted&#x22;, attributes: [&#x22;+id: int&#x22;] }} />
<ClassNode dimmed data={{ name: &#x22;Dimmed&#x22;, attributes: [&#x22;+id: int&#x22;] }} />
</div>`"
>
  <div className="flex gap-4">
    <ClassNode data="{ name: &#x22;Normal&#x22;, attributes: [&#x22;+id: int&#x22;] }" />

    <ClassNode data="{ name: &#x22;Highlighted&#x22;, attributes: [&#x22;+id: int&#x22;] }" />

    <ClassNode data="{ name: &#x22;Dimmed&#x22;, attributes: [&#x22;+id: int&#x22;] }" />
  </div>
</DiagramPreview>

With Mermaid [#with-mermaid]

<DiagramPreview
  title="ClassDiagram from Mermaid syntax"
  code="`import { ClassDiagram } from '@diax/ui-react/mermaid';

<ClassDiagram chart={\`

class Animal {
  +String name
  +eat() void
}
class Dog {
  +bark() void
}
Animal <|-- Dog
\`} centered density=&#x22;spacious&#x22; />`"

  <ClassDiagram
    chart="`classDiagram
