Props [#props]

ClassNode [#classnode]

| Prop          | Type                                           | Description      |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `data`        | `{ name, stereotype?, attributes?, methods? }` | Data-driven mode |
| `highlighted` | `boolean`                                      | Accent ring      |
| `dimmed`      | `boolean`                                      | Reduced opacity  |

ClassHeader [#classheader]

| Prop         | Type     | Description                                    |
| ------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `stereotype` | `string` | UML stereotype (e.g., "interface", "abstract") |

ClassAttributes / ClassMethods [#classattributes--classmethods]

| Prop    | Type       | Description                                          |
| ------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `items` | `string[]` | Member strings (prefix with +/-/#/\~ for visibility) |


# Data Model Recipes (/docs/ui-react/data-model-recipes)





One model, four visual questions [#one-model-four-visual-questions]

A database design review is not one giant ER diagram. Readers usually ask four different questions:

1. Which entities own which fields and relationships?
2. How can a record move between durable states?
3. How did the schema evolve without losing reversibility?
4. Does the read strategy stay inside its performance budget?

Each question deserves the native structure that preserves its meaning. These recipes combine
`EntityNode`, `StateNode` and the isolated Presentation entry; they do not add a `schema` mode or a
second data-model DSL.

<Callout type="info">
  These examples were generalized from a real SQLite persistence design. The original document
  combined ER cards, lifecycle state, migration history, pragmas and query evidence. DiaX keeps
  those concerns composable instead of flattening them into one universal component.
</Callout>

Relational schema: entities plus measured cardinality [#relational-schema-entities-plus-measured-cardinality]

<DiagramPreview title="Relational schema map" description="One parent entity, two foreign-key collections and visible cardinality labels" code="relationalSchemaRecipeCode">
  <RelationalSchemaRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

Use `EntityNode` when the table shape and field vocabulary matter. Keep PK, FK and UK visible as
text; color only accelerates scanning. `ConnectionSurface` measures the entity cards after fonts,
localized field names and application CSS have settled.

This recipe deliberately uses ordinary `nodes` in authored CSS rather than introducing `Table`,
`Column`, `ForeignKey` or `Cardinality` objects. The data model already has those concepts; DiaX only
needs stable target IDs and relations.

Constraint contract [#constraint-contract]

Known constraint abbreviations now ship with self-contained package styling and accessible names:

| Visible text | Accessible name | Default semantic tone |
| ------------ | --------------- | --------------------- |
| `PK`         | Primary key     | warning               |
| `FK`         | Foreign key     | information           |
| `UK`         | Unique key      | accent                |

The package stylesheet uses `data-diax-ui-part="constraint"`; consumers do not need Tailwind's
amber, blue or dark-mode utility classes for these badges. Unknown constraint strings remain
visible and receive the neutral treatment.

Record lifecycle: main path first [#record-lifecycle-main-path-first]

<DiagramPreview title="Record lifecycle" description="Four durable states connected separately from exception and rollback policy" code="recordLifecycleRecipeCode">
  <RecordLifecycleRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

Use `StateNode` for durable states, not for every action. The main transitions belong in the
centralized relation list. Exceptional rules such as “any state → ignored” are often easier to read
as a definition list below the graph than as four duplicate feedback edges.

This distinction keeps dense state machines reviewable:

* a state answers “what can be true now?”;
* an edge label answers “what transition happened?”;
* an exception note answers “what policy applies across several states?”

Do not encode these three jobs in one overloaded state component.

Migration ledger: chronology is document structure [#migration-ledger-chronology-is-document-structure]

<DiagramPreview title="Schema migration ledger" description="A durable store beside three ordered, reversible migration stages" code="migrationLedgerRecipeCode">
  <MigrationLedgerRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

The current database is a `DataStoreNode`. Version history is an `<ol>` containing `StageNode`
records. Neither needs arrows to communicate its primary meaning, so the recipe does not load
Connect.

Keep migration rules visible beside the version that depends on them:

* make DDL idempotent;
* check the existing schema before `ALTER`;
* introduce nullable data before enforcing it;
* advance the stored version only after the migration succeeds.

A public `MigrationTimeline` would mostly rename `<ol>` and forward Stage props. Deleting it would
remove little complexity, so it remains a recipe.

Query budget: evidence is not topology [#query-budget-evidence-is-not-topology]

<DiagramPreview title="Query budget" description="Metric summaries plus a native scaling table—no graph runtime required" code="queryBudgetRecipeCode">
  <QueryBudgetRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

The question is quantitative, not relational. `MetricNode` makes the headline result reusable;
`table`, `caption`, column scopes and row scopes preserve the comparison. The internal scroll region
is keyboard focusable on narrow screens, while the page itself remains overflow-free.

This is an important DiaX design rule: a rich visual explanation may contain sections that do not
need DiaX. Composition is a feature. Loading a graph runtime for every table, KPI or annotation
would weaken both DX and tree-shaking.

Import boundaries [#import-boundaries]

Choose entries per role instead of importing the entire visual vocabulary:

```tsx contract
import { EntityNode, StateNode } from '@diax/ui-react';
import {
  DataStoreNode,
  DiagramFrame,
  MetricNode,
  StageNode,
} from '@diax/ui-react/presentation';
import { ConnectionSurface, connectionTarget } from '@diax/react/connect';
```

* ER and state shapes stay in the small `@diax/ui-react` root.
* Report roles stay in the independent `/presentation` leaf.
* Connect is needed only by the relational and lifecycle recipes.
* Mermaid parsing remains isolated in `/mermaid` and is not loaded here.

AI authoring prompt [#ai-authoring-prompt]

Give an agent the visual question and the ownership rule:

```text
Create a React visual explanation for a SQLite-backed record model.

Use EntityNode for tables and fields, StateNode for durable lifecycle states,
StageNode inside an ordered list for schema versions, and MetricNode plus a native
table for query evidence. Use ConnectionSurface only for foreign-key and state-transition
relations. Keep constraint abbreviations, transition labels and migration guarantees visible.

Do not invent SchemaDiagram, lifecycle mode, coordinates, ports or SVG table shapes.
The result must preserve reading order at 320 px and remain meaningful when edges are hidden.
```

For untrusted model output, validate a data contract first and map known entity, state, stage and
metric types to these trusted React renderers. Do not execute model-produced JSX at runtime.

Graduation decisions [#graduation-decisions]

| Candidate                         | Decision                  | Reason                                                               |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `EntityNode` constraint semantics | Deepen existing primitive | Accessibility and theme behavior otherwise repeat in every ER caller |
| `SchemaDiagram`                   | Reject                    | Topology already belongs to Diagram or Connect                       |
| `Lifecycle` mode                  | Reject                    | States and relations already express the model                       |
| `MigrationTimeline`               | Keep as recipe            | Native ordered lists and StageNode contain the useful semantics      |
| `QueryBudget` component           | Keep as recipe            | Copy, dimensions and thresholds are application-owned evidence       |

The useful public interface stays small while the recipe catalog becomes richer. That is the
intended direction for `@diax/ui-react`: reusable semantic roles, abundant copy-owned compositions.


# EntityNode (/docs/ui-react/er-diagram)





Overview [#overview]

`EntityNode` renders ER diagram entities in a table-style layout with header and attribute rows.
PK/FK/UK constraint badges include visible abbreviations, accessible names and self-contained
package styling. They do not depend on Tailwind color utilities or a host `.dark` selector.

Compound Composition [#compound-composition]

<DiagramPreview
  title="EntityNode — compound composition"
  code="`import { EntityNode, EntityHeader, EntityAttributes, EntityAttribute } from '@diax/ui-react';

<EntityNode>
<EntityHeader>CUSTOMER</EntityHeader>
<EntityAttributes>
  <EntityAttribute constraint=&#x22;PK&#x22; name=&#x22;id&#x22; type=&#x22;int&#x22; />
  <EntityAttribute constraint=&#x22;FK&#x22; name=&#x22;order_id&#x22; type=&#x22;int&#x22; />
  <EntityAttribute name=&#x22;name&#x22; type=&#x22;varchar(255)&#x22; />
  <EntityAttribute name=&#x22;email&#x22; type=&#x22;varchar(255)&#x22; />
</EntityAttributes>
</EntityNode>`"
>
  <EntityNode>
    <EntityHeader>
      CUSTOMER
    </EntityHeader>

    <EntityAttributes>
      <EntityAttribute constraint="PK" name="id" type="int" />

      <EntityAttribute constraint="FK" name="order_id" type="int" />

      <EntityAttribute name="name" type="varchar(255)" />

      <EntityAttribute name="email" type="varchar(255)" />
    </EntityAttributes>
  </EntityNode>
</DiagramPreview>

Data-driven [#data-driven]

<DiagramPreview
  title="EntityNode — data prop"
  code="`<EntityNode data={{
name: &#x22;ORDER&#x22;,
attributes: [
  { name: &#x22;id&#x22;, type: &#x22;int&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;PK&#x22; },
  { name: &#x22;customer_id&#x22;, type: &#x22;int&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;FK&#x22; },
  { name: &#x22;total&#x22;, type: &#x22;decimal(10,2)&#x22; },
  { name: &#x22;status&#x22;, type: &#x22;varchar(20)&#x22; },
  { name: &#x22;sku&#x22;, type: &#x22;varchar(50)&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;UK&#x22; },
],
}} />`"
>
  <EntityNode
    data="{
  name: &#x22;ORDER&#x22;,
  attributes: [
    { name: &#x22;id&#x22;, type: &#x22;int&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;PK&#x22; },
    { name: &#x22;customer_id&#x22;, type: &#x22;int&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;FK&#x22; },
    { name: &#x22;total&#x22;, type: &#x22;decimal(10,2)&#x22; },
    { name: &#x22;status&#x22;, type: &#x22;varchar(20)&#x22; },
    { name: &#x22;sku&#x22;, type: &#x22;varchar(50)&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;UK&#x22; },
  ],
}"
  />
</DiagramPreview>

Constraint Badges [#constraint-badges]

| Constraint | Color  | Meaning     |
| ---------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `PK`       | Amber  | Primary Key |
| `FK`       | Blue   | Foreign Key |
| `UK`       | Purple | Unique Key  |

Known abbreviations expose `Primary key`, `Foreign key` and `Unique key` to assistive technology.
Custom constraint strings remain visible and receive the neutral token. The badges also use
`data-diax-ui-part="constraint"` and `data-constraint`, so application themes can restyle them
without replacing the component structure.

For a complete parent/child schema, lifecycle and migration example, see
[Data Model Recipes](/docs/ui-react/data-model-recipes).

Interactive States [#interactive-states]

<DiagramPreview
  title="Highlighted & dimmed"
  code="`<div className=&#x22;flex gap-4&#x22;>
<EntityNode data={{ name: &#x22;NORMAL&#x22;, attributes: [{ name: &#x22;id&#x22;, type: &#x22;int&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;PK&#x22; }] }} />
<EntityNode highlighted data={{ name: &#x22;HIGHLIGHTED&#x22;, attributes: [{ name: &#x22;id&#x22;, type: &#x22;int&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;PK&#x22; }] }} />
<EntityNode dimmed data={{ name: &#x22;DIMMED&#x22;, attributes: [{ name: &#x22;id&#x22;, type: &#x22;int&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;PK&#x22; }] }} />
</div>`"
>
  <div className="flex gap-4">
    <EntityNode data="{ name: &#x22;NORMAL&#x22;, attributes: [{ name: &#x22;id&#x22;, type: &#x22;int&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;PK&#x22; }] }" />

    <EntityNode data="{ name: &#x22;HIGHLIGHTED&#x22;, attributes: [{ name: &#x22;id&#x22;, type: &#x22;int&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;PK&#x22; }] }" />

    <EntityNode data="{ name: &#x22;DIMMED&#x22;, attributes: [{ name: &#x22;id&#x22;, type: &#x22;int&#x22;, constraint: &#x22;PK&#x22; }] }" />
  </div>
</DiagramPreview>

Props [#props]

EntityAttribute [#entityattribute]

| Prop         | Type                             | Description      |
| ------------ | -------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `name`       | `string`                         | Attribute name   |
| `type`       | `string`                         | Data type        |
| `constraint` | `"PK" \| "FK" \| "UK" \| string` | Constraint badge |


# FlowNode (/docs/ui-react/flowchart)





Overview [#overview]

`FlowNode` renders flow diagram nodes with configurable shapes via the `variant` prop.

Variants [#variants]

| Variant    | Shape                  | Use Case          |
| ---------- | ---------------------- | ----------------- |
| `default`  | Rounded rectangle      | General steps     |
| `decision` | Diamond (rotated)      | Yes/No branches   |
| `terminal` | Stadium/pill           | Start/End         |
| `database` | Cylinder top           | Databases, stores |
| `process`  | Sharp rectangle        | Processing steps  |
| `io`       | Parallelogram (skewed) | Input/Output      |

All Variants [#all-variants]

  title="FlowNode — 6 shape variants"

<FlowNode variant=&#x22;terminal&#x22;>Terminal</FlowNode>
<FlowNode variant=&#x22;database&#x22;>Database</FlowNode>
<FlowNode variant=&#x22;process&#x22;>Process</FlowNode>
<FlowNode variant=&#x22;io&#x22;>I/O</FlowNode>
</div>`"
>
  <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4 items-center">
    <FlowNode variant="default">
      Default
    </FlowNode>

    <FlowNode variant="decision">
      Decision
    </FlowNode>

    <FlowNode variant="terminal">
      Terminal
    </FlowNode>

    <FlowNode variant="database">
      Database
    </FlowNode>

    <FlowNode variant="process">
      Process
    </FlowNode>

    <FlowNode variant="io">
      I/O
    </FlowNode>
  </div>
</DiagramPreview>

Highlighted & Dimmed States [#highlighted--dimmed-states]

<DiagramPreview
  title="Interactive states"
  code="`<div className=&#x22;flex flex-wrap gap-4 items-center&#x22;>

With FlowDiagram + nodeTypes [#with-flowdiagram--nodetypes]

<DiagramPreview
  title="CI Pipeline with typed nodes"
  code="`import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react';
import { flowNodeRenderer } from '@diax/ui-react';

<FlowDiagram
nodes={[
  { id: 'start', type: 'terminal', content: 'Start' },
  { id: 'check', type: 'decision', content: 'Tests pass?' },
  { id: 'db', type: 'database', content: 'Save results' },
  { id: 'end', type: 'terminal', content: 'Done' },
]}
relations={['start->check', 'check->|yes|db', 'db->end']}
nodeTypes={{
  terminal: flowNodeRenderer('terminal'),
  decision: flowNodeRenderer('decision'),
  database: flowNodeRenderer('database'),
}}
density=&#x22;spacious&#x22;
centered
/>`"
>
  <FlowDiagram
    nodes="[
    { id: 'start', type: 'terminal', content: 'Start' },
    { id: 'check', type: 'decision', content: 'Tests pass?' },
    { id: 'db', type: 'database', content: 'Save results' },
    { id: 'end', type: 'terminal', content: 'Done' },
  ]"
    relations="['start->check', 'check->|yes|db', 'db->end']"
    density="spacious"
  />
</DiagramPreview>

Props [#props]

| Prop          | Type          | Default     | Description                 |
| ------------- | ------------- | ----------- | --------------------------- |
| `variant`     | `FlowVariant` | `"default"` | Shape variant               |
| `highlighted` | `boolean`     | `false`     | Accent ring + scale         |
| `dimmed`      | `boolean`     | `false`     | Reduced opacity             |
| `className`   | `string`      | —           | Additional Tailwind classes |


# UI Primitives (/docs/ui-react)



Overview [#overview]

`@diax/ui-react` provides composable DOM presentation primitives for recurring visual roles such as
processes, decisions, entities, states and hierarchical ideas. The family names below are a useful
vocabulary, not a closed renderer or a promise to mirror every Mermaid chart type one for one.

Each primitive follows a composable DOM pattern and is compatible with DiaX CSS variables. Use the
pieces inside Diagram or Connect, or independently in ordinary application UI. The package ships a
self-contained stylesheet; Tailwind remains an application choice rather than a peer requirement.

Standalone `@diax/ui-react/presentation` consumers install only `@diax/ui-react` (plus the required
React peer). Add the React adapter and Core only when the application also renders Diagram or
Connect:

<InstallTabs packages="['@diax/ui-react', '@diax/react']" description="DOM presets plus the React diagram runtime" />

Add `@diax/mermaid` only when importing Mermaid source through `@diax/ui-react/mermaid`:

<InstallTabs packages="['@diax/mermaid']" description="Optional Mermaid parser" />

Import the preset stylesheet once in your application entry:

```css title="app.css"
@import '@diax/ui-react/styles.css';
```

The stylesheet uses low-specificity selectors and DiaX CSS variables, so application styles and
`className` overrides remain in control. Tailwind is optional for npm consumers.

Quick Start: style Diagram data [#quick-start-style-diagram-data]

Keep topology as data and allowlist the presentation for each node type:

```tsx contract
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react';
import { flowNodeRenderer } from '@diax/ui-react';

export function ReleaseDecision() {
  return (
    <FlowDiagram
      nodes={[
        { id: 'build', type: 'process', content: 'Build' },
        { id: 'tests', type: 'decision', content: 'Tests pass?' },
        { id: 'deploy', type: 'terminal', content: 'Deploy' },
      ]}
      relations={['build->tests', 'tests->deploy']}
      nodeTypes={{
        process: flowNodeRenderer('process'),
        decision: flowNodeRenderer('decision'),
        terminal: flowNodeRenderer('terminal'),
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

The root entry contains only DOM primitives and renderer adapters. It does not parse Mermaid.

When to use primitives [#when-to-use-primitives]

Use a primitive when the same semantic card or visual role has appeared in at least 2 real diagrams
and should share structure, accessibility and theme tokens. Keep one-off report composition in your
application's JSX and design system. This package should reduce repeated presentation work without
turning every Mermaid grammar family into a permanent React component hierarchy.

DiaX-owned examples follow the [Visual Constitution](/docs/guide/visual-constitution): semantic roles
may share structure, but the host owns visual identity and different communication jobs should not
collapse into one rounded-card skin.

For promotion reviews, architecture briefs and AI-generated visual explanations, start with the
[Presentation Recipes](/docs/ui-react/presentation-recipes). They combine semantic HTML, metrics and
Connect without turning report-specific cards into permanent package exports.

For relational schemas, record lifecycles, migration history and performance evidence, use the
[Data Model Recipes](/docs/ui-react/data-model-recipes). They demonstrate how the root shape entry,
the isolated Presentation entry and opt-in Connect compose without a `schema` mode.

For outcome evidence, decision scopes, reversible source changes and adoption policy, use the
[Product Brief Recipes](/docs/ui-react/product-brief-recipes). They deliberately load only the
Presentation entry and native HTML—no graph, Mermaid or chart runtime.

Optional: render supported Mermaid [#optional-render-supported-mermaid]

Add `@diax/mermaid` and use the separate composition entry only when Mermaid text is your input:

```tsx
import { SmartMermaidDiagram } from '@diax/ui-react/mermaid';

<SmartMermaidDiagram chart={`
  classDiagram
  class Animal
  class Dog
  Animal <|-- Dog
`} />
```

`SmartMermaidDiagram` detects the supported family and applies its matching DOM renderers.
Unsupported Mermaid families are reported rather than silently approximated.

Available Components [#available-components]

| Component                                                           | Diagram Type             | Key Features                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`DiagramFrame`, semantic nodes](/docs/ui-react/presentation-nodes) | Reports and architecture | Actors, systems, artifacts, metrics, stages, evidence, decisions, risk, stores and custom roles |
| [`FlowNode`](/docs/ui-react/flowchart)                              | Flowchart                | 6 shape variants (default, decision, terminal, database, process, io)                           |
| [`ClassNode`](/docs/ui-react/class-diagram)                         | UML Class                | Three-section compound (header, attributes, methods)                                            |
| [`EntityNode`](/docs/ui-react/er-diagram)                           | ER Diagram               | Table-style with PK/FK/UK constraint badges                                                     |
| [`StateNode`](/docs/ui-react/state-diagram)                         | State Machine            | Three variants (default, initial dot, final double circle)                                      |
| [`RequirementNode`](/docs/ui-react/requirement-diagram)             | Requirements             | Type badge + priority indicator                                                                 |
| [`MindmapNode`](/docs/ui-react/mindmap)                             | Mindmap                  | Depth-aware auto styling with color cycling                                                     |

Choosing a Diagram Type [#choosing-a-diagram-type]

Not sure which component to use? Here's a quick guide:

| Need to show\...                               | Use                                                       | Example                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| A report, architecture brief or evidence chain | [`Presentation Nodes`](/docs/ui-react/presentation-nodes) | Promotion review, incident response, AI explanation |
| Processes, workflows, pipelines                | [`FlowNode`](/docs/ui-react/flowchart)                    | CI/CD pipelines, user flows, decision trees         |
| Class hierarchies, interfaces                  | [`ClassNode`](/docs/ui-react/class-diagram)               | UML class diagrams, API schemas                     |
| Database schemas, relationships                | [`EntityNode`](/docs/ui-react/er-diagram)                 | ER diagrams, data models                            |
| State machines, transitions                    | [`StateNode`](/docs/ui-react/state-diagram)               | Auth flows, lifecycle states                        |
| Requirements traceability                      | [`RequirementNode`](/docs/ui-react/requirement-diagram)   | Spec documents, compliance                          |
| Hierarchical/radial ideas                      | [`MindmapNode`](/docs/ui-react/mindmap)                   | Brainstorming, topic trees                          |
| **Mixed / Unknown**                            | [`SmartMermaidDiagram`](/docs/ui-react/smart-mermaid)     | Auto-detects from Mermaid syntax                    |

Usage Patterns [#usage-patterns]

1\. nodeTypes registry (recommended for application data) [#1-nodetypes-registry-recommended-for-application-data]

Use individual renderer adapters with `FlowDiagram`:

```tsx
import { flowNodeRenderer, classNodeRenderer } from '@diax/ui-react';

<FlowDiagram
  nodeTypes={{
    decision: flowNodeRenderer("decision"),
    class: classNodeRenderer,
  }}
  nodes={nodes}
  relations={relations}
/>
```

2\. Direct compound components [#2-direct-compound-components]

Compose one semantic node without adopting a diagram renderer:

```tsx
import { ClassNode, ClassHeader, ClassAttributes } from '@diax/ui-react';

<ClassNode>
  <ClassHeader stereotype="interface">Serializable</ClassHeader>
  <ClassAttributes items={["+serialize(): string"]} />
</ClassNode>
```

3\. SmartMermaidDiagram [#3-smartmermaiddiagram]

Detect and render a supported Mermaid family:

```tsx
import { SmartMermaidDiagram } from '@diax/ui-react/mermaid';

<SmartMermaidDiagram chart={mermaidText} theme="light" />
```

4\. Family-specific Mermaid composition [#4-family-specific-mermaid-composition]

When the family is already known:

```tsx
import { ClassDiagram, ERDiagram } from '@diax/ui-react/mermaid';

<ClassDiagram chart={classMermaid} />
<ERDiagram chart={erMermaid} />
```

Theme Integration [#theme-integration]

All components respect DiaX CSS variables set by the `theme` prop:

```tsx
<SmartMermaidDiagram chart={chart} theme="notion" />
```

Override individual variables:

```css
.my-diagram {
  --diax-node-bg: #1a1a2e;
  --diax-accent: #e94560;
  --diax-node-text: #eee;
}
```


# MindmapNode (/docs/ui-react/mindmap)





Overview [#overview]

`MindmapNode` renders depth-aware mindmap nodes. Colors cycle through a built-in
palette based on `depth`, and font/padding sizes decrease at deeper levels.

Depth Levels [#depth-levels]

<DiagramPreview
  title="MindmapNode — depth levels"
  code="`import { MindmapNode } from '@diax/ui-react';

<div className=&#x22;flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4&#x22;>
<MindmapNode depth={0}>Root Topic</MindmapNode>
<MindmapNode depth={1}>Branch A</MindmapNode>
<MindmapNode depth={2}>Sub-topic</MindmapNode>
<MindmapNode depth={3}>Deep Leaf</MindmapNode>
<MindmapNode depth={4}>Deeper Leaf</MindmapNode>
</div>`"
>
  <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
    <MindmapNode depth="0">
      Root Topic
    </MindmapNode>

    <MindmapNode depth="1">
      Branch A
    </MindmapNode>

    <MindmapNode depth="2">
      Sub-topic
    </MindmapNode>

    <MindmapNode depth="3">
      Deep Leaf
    </MindmapNode>

    <MindmapNode depth="4">
      Deeper Leaf
    </MindmapNode>
  </div>
</DiagramPreview>

Color Cycling [#color-cycling]

The depth palette cycles through 6 colors: violet → amber → emerald → sky → rose → orange.
After depth 5 the cycle repeats.

Sizing [#sizing]

| Depth | Font                      | Padding       | Border Radius |
| ----- | ------------------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| 0     | `text-lg font-bold`       | `px-5 py-3`   | `rounded-xl`  |
| 1     | `text-base font-semibold` | `px-4 py-2`   | `rounded-lg`  |
| 2+    | `text-sm`                 | `px-3 py-1.5` | `rounded-md`  |

Props [#props]

| Prop       | Type        | Default | Description                            |
| ---------- | ----------- | ------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `depth`    | `number`    | `0`     | Nesting depth, controls color + sizing |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | —       | Node label content                     |


# Presentation Nodes (/docs/ui-react/presentation-nodes)





Choose by meaning, not shape [#choose-by-meaning-not-shape]

Presentation nodes give AI agents and people a small, recognizable vocabulary for the visual roles
that recur in architecture briefs, incident reviews, promotion decks, roadmaps and technical blogs.
They are real DOM, so their content can contain icons, localized text, links and application-owned
controls. DiaX still owns only topology, measurement and connectors.

<DiagramPreview title="Presentation primitive catalog" description="Nine semantic roles plus one escape hatch, loaded from the isolated presentation entry" code="presentationPrimitivesCode">
  <PresentationPrimitivesPreview />
</DiagramPreview>

The narrow color rail is a scanning aid, not the meaning itself. Every built-in status is also
visible as text, forced-colors replaces decoration with system colors, and the DOM reading order is
complete when arrows are hidden.

Install [#install]

<InstallTabs packages="['@diax/ui-react']" description="Standalone presentation primitives (peer dependency: React >= 18)" />

Add `@diax/react` and `diax` only when these DOM components sit inside Diagram or Connect. The
presentation entry itself does not load either runtime.

Import the self-contained stylesheet once. Tailwind is not required by the package:

```css title="app.css"
@import '@diax/ui-react/styles.css';
```

Preset selectors live in the CSS `components` cascade layer and use `:where()`. Unlayered
application CSS and utility layers can therefore override widths, spacing and surfaces without
`!important`. The package does not inspect a `.dark` class or require a theme provider; map its
tokens from the theme boundary your application already owns.

Component selector [#component-selector]

| What the reader needs to recognize            | Component       | Typical examples                                 |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| A complete exportable visual                  | `DiagramFrame`  | Blog figure, report card, slide-ready diagram    |
| A person, team or external participant        | `ActorNode`     | Customer, approver, owning team                  |
| An owned technical responsibility             | `SystemNode`    | Service, app, module, platform, tool             |
| A quantitative result                         | `MetricNode`    | Coverage, duration, cost, conversion             |
| A phase with progress                         | `StageNode`     | Migration, rollout, roadmap, SOP                 |
| A reproducible observation                    | `EvidenceNode`  | Test result, trace, citation, benchmark          |
| A concrete output with engineering provenance | `ArtifactNode`  | Build bundle, package, image, generated snapshot |
| A reviewable decision record                  | `DecisionNode`  | Technical selection, approval, recommendation    |
| A constraint that needs action                | `RiskNode`      | Security risk, dependency, blocker               |
| Durable state or an exchange boundary         | `DataStoreNode` | Database, queue, registry, artifact store        |
| A product-specific visual role                | `NodeCard`      | Policy, domain event, custom application term    |

Do not choose a component because it has the color or silhouette you want. Choose the role first,
then set `tone` or application CSS. A database that is merely one step in a simple Mermaid-style
flow can still use `FlowNode variant="database"`; use `DataStoreNode` when schema, durability or
ownership is part of the explanation.

DiagramFrame and DiagramLegend [#diagramframe-and-diagramlegend]

`DiagramFrame` renders a named `<figure>` with a header, body and optional `<figcaption>`. It is the
outer presentation surface; it does not create a graph, coordinate system or nested layout model.

```tsx contract
import { DiagramFrame, DiagramLegend, NodeBadge } from '@diax/ui-react/presentation';

export function ReleaseFigure() {
  return (
    <DiagramFrame
      eyebrow="Release candidate"
      title="Evidence before confidence"
      description="What must be true before publishing."
      actions={<NodeBadge tone="accent">Alpha</NodeBadge>}
      caption="Generated from the locked release candidate."
    >
      <DiagramLegend
        items={[
          { label: 'Verified', description: 'Reproducible contract', tone: 'success' },
          { label: 'Risk', description: 'Owner action required', tone: 'danger' },
        ]}
      />
    </DiagramFrame>
  );
}
```

| Prop              | Type        | Purpose                                                       |
| ----------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`           | `ReactNode` | Required accessible figure name                               |
| `eyebrow`         | `ReactNode` | Short category such as “Architecture” or “Release candidate”  |
| `description`     | `ReactNode` | What the visual is meant to explain                           |
| `icon`, `actions` | `ReactNode` | Optional application-owned affordances                        |
| `caption`         | `ReactNode` | Provenance, caveat or export context rendered as `figcaption` |
| `tone`            | `NodeTone`  | Semantic signal rail; defaults to `accent`                    |

NodeCard and NodeBadge [#nodecard-and-nodebadge]

`NodeCard` is the escape hatch for a real application role that does not deserve another package
export. It owns accessible naming, a stable measurement box, highlight/dim state and theme tokens.
It does not accept relations, position or layout options.

```tsx contract
import { NodeBadge, NodeCard } from '@diax/ui-react/presentation';

export function PolicyNode() {
  return (
    <NodeCard
      eyebrow="Policy"
      title="Two reviewers required"
      description="A product-specific role stays on the shared surface."
      badge={<NodeBadge tone="warning">Enforced</NodeBadge>}
    />
  );
}
```

Shared presentation props are deliberately small:

| Prop          | Values                                                      | Meaning                                         |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `tone`        | `neutral`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | Semantic emphasis, never the only status signal |
| `size`        | `compact`, `default`, `wide`                                | Measurement-friendly width budget               |
| `highlighted` | `boolean`                                                   | Current relation or search focus                |
| `dimmed`      | `boolean`                                                   | De-emphasized context                           |
| `className`   | `string`                                                    | Application layout and deliberate overrides     |

All node components also accept native `<article>` attributes. `DiagramFrame`, `DiagramLegend` and
`NodeBadge` accept native `<figure>`, `<ul>` and `<span>` attributes respectively, so test IDs,
language metadata and product-specific `aria-*` attributes do not require wrapper elements.

Role component API [#role-component-api]

| Component       | Required props      | Role-specific props                                                            | Defaults              |
| --------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| `ActorNode`     | `name`              | `roleLabel`, `avatar`, `status`, `statusLabel`                                 | neutral, no status    |
| `SystemNode`    | `name`              | `kind`, `status`, `statusLabel`, `tags`                                        | info                  |
| `MetricNode`    | `label`, `value`    | `delta`, `trend`, `context`                                                    | flat trend            |
| `StageNode`     | `title`             | `step`, `status`, `statusLabel`, `owner`                                       | upcoming              |
| `EvidenceNode`  | `title`             | `source`, `strength`, `strengthLabel`                                          | medium evidence       |
| `ArtifactNode`  | `name`              | `kind`, `version`, `source`, `status`, localized labels                        | info, no status       |
| `DecisionNode`  | `title`             | `outcome`, `criteria`, `rationale`, `status`, `statusLabel`, `owner`, `labels` | accent, no status     |
| `RiskNode`      | `title`, `severity` | `severityLabel`, `mitigation`                                                  | severity-derived tone |
| `DataStoreNode` | `name`              | `engine`, `entries`                                                            | accent                |

Every wrapper also accepts the shared `description`, `icon`, `size`, `tone`, `highlighted` and
`dimmed` props unless that field is replaced by a more precise role prop. Status labels remain
visible text; do not replace them with color-only dots or title tooltips.

Architecture roles [#architecture-roles]

Use role-specific names when an AI agent or a new teammate should understand the intent without
reading the styling implementation.

```tsx contract
import { ActorNode, ArtifactNode, DataStoreNode, SystemNode } from '@diax/ui-react/presentation';

export function ArchitectureRoles() {
  return (
    <div>
      <ActorNode
        name="Platform team"
        roleLabel="Release owner"
        status="active"
        statusLabel="Reviewing"
      />
      <SystemNode
        name="Artifact registry"
        kind="Owned service"
        status="healthy"
        tags={['provenance', 'immutable']}
      />
      <ArtifactNode
        name="frontend-dist.zip"
        kind="Deployment bundle"
        version="main@8fbaef0"
        source="install-build #1842"
        status="verified"
        statusLabel="Registry ready"
      />
      <DataStoreNode
        name="Evidence ledger"
        engine="SQLite"
        entries={['runs', 'artifacts', 'attestations']}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

`ActorNode` uses `roleLabel`, not `role`. The latter is a native ARIA attribute; overloading it with
“Approver” or “Customer” would create invalid accessibility semantics.

Engineering artifacts and provenance [#engineering-artifacts-and-provenance]

`ArtifactNode` describes a concrete, passive output that another system produces, stores or
consumes. It is deliberately different from the surrounding architecture roles:

* `SystemNode` is the build service or injection worker that performs work.
* `DataStoreNode` is the registry or durable collection that holds many records or artifacts.
* `EvidenceNode` is an observation used to support a claim.
* `ArtifactNode` is the particular bundle, package, image or generated snapshot moving between them.

```tsx contract
import { ArtifactNode } from '@diax/ui-react/presentation';

export function DeploymentArtifact() {
  return (
    <ArtifactNode
      name="frontend-dist.zip"
      kind="Deployment bundle"
      version="sha256:7a2f…91c4"
      versionLabel="Digest"
      source="install-build #1842 · main@8fbaef0"
      status="published"
      statusLabel="Registry ready"
      description="Immutable files consumed by the injection pipeline."
    />
  );
}
```

The compact manifest uses real `<dl>`, `<dt>` and `<dd>` markup. Version and source stay optional:
do not invent placeholder provenance to fill the component. `status` is limited to `verified` and
`published`; use `statusLabel` for product language and localization. Candidate, deprecated and
retired lifecycle language belongs in application composition until repeated scenarios justify a
shared semantic contract.
Artifact identity does not imply a relation, download action or storage API. Keep producer →
artifact → consumer topology in centralized Diagram relations or authored Connect DOM, and place
interactive actions in application-owned composition rather than hiding them in the card.

Results, evidence and risk [#results-evidence-and-risk]

Metrics use real `<dl>/<dt>/<dd>` markup. Evidence keeps provenance visible. Risk always pairs
severity with text and can keep mitigation beside the problem instead of hiding it in a tooltip.

```tsx contract
import { EvidenceNode, MetricNode, RiskNode } from '@diax/ui-react/presentation';

export function DecisionEvidence() {
  return (
    <div>
      <MetricNode
        label="Contract coverage"
        value="92%"
        delta="+8%"
        trend="up"
        context="since Alpha 3"
      />
      <EvidenceNode
        title="Browser matrix passed"
        description="Chromium, Firefox and WebKit"
        strength="high"
        strengthLabel="Verified"
        source="CI run #1842"
        sourceLabel="Verified by"
      />
      <RiskNode
        title="Unsigned package"
        severity="critical"
        severityLabel="Blocks release"
        mitigation="Require npm provenance before promotion."
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

`trend="up"` is visually positive by default, but product meaning may differ: an increasing error
rate is bad. Set `tone="danger"` explicitly when the domain interpretation differs from the numeric
direction.

Decision records, not branching gateways [#decision-records-not-branching-gateways]

`DecisionNode` captures a reviewable choice: its outcome, criteria, rationale, status and owner stay
understandable when arrows are hidden. It deliberately has no `options`, `branches` or `relations`
props. Put branch semantics in centralized relations and visible edge labels.

```tsx contract
import { DecisionNode } from '@diax/ui-react/presentation';

export function RenderingDecision() {
  return (
    <DecisionNode
      title="Choose the rendering owner"
      outcome="DOM + CSS for content; DiaX for measured relations"
      status="approved"
      statusLabel="Accepted"
      criteria={['Reproducible output', 'Native rich content', 'AI-familiar authoring']}
      rationale="Keep content in the platform with the strongest composition primitives."
      owner="Owner · Architecture"
    />
  );
}
```

This differs from `FlowNode variant="decision"`, which is a compact flowchart shape for a branching
question such as “Cache hit?”. The shape belongs in a process graph; the record belongs in a report,
architecture brief or decision trail. AI prompts should name the intended role instead of asking for
a generic “decision box”. The `labels` prop can localize the visible Outcome, Criteria and Rationale
headings without replacing the component structure.

Workflow stages [#workflow-stages]

`StageNode` covers ordered SOPs, migrations, roadmaps and phased rollouts. `step` is display content,
not a layout coordinate; the relations or authored DOM still define order.

```tsx contract
import { StageNode } from '@diax/ui-react/presentation';

export function RolloutStage() {
  return (
    <StageNode
      step="03 / 04"
      title="Canary rollout"
      status="active"
      statusLabel="In progress"
      owner="Owner · Platform"
      description="Promote only after installed-consumer verification."
    />
  );
}
```

Put components inside Diagram data [#put-components-inside-diagram-data]

Rich DOM is ordinary node content. Keep topology centralized instead of wrapping every node in
another JSX definition element:

```tsx contract
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react';
import { ActorNode, EvidenceNode, SystemNode } from '@diax/ui-react/presentation';

export function ReleaseChain() {
  const nodes = [
    { id: 'owner', content: <ActorNode name="Owner" roleLabel="Approver" /> },
    { id: 'registry', content: <SystemNode name="Registry" kind="Service" /> },
    { id: 'evidence', content: <EvidenceNode title="Provenance verified" source="npm" /> },
  ];

  return (
    <FlowDiagram
      nodes={nodes}
      relations={['owner->registry', 'registry->evidence']}
    />
  );
}
```

The same components can be placed in authored Grid/Flex DOM and measured with
`@diax/react/connect`. They do not inspect whether Diagram, Connect or ordinary HTML owns layout.

Theme tokens [#theme-tokens]

Importing the stylesheet gives useful defaults without taking away application ownership. Override
tokens on a page, figure or individual node; no React provider is required.

| Token                                                      | Controls                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `--diax-node-bg`, `--diax-node-text`, `--diax-node-border` | Shared surface colors                          |
| `--diax-node-shadow`                                       | Node elevation; set to `none` in flat products |
| `--diax-accent`                                            | Default accent rail and highlighted state      |
| `--diax-ui-info`, `--diax-ui-success`                      | Informational and verified states              |
| `--diax-ui-warning`, `--diax-ui-danger`                    | Attention and blocking states                  |
| `--diax-ui-radius`, `--diax-frame-radius`                  | Node and export frame corners                  |
| `--diax-ui-font`, `--diax-ui-data-font`                    | UI copy and numeric/code typography            |
| `--diax-frame-bg`, `--diax-frame-shadow`                   | Complete figure surface                        |

```css
.release-evidence {
  --diax-accent: oklch(0.62 0.17 265);
  --diax-ui-radius: 0.5rem;
  --diax-node-shadow: none;
}

.dark .release-evidence {
  --diax-node-bg: #1f2024;
  --diax-node-text: #f5f5f6;
  --diax-node-border: rgb(245 245 246 / 18%);
  --diax-frame-bg: #151619;
  --diax-accent: #a5adff;
}
```

The package stylesheet includes narrow-container, reduced-motion, forced-colors and print rules.
Print rules deliberately reset frame, node and badge surfaces to white paper with dark text even
when the host is dark. Application CSS still owns page size, recipe layout and interactive edge
controls because a 16:9 slide, article column and A4 export have different wrapping constraints.

AI authoring vocabulary [#ai-authoring-vocabulary]

Give an agent semantic roles rather than a request for “beautiful cards”:

```text
Use ActorNode for people or teams, SystemNode for owned technical responsibilities,
ArtifactNode for concrete outputs with version and producer provenance, DataStoreNode for durable
collections, StageNode for ordered work, MetricNode for quantities, EvidenceNode for reproducible
observations, DecisionNode for reviewable choices, and RiskNode for constraints requiring action.

Use NodeCard only when none of those roles match. Keep relations in one nodes + relations
definition. Do not invent a new component name, layout mode, coordinates or SVG shape.
Every status must include visible text. Every evidence node must name its source.
```

For untrusted model output, keep generating schema-validated data and map allowlisted types to these
trusted components. Do not compile model-produced JSX at runtime.

Why these components graduated [#why-these-components-graduated]

The promotion-review corpus contains dozens of independent visuals. The same step badge alone was
reimplemented in nine chart modules; report frames, stages, system roles, stores, risks, outcomes
and evidence language recur across architecture, security, i18n and rollout stories. These
components now pass the deletion test: removing them would push naming, accessible status,
forced-colors behavior, theme tokens and measurement-safe structure back into many callers. The
artifact role separately recurs in an artifact archive/reuse workflow and a dist injection pipeline;
removing it would again conflate a passive build output with the system or store around it.

The complete report compositions still stay application-owned. A “mobile migration comparison” or
“supply-chain response” component would encode one document's wording and layout, not a reusable
visual role.


# Presentation Recipes (/docs/ui-react/presentation-recipes)





Keep presentation in JSX [#keep-presentation-in-jsx]

Promotion reviews, architecture briefs, blog figures and AI-generated explanations rarely consist of
one graph. They combine claims, metrics, code, evidence, decisions and a few relationships. Keep that
composition as semantic HTML and CSS; use Connect only for the relations that materially improve the
story.

<Callout type="info">
  These complete compositions remain copy-owned recipes. Their recurring inner roles can now use
  [`@diax/ui-react/presentation` Presentation Nodes](/docs/ui-react/presentation-nodes), while report-specific
  wording, grids and system boundaries stay in your application.
</Callout>

<DiagramPreview title="Evidence ledger" description="A responsive claim → evidence → decision composition over real DOM" code="presentationRecipeCode">
  <PresentationRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

The signature is not a generic dashboard card. It is an evidence ledger: every visual block has one
role, visible provenance language and a reviewable relationship to the next decision. The authored
DOM still controls the reading order when edges are absent, loading or suppressed by print tooling.

System boundary brief [#system-boundary-brief]

Architecture explanations have a different job: show where ownership changes without flattening
every layer, actor and panel into one graph model.

<DiagramPreview title="System boundary brief" description="External input → owned control plane → durable evidence" code="systemBoundaryRecipeCode">
  <SystemBoundaryRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

The green enclosure is an ordinary semantic `<section>`, not a DiaX Group. Its heading, rail,
internal grid and responsive behavior belong to authored HTML/CSS. Only the four cards that act as
relation endpoints use `connectionTarget()`. This keeps “system boundary” in the application's
domain vocabulary without adding a second containment or layout model to Connect.

For an AI author, state that distinction explicitly:

```text
Create a React architecture brief with one external actor, one owned system boundary,
two internal responsibilities and one evidence sink.

Layout owner: authored JSX/CSS. The system boundary is a semantic section, not a graph node.
Connect only these exact targets: deploy job → artifact intake → promotion decision → ledger.
Keep relation labels short, preserve that DOM reading order at 320 px, and make ownership
understandable when all arrows are hidden.
```

Timeline: chronology is an ordered list [#timeline-chronology-is-an-ordered-list]

<DiagramPreview title="Rollout timeline" description="An ordered narrative composed from StageNode, without a timeline mode" code="timelineRecipeCode">
  <TimelineRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

Use an `<ol>` when the reader must understand order even if CSS, color or connectors disappear.
`StageNode` owns each phase's visible status and owner; the list owns chronology. Dates, milestones,
duration scales and dependency graphs vary too much across roadmaps, migrations and incident reviews
to justify a public `Timeline` component today.

Comparison: preserve the two-dimensional question [#comparison-preserve-the-two-dimensional-question]

<DiagramPreview title="Rendering strategy comparison" description="A native comparison table followed by a reviewable DecisionNode" code="comparisonRecipeCode">
  <ComparisonRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

Comparisons are not graphs by default. Use `<table>`, column and row scopes, a caption, and a focused
internal scroll region on narrow screens. Highlighting a recommended column is useful decoration;
the visible “Recommended” text and following `DecisionNode` carry the conclusion. Before/after stories
with only two narrative panels may use two articles instead, but should not pretend to be a matrix.

Swimlane: authored ownership, measured handoffs [#swimlane-authored-ownership-measured-handoffs]

<DiagramPreview title="Incident response swimlane" description="Named team sections with Connect measuring only cross-lane handoffs" code="swimlaneRecipeCode">
  <SwimlaneRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

A lane is a responsibility boundary, not another DiaX topology object. Keep it as a named `<section>`
and place real DOM tasks inside it. Connect the few handoffs that help the reader follow the response.
At narrow widths the sections stack in source order, preserving Security → Platform → Release without
requiring mobile coordinates or alternate relations.

These recipes also expose three different design decisions that a generic component would hide:

| Recipe     | Native structure             | What DiaX owns                                    |
| ---------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Timeline   | `<ol>`                       | Nothing unless cross-stage dependencies add value |
| Comparison | `<table>` + decision article | Nothing; this is document semantics               |
| Swimlane   | Named `<section>` lanes      | Target measurement and handoff connectors         |

Why these stay recipes [#why-these-stay-recipes]

| Concern                               | Owner                 | Reason                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claim, metric and decision wording    | Application           | Product language differs across reports                        |
| Grid, typography and responsive order | Application CSS       | Presentation hierarchy is the authored content                 |
| Trust or system boundary enclosure    | Application DOM/CSS   | Ownership vocabulary and nesting differ across products        |
| Target measurement and edge lifecycle | `@diax/react/connect` | Repeated browser complexity belongs behind a deep interface    |
| Relation validation and diagnostics   | DiaX                  | Topology should remain reviewable by people, TypeScript and AI |
| Export, page size and brand fonts     | Report workflow       | These policies are not graph semantics                         |

Deleting the application-owned composition removes its report-specific hierarchy. Deleting Connect
would push DOM measurement, observers, anchors, SVG layers and cleanup into every report. The
recurring metric, evidence, risk, actor, stage, system and store roles have graduated into
Presentation Nodes; the evidence-ledger and system-boundary compositions deliberately have not.

Semantic structure first [#semantic-structure-first]

Use native elements before styling hooks:

* `<figure>` and `<figcaption>` describe one exportable visual;
* `<article>` owns a claim that can stand alone;
* `<dl>`, `<dt>` and `<dd>` preserve metric name/value semantics;
* `<aside>` contains the resulting recommendation or constraint;
* `<section aria-labelledby>` gives an authored system boundary a durable accessible name;
* `connectionTarget()` marks the exact existing element DiaX should measure.

Do not turn every caption, badge or metric into a graph node. A target is a measured endpoint, not a
new content taxonomy.

Vendor identity decorates a semantic role [#vendor-identity-decorates-a-semantic-role]

A provider logo answers &#x2A;*whose product is this?** It does not answer &#x2A;*what does this node do?**
Choose `ActorNode`, `SystemNode`, `ArtifactNode` or another semantic role first. Use `NodeCard` only
when the application has a real role that does not match one of those components; then add an
application-owned mark through `icon`. A person's or team's approved portrait can use
`ActorNode.avatar` under the same policy.

The visible title remains the accessible identity. Treat a familiar mark as decoration, hide it from
the accessibility tree, and never make a reader infer “GitHub”, “AWS” or another vendor from color or
shape alone. The application—not DiaX—owns the icon import, allowlist, source, license/trademark
review and bundle cost.

```tsx contract
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/react';
import { NodeCard, SystemNode } from '@diax/ui-react/presentation';

function RepositoryMark() {
  return (
    <svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="20" height="20">
      <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9" fill="currentColor" />
    </svg>
  );
}

const providerAllowlist = {
  sourceHost: {
    label: 'Approved source host',
    icon: <RepositoryMark />,
  },
} as const;

export function ProviderTopology() {
  return (
    <FlowDiagram
      nodes={[
        { id: 'repo', type: 'provider', content: 'sourceHost' },
        { id: 'build', type: 'system', content: 'Build service' },
      ]}
      relations={[{ from: 'repo', to: 'build', label: 'verified source' }]}
      nodeTypes={{
        provider: (node, state) => {
          const key = typeof node.content === 'string' ? node.content : '';
          const provider = key === 'sourceHost' ? providerAllowlist.sourceHost : undefined;
          return (
            <NodeCard
              eyebrow="Source provider"
              title={provider?.label ?? 'External source'}
              description={provider ? 'Approved application asset' : 'Vendor identity not verified'}
              icon={provider?.icon}
              highlighted={state === 'highlighted'}
              dimmed={state === 'dimmed'}
            />
          );
        },
        system: (node, state) => (
          <SystemNode
            name={node.content}
            kind="Owned responsibility"
            highlighted={state === 'highlighted'}
            dimmed={state === 'dimmed'}
          />
        ),
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

The generated definition selects only the allowlisted `sourceHost` ID. It cannot provide an import,
SVG payload or logo URL. When the ID is absent or unknown, the renderer keeps the semantic fallback
and omits the mark; it does not search the network or guess a visually similar vendor.

Do not add `brand` to the shared graph schema. Vendor identity is optional presentation metadata in
trusted application code. Topology, role, visible name and provenance must remain meaningful when
every logo is removed.

Responsive and print contract [#responsive-and-print-contract]

Use auto anchors when the same authored surface changes from columns to rows. Fixed left/right
anchors encode desktop geometry and usually become wrong at narrow widths. Budget the connector
track from the largest expected label. These recipes keep 48px between stacked cards and 80–96px
between columns, leaving at least 8px around their current labels.

The Tailwind 4 examples use `@container` and `@min-[44rem]` utilities. The equivalent plain CSS
keeps each recipe's authored grid explicit:

```css
:is(.visual-frame, .architecture-frame) {
  container-type: inline-size;
  break-inside: avoid;
}

:is(.visual-frame__story, .architecture-story) {
  display: grid;
  gap: 3rem;
}

@container (width >= 44rem) {
  .visual-frame__story {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr));
    column-gap: 6rem;
  }

  .architecture-story {
    grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 0.72fr) minmax(0, 2fr) minmax(0, 0.82fr);
    column-gap: 5rem;
  }
}

@media print {
  :is(.visual-frame, .architecture-frame) {
    color: #111;
    background: #fff;
    box-shadow: none;
  }

  :is(.visual-frame, .architecture-frame) :is(.diax-edge-hitbox, [data-diax-edge-action]) {
    display: none;
  }
}
```

`@diax/ui-react/styles.css` already resets `DiagramFrame`, presentation nodes and badges to a
high-contrast paper palette. The recipe still owns page size, authored tables and whether interactive
Connect hit areas or application actions belong in the exported artifact. Browser automation checks
computed print styles and overflow. A selected product-brief corpus additionally generates four
bounded A4 pages, but it still cannot prove installed brand fonts or a physical print.

Test at the actual destination ratio. A 16:9 presentation, an article column and an A4/PDF page have
different line lengths and failure modes; `aspect-ratio` is a recipe constraint, not a Core option.

AI authoring contract [#ai-authoring-contract]

Give an agent roles and invariants rather than asking for “a beautiful chart”:

```text
Create a semantic React figure for a release decision.

Layout owner: authored JSX/CSS; use @diax/react/connect only for relations.
Reading order: claim, observed evidence, decision.
Evidence: render metrics with dl/dt/dd and include units in visible text.
Relations: centralized object-form definitions with stable local IDs.
Constraints: no absolute node coordinates, no generated SVG, no arbitrary HTML,
responsive at 320 px, printable without color, and meaningful when edges are hidden.
```

For untrusted runtime generation, do not compile model-produced JSX. Generate a schema-validated
Diagram Definition and map allowlisted node types to trusted renderers instead. See
[AI & Agents](/docs/guide/ai-integration).

When a recipe graduates into UI React [#when-a-recipe-graduates-into-ui-react]

A presentation role may become a public primitive only after it:

1. appears in at least two distinct real diagram families;
2. hides repeated accessibility, theme or interaction behavior—not only class names;
3. remains useful inside Diagram, Connect and ordinary DOM;
4. has forced-colors, keyboard, responsive and visual contracts;
5. does not introduce a second topology or layout model.

Until then, copy-owned JSX gives teams and AI agents more expressive freedom with less compatibility
surface.

The first graduation happened after the promotion-review corpus showed repeated implementations
across architecture, security, i18n and rollout diagrams. See
[Presentation Nodes](/docs/ui-react/presentation-nodes) for the resulting small interface and the
roles that remain application-owned.

Continue with [Data Model Recipes](/docs/ui-react/data-model-recipes) for relational entities,
record states, schema evolution and query-budget evidence derived from a real SQLite design.

Continue with [Product Brief Recipes](/docs/ui-react/product-brief-recipes) for outcome ledgers,
capability scopes, reversible code evidence and friction-removal policy that do not require a graph
runtime at all.

Continue with [Export DOM Visuals](/docs/guide/exporting) when the composed DOM needs to become PNG,
`foreignObject` SVG or a paginated print artifact.


# Product Brief Recipes (/docs/ui-react/product-brief-recipes)





Visual explanations are not card collections [#visual-explanations-are-not-card-collections]

Product reviews, engineering promotion material and AI-generated briefs often need metrics, scope,
code evidence and adoption policy on the same page. That does not make them four graph types—and it
does not make them a dashboard of interchangeable rounded cards.

This recipe family uses four deliberately different structures:

| Reader question                          | Native structure                 | Reused UI primitive            |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Did the work change the cost curve?      | outcome ledger table             | `MetricNode`, `DiagramFrame`   |
| Which decision scope am I looking at?    | ordered scope lenses             | `NodeBadge`, `DiagramFrame`    |
| Can the change be reversed?              | selectable diff + invariant list | `EvidenceNode`, `DiagramFrame` |
| Which user work did the platform absorb? | ordered friction register        | `NodeBadge`, `DecisionNode`    |

<Callout type="info">
  These compositions were generalized from real engineering-review visuals. The source material is
  evidence, not an interface specification: none of these recipes adds a product-brief mode, graph
  node type or runtime dependency.
</Callout>

Art direction: an engineering review folio [#art-direction-an-engineering-review-folio]

The page behaves like a review packet, not a component-store landing page:

* dark ink carries the argument; semantic blue, green, amber and red only annotate decisions;
* tabular numbers, versions and code use monospace; body text stays in the host document face;
* horizontal rules encode comparable rows, ordered scope and evidence boundaries;
* shadows and rounded enclosures are reserved for reusable DiaX nodes, not applied to every group;
* labels name a real unit, state, scope or owner—never a decorative category.

The signature is structural variety. If every section used the same card shell, readers would need
to decode the content before knowing whether it is a metric, hierarchy, diff or operating policy.

Outcome ledger: keep the baseline in frame [#outcome-ledger-keep-the-baseline-in-frame]

<DiagramPreview title="Outcome ledger" description="A baseline, comparable units and sample rows without loading a chart library" code="outcomeLedgerRecipeCode">
  <OutcomeLedgerRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

Use a native table when each row shares the same dimensions. The miniature reduction rail improves
scanning but remains `aria-hidden`; the percentage cell is the actual value. Keeping the unchanged
reference row prevents the visual from implying that every sampled surface improved.

This recipe intentionally does not wrap Recharts, Vega or another quantitative grammar. Use a real
chart library when scale, distribution or interaction matters. Use this ledger when the review task
is exact row-level comparison.

Capability lenses: order the reader's scope [#capability-lenses-order-the-readers-scope]

<DiagramPreview title="Capability lenses" description="Build → project → portfolio questions expressed as an ordered scope model" code="capabilityLensesRecipeCode">
  <CapabilityLensesRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

The numbers are not decorative. L1, L2 and L3 represent a widening decision scope:

1. **Build:** diagnose one run.
2. **Project:** compare repository history.
3. **Portfolio:** prioritize organizational action.

An `<ol>` preserves that progression without arrows or a hierarchy runtime. The content changes
from source findings to trends to governance, so a public `CapabilityMap` would mostly rename native
document structure and freeze one product's vocabulary.

Reversible change record: show the round trip [#reversible-change-record-show-the-round-trip]

<DiagramPreview title="Reversible change record" description="Selectable source diff, rollback invariants and visible test provenance" code="reversibleChangeRecipeCode">
  <ReversibleChangeRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

Before/after screenshots hide the most valuable properties of technical evidence: selection,
copying, search, zoom and screen-reader access. Keep code as `<pre><code>` and use `<del>` / `<ins>`
when the removal and insertion are part of the claim.

The invariant list answers a different question from the diff. The diff shows the mutation; the
ordered list explains the rollback algorithm; `EvidenceNode` names how the round trip was verified.
Combining those jobs into one `BeforeAfter` component would make each of them weaker.

Friction register: make invisible platform work reviewable [#friction-register-make-invisible-platform-work-reviewable]

<DiagramPreview title="Friction removal register" description="Obstacle → platform intervention → remaining user effort, followed by an owner decision" code="frictionRegisterRecipeCode">
  <FrictionRegisterRecipePreview />
</DiagramPreview>

“Zero friction” is not a visual tone. It is an ownership claim that should be auditable row by row:

* name the original work imposed on the user;
* name the automation or governance that absorbed it;
* state the remaining effort in visible text;
* finish with a reviewable adoption contract.

The register uses an ordered list because each intervention stands alone and narrow screens should
stack each record without turning column headings into an inaccessible mobile table. The final
`DecisionNode` records the product promise; it does not connect the rows into a fake workflow.

Loading boundary [#loading-boundary]

All four recipes import only the parser-free Presentation entry:

```tsx contract
import {
  DecisionNode,
  DiagramFrame,
  EvidenceNode,
  MetricNode,
  NodeBadge,
} from '@diax/ui-react/presentation';
```

They do not load `@diax/react`, Connect, Mermaid or a chart runtime. This is intentional: composition
should not pay for relation measurement when the reader's question is tabular, hierarchical or
documentary.

Responsive and accessibility contract [#responsive-and-accessibility-contract]

Each recipe keeps one durable DOM order:

* outcome and code regions scroll internally when content genuinely needs horizontal width;
* capability and friction records reflow in source order at 320 px;
* tables keep captions and row/column scopes;
* focusable scroll regions expose a visible focus boundary;
* colored rails, diff backgrounds and badges repeat their meaning as text;
* forced colors retains borders and textual status without depending on shadows.

Automation can verify reflow, overflow, focus paint and semantic elements. It cannot claim a real
Windows High Contrast session, hardware Safari rendering, projector legibility or a physical print.
The release preflight also places these four figures on four separate A4 PDF pages and rejects
overflow or accidental pagination; see [Export DOM Visuals](/docs/guide/exporting) for the output
contract and viewer limitations.

AI authoring prompt [#ai-authoring-prompt]

Ask an agent to classify the reader's question before selecting a structure:

```text
Create a React engineering-review figure from structured evidence.

If the question compares exact values across the same dimensions, use a native table.
If it widens through named decision scopes, use an ordered list of semantic sections.
If it claims a code transformation is reversible, show selectable before/after code,
rollback invariants and evidence provenance.
If it claims zero-friction adoption, name obstacle, platform intervention and remaining user effort.

Use @diax/ui-react/presentation only for recurring semantic roles.
Do not invent a graph, relations, SVG chart, universal card shell or new public component.
Preserve reading order at 320 px and keep every claim meaningful without color.
```

For runtime-generated, untrusted content, validate the facts before mapping them into these trusted
renderers. Do not execute model-produced JSX.

Graduation decisions [#graduation-decisions]

| Candidate                                    | Decision           | Reason                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `OutcomeChart`                               | Reject             | Exact comparison belongs to table semantics; distributions belong to chart libraries |
| `CapabilityMap`                              | Keep as recipe     | Levels and scope vocabulary remain product-specific                                  |
| `BeforeAfter`                                | Keep as native DOM | Text, code, UI and image comparisons need different semantics                        |
| `OnboardingStrategy`                         | Reject             | Adoption ownership is content, not a reusable visual component                       |
| `MetricNode`, `EvidenceNode`, `DecisionNode` | Reuse              | Their semantics and accessibility repeat across independent reports                  |

The public UI vocabulary stays small while the recipe catalog gets more expressive. That is the
intended asymmetry: deep reusable roles, abundant application-owned visual explanations.


# RequirementNode (/docs/ui-react/requirement-diagram)





Overview [#overview]

`RequirementNode` renders requirement diagram nodes with type classification badges,
priority indicators, and optional risk levels.

All Type Badges [#all-type-badges]

<DiagramPreview
  title="RequirementNode — type badges"
  code="`import { RequirementNode } from '@diax/ui-react';

<div className=&#x22;flex flex-wrap gap-4&#x22;>
<RequirementNode type=&#x22;functional&#x22; reqId=&#x22;REQ-001&#x22; priority=&#x22;high&#x22;>
  User Authentication
</RequirementNode>
<RequirementNode type=&#x22;performance&#x22; reqId=&#x22;REQ-002&#x22; priority=&#x22;medium&#x22;>
  Sub-200ms Response
</RequirementNode>
<RequirementNode type=&#x22;interface&#x22; reqId=&#x22;REQ-003&#x22; priority=&#x22;low&#x22;>
  REST API v2
</RequirementNode>
<RequirementNode type=&#x22;design&#x22; reqId=&#x22;REQ-004&#x22; risk=&#x22;high&#x22;>
  Microservice Split
</RequirementNode>
</div>`"
>
  <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
    <RequirementNode type="functional" reqId="REQ-001" priority="high">
      User Authentication
    </RequirementNode>

    <RequirementNode type="performance" reqId="REQ-002" priority="medium">
      Sub-200ms Response
    </RequirementNode>

    <RequirementNode type="interface" reqId="REQ-003" priority="low">
      REST API v2
    </RequirementNode>

    <RequirementNode type="design" reqId="REQ-004" risk="high">
      Microservice Split
    </RequirementNode>
  </div>

ElementNode [#elementnode]

Type Badges [#type-badges]

| Type          | Color  |
| ------------- | ------ |
| `functional`  | Blue   |
| `performance` | Orange |
| `interface`   | Violet |
| `design`      | Teal   |
| `physical`    | Rose   |

Priority Indicators [#priority-indicators]

| Priority | Indicator |
| -------- | --------- |
| `high`   | Red dot   |
| `medium` | Amber dot |
| `low`    | Green dot |

Props [#props]

RequirementNode [#requirementnode]

| Prop       | Type                          | Description            |
| ---------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `type`     | `RequirementType`             | Category badge         |
| `priority` | `"high" \| "medium" \| "low"` | Priority dot           |
| `risk`     | `"high" \| "medium" \| "low"` | Risk footer            |
| `reqId`    | `string`                      | ID displayed in header |

ElementNode [#elementnode-1]

| Prop          | Type     | Description                                   |
| ------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `elementType` | `string` | Type annotation (e.g., "module", "component") |


# SmartMermaidDiagram (/docs/ui-react/smart-mermaid)





Overview [#overview]

`SmartMermaidDiagram` parses any supported Mermaid syntax, auto-detects the diagram
type, and renders it using the matching preset node components from `@diax/ui-react`.

Supported types: `flowchart`, `classDiagram`, `stateDiagram`, `erDiagram`, `requirement`, `mindmap`.

Flowchart [#flowchart]

<DiagramPreview
  title="Auto-detected flowchart"
  code="`import { SmartMermaidDiagram } from '@diax/ui-react/mermaid';

<SmartMermaidDiagram chart={\`
graph TD
  A[Start] --> B{Decision}
  B -->|Yes| C[Process]
  B -->|No| D[End]
  C --> D
\`} />`"
>
  <SmartMermaidDiagram
    chart="`graph TD
  A[Start] --> B{Decision}
  B -->|Yes| C[Process]
  B -->|No| D[End]
  C --> D`"
  />
</DiagramPreview>

Class Diagram [#class-diagram]

<DiagramPreview
  title="Auto-detected classDiagram"
  code="`import { SmartMermaidDiagram } from '@diax/ui-react/mermaid';

<SmartMermaidDiagram chart={\`
classDiagram
  class Animal {
    +String name
    +int age
    +makeSound()
  }
  class Dog {
    +fetch()
  }
  Animal <|-- Dog
\`} />`"
>
  <SmartMermaidDiagram
    chart="`classDiagram
  class Animal {
    +String name
    +int age
    +makeSound()
  }
  class Dog {
    +fetch()
  }
  Animal <|-- Dog`"
  />
</DiagramPreview>

<SmartMermaidDiagram chart={\`
erDiagram
  CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
  ORDER ||--|{ LINE-ITEM : contains
\`} />`"

Custom nodeTypes Override [#custom-nodetypes-override]

You can override or extend the auto-detected nodeTypes registry:

```tsx
import { SmartMermaidDiagram } from '@diax/ui-react/mermaid';

<SmartMermaidDiagram
  chart={`graph TD
    A[Custom] --> B[Nodes]
  `}
  nodeTypes={{
    default: (node) => (
      <div className="custom-node">{node.content}</div>
    ),
  }}
/>
```

Props [#props]

| Prop         | Type                                     | Default          | Description                                                           |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `chart`      | `string`                                 | —                | Mermaid syntax string (required)                                      |
| `nodeTypes`  | `Record<string, NodeRenderer>`           | —                | Override/extend auto-detected renderers                               |
| `renderNode` | `(node, context) => ReactNode`           | —                | Locally override nodes while retaining `context.defaultNode`          |
| `direction`  | `Direction`                              | `'horizontal'`   | Layout direction                                                      |
| `density`    | `Density`                                | `'comfortable'`  | Spacing between nodes                                                 |
| `theme`      | `ThemeName \| DiaxTheme`                 | —                | Theme preset or custom theme object                                   |
| `pathType`   | `'bezier' \| 'straight' \| 'orthogonal'` | `'bezier'`       | Edge path style                                                       |
| `className`  | `string`                                 | —                | Container class                                                       |
| `centered`   | `boolean`                                | `false`          | Center nodes in grid cells                                            |
| `fallback`   | `ReactNode \| (error) => ReactNode`      | accessible error | Custom invalid-input UI; the diagnostic is available as `error.cause` |
| `onError`    | `(error) => void`                        | —                | Observe detection or parsing failures                                 |

How It Works [#how-it-works]

1. `parseMermaid(chart)` detects and parses through one public entry
2. The matching transformer converts the supported Mermaid subset → `DiaxAST`
3. `BUILTIN_NODE_TYPES[type]` provides the default nodeTypes registry
4. Custom `nodeTypes` prop is merged on top (overrides win)
5. `FlowDiagram` renders with the resolved `nodeTypes` + `renderNode`

This is the same **component registry** pattern used by Formily — type strings
map to render functions, and the registry is extensible at runtime.


# StateNode (/docs/ui-react/state-diagram)





Overview [#overview]

`StateNode` renders state machine nodes with three variants: default (rounded rectangle),
initial (filled circle), and final (double circle).

All Variants [#all-variants]
