Props [#props]

| Prop          | Type                                | Default     | Description        |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------ |
| `variant`     | `"default" \| "initial" \| "final"` | `"default"` | Node shape variant |
| `active`      | `boolean`                           | `false`     | Accent border glow |
| `highlighted` | `boolean`                           | `false`     | Ring + scale       |
| `dimmed`      | `boolean`                           | `false`     | Reduced opacity    |


# Advanced (/docs/vue/advanced)



Highlight on Hover [#highlight-on-hover]

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDiagram } from '@diax/vue';

const { nodes, highlightedNodes, highlightedEdgeIds, containerStyle } = useDiagram({
  nodes: [...],
  relations: [...],
  highlightOnHover: true,
});

// Forward both sets when composing useEdgeRenderer yourself.
void highlightedNodes;
void highlightedEdgeIds;
</script>

<template>
  <div :style="containerStyle">
    <div
      v-for="node in nodes"
      :key="node.id"
      v-bind="node.bindProps"
      :class="{
        'opacity-25': node.bindProps['data-flow-state'] === 'dimmed',
        'ring-2 ring-indigo-500':
          node.bindProps['data-flow-state'] === 'highlighted',
      }"
    >
      {{ node.data.content }}
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

***

Centralized Topology and Template Presentation [#centralized-topology-and-template-presentation]

Vue keeps topology in `:nodes` and `:relations`, then uses scoped slots for framework-native
presentation. React adds an optional `@diax/react/jsx` authoring Adapter for small static TSX
definitions; dynamic data still uses the same centralized nodes and relations as Vue.

| Mode                                            | Best for                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| **Data-driven** (`:nodes` + `:relations` props) | AI output, JSON APIs, dynamic data, simple diagrams |
| **Scoped slots** (`#node`)                      | Complex custom content and per-node styling         |

Combine both approaches for maximum flexibility:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/vue';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'fe', type: 'frontend', content: 'Frontend' },
  { id: 'api', type: 'backend', content: 'API Server' },
  { id: 'db', type: 'database', content: 'PostgreSQL' },
];

const relations = ['fe->|gRPC|api', 'api->|SQL|db'];
</script>

<template>
  <FlowDiagram :nodes="nodes" :relations="relations" density="spacious">
    <template #node="{ node, state }">
      <div
        class="flex items-center gap-2 px-4 py-3 rounded-xl"
        :class="{
          'bg-blue-500/10 border border-blue-500/20': node.type === 'frontend',
          'bg-emerald-500/10 border border-emerald-500/20':
            node.type === 'backend',
          'bg-amber-500/10 border border-amber-500/20':
            node.type === 'database',
          'opacity-25': state === 'dimmed',
          'ring-2 ring-indigo-500': state === 'highlighted',
        }"
      >
        {{ node.content }}
      </div>
    </template>
  </FlowDiagram>
</template>
```

***

DOM ID Namespaces [#dom-id-namespaces]

Use `namespace` to prevent resolved DOM IDs from colliding across diagrams:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDiagram } from '@diax/vue';

const frontend = useDiagram({
  nodes: [...],
  relations: ['gw->bff'],
  namespace: 'fe',
});

const backend = useDiagram({
  nodes: [...],
  relations: ['svc->db'],
  namespace: 'be',
});
</script>
```

Node IDs become `namespace::nodeId` in the DOM. Each built-in renderer measures only its own
diagram container, so it does not draw an edge between separate canvases. Keep connected topology
inside one diagram. DOM-first Connect is public from `@diax/react/connect`, but a Vue Connect adapter
is not available yet.

***

Mindmap Layout [#mindmap-layout]

Use `layout: 'mindmap'` for center-outward radial diagrams:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDiagram } from '@diax/vue';

const { nodes, containerStyle } = useDiagram({
  nodes: [
    { id: 'core', content: 'Platform' },
    { id: 'fe', content: 'Frontend' },
    { id: 'be', content: 'Backend' },
    { id: 'infra', content: 'Infrastructure' },
    { id: 'auth', content: 'Auth' },
    { id: 'db', content: 'Database' },
  ],
  relations: ['core->fe', 'core->be', 'core->infra', 'be->auth', 'be->db'],
  layout: 'mindmap',
});
</script>

<template>
  <div :style="containerStyle">
    <div v-for="node in nodes" :key="node.id" v-bind="node.bindProps">
      <div
        class="px-4 py-2 rounded-xl border border-white/8 bg-gradient-to-b from-white/6 to-white/2"
      >
        {{ node.data.content }}
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

Or use the `<Mindmap>` component directly:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Mindmap } from '@diax/vue';
</script>

<template>
  <Mindmap
    :nodes="[
      { id: 'core', content: 'Platform' },
      { id: 'fe', content: 'Frontend' },
      { id: 'be', content: 'Backend' },
    ]"
    :relations="['core->fe', 'core->be']"
  />
</template>
```


# Headless Composables (/docs/vue/composables)



Headless: useDiagram Composable [#headless-usediagram-composable]

For full headless control, use the `useDiagram` composable directly:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDiagram } from '@diax/vue';

const { nodes, edges, layoutMap, containerStyle } = useDiagram({ // [!code highlight]
  nodes: [
    { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'Process' },
    { id: 'c', content: 'End' },
  ],
  relations: ['a->b', 'b->c'],
});
</script>

<template>
  <div :style="containerStyle">
    <div
      v-for="node in nodes"
      :key="node.id"
      v-bind="node.bindProps" // [!code highlight]
    >
      <div class="px-4 py-2 rounded-xl border border-white/8 bg-gradient-to-b from-white/6 to-white/2">
        {{ node.data.content }}
      </div>
    </div>
    <!-- Edge rendering via SVG overlay (same pattern as React) -->
  </div>
</template>
```

Understanding `node.bindProps` [#understanding-nodebindprops]

When rendering nodes manually in Vue, you must spread `node.bindProps` exclusively onto the wrapper DOM element:

```vue
<div v-for="node in nodes" :key="node.id" v-bind="node.bindProps">
  <!-- Custom Content -->
</div>
```

The `bindProps` object automates:

1. **Grid Placement**: `style.gridColumn` and `style.gridRow` logic to align the node visually.
2. **Measurement Binding**: `data-diax-node` ID tags used by internal sizing hooks.
3. **Accessibility**: `aria-flowto` is added explicitly indicating next step relationships.
4. **Interactivity Hooks**: Mouse enter/leave events triggering `highlightOnHover` actions.

Reactive Options [#reactive-options]

You can pass a `ref` as options for fully reactive updates:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { useDiagram } from '@diax/vue';

const options = ref({
  nodes: [
    { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'End' },
  ],
  relations: ['a->b'],
  direction: 'horizontal' as const,
});

const { nodes, containerStyle } = useDiagram(options);

// Reactively update
function addNode() {
  options.value = {
    ...options.value,
    nodes: [...options.value.nodes, { id: 'c', content: 'New Node' }],
    relations: [...options.value.relations, 'b->c'],
  };
}
</script>
```

Reactive themes [#reactive-themes]

Theme selection is ordinary Vue state. DiaX intentionally does not wrap `ref()` with a parallel
`useTheme` interface; pass the value to the diagram and let the diagram own CSS injection:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { FlowDiagram, type ThemeInput } from '@diax/vue';

const theme = ref<ThemeInput>('linear');

function toggle() {
  theme.value = theme.value === 'light' ? 'linear' : 'light';
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="p-8">
    <button @click="toggle">Toggle Theme</button>
    <FlowDiagram :nodes="nodes" :relations="relations" :theme="theme" />
  </div>
</template>
```

For a manual CSS-variable object outside a diagram, import `resolveTheme` and `themeToStyle` from
the explicit `diax/themes` leaf instead of loading that policy through the Vue root.

Independent payload types [#independent-payload-types]

The composable is typed as `useDiagram<NodeContent, EdgeLabel, GroupLabel>()`. Its node, edge, and
group refs preserve those types independently. Ordinary object literals and typed refs infer the
payloads; explicit arguments are only needed when an empty array removes inference context. String
relation shorthand remains part of the parsed edge-label union.

Image Export [#image-export]

`@diax/vue` does not currently export a `useExport` composable. DiaX diagrams combine ordinary DOM
nodes and an SVG edge layer, so serializing only the SVG cannot preserve the complete diagram.

For now, bind a template ref to a wrapper you own and integrate a DOM-capture library at the
application boundary. Pin fonts, background colors and asset loading in that integration and test
the resulting image in the browsers you support. The Playground now verifies complete DOM + SVG
PNG/SVG export as an opt-in product workflow, but that implementation is not a stable framework
interface. See [Export DOM Visuals](/docs/guide/exporting).


# Custom Rendering (/docs/vue/custom-rendering)



Custom Rendering [#custom-rendering]

Use the `#node` scoped slot to customize how nodes look while keeping all layout logic:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/vue';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
  { id: 'b', content: 'Process' },
  { id: 'c', content: 'End' },
];

const relations = ['a->b', 'b->c'];
</script>

<template>
  <FlowDiagram
    :nodes="nodes"
    :relations="relations"
    highlight-on-hover
  >
    <template #node="{ node, state }">
      <div
        class="px-4 py-2 rounded-xl border"
        :class="{
          'ring-2 ring-blue-500': state === 'highlighted',
          'opacity-25': state === 'dimmed',
        }"
      >
        {{ node.content }}
      </div>
    </template>
  </FlowDiagram>
</template>
```

TypeScript Generics & Strong Typing [#typescript-generics--strong-typing]

DiaX Vue bindings support strict generic payload inference. Pass specific types to safely use `node.data.content` anywhere:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDiagram } from '@diax/vue';

interface ServerData {
  ip: string;
  uptime: number;
}

const { nodes } = useDiagram<ServerData>({
  nodes: [{ id: 'web1', content: { ip: '10.0.0.1', uptime: 99.9 } }],
    relations: []
});
</script>

<template>
  <div v-for="node in nodes" :key="node.id">
    <!-- Strictly typed! -->
    {{ node.data.content.ip }} - {{ node.data.content.uptime }}%
  </div>
</template>
```

Node States [#node-states]

The `state` value in the scoped slot tells you the current interaction state:

| State           | When              | Suggested style  |
| --------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| `undefined`     | Default           | Normal           |
| `"highlighted"` | On hover path     | Ring/glow effect |
| `"dimmed"`      | Not on hover path | Reduced opacity  |

Node Type Registry (`nodeTypes`) [#node-type-registry-nodetypes]

Define reusable node renderers by type, then reference them in the nodes array:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/vue';
import { h } from 'vue';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'gw', type: 'gateway', content: 'API Gateway' },
  { id: 'auth', type: 'service', content: 'Auth Service' },
  { id: 'user', type: 'service', content: 'User Service' },
];

const relations = ['gw->auth', 'gw->user'];

const nodeTypes = {
  gateway: (node: { content: string }) => h(
    'div',
    { class: 'rounded-xl border border-indigo-500/20 bg-indigo-500/10 px-5 py-3' },
    `⬡ ${node.content}`,
  ),
  service: (node: { content: string }) => h(
    'div',
    { class: 'rounded-lg border border-emerald-500/20 bg-emerald-500/10 px-4 py-2' },
    `● ${node.content}`,
  ),
};
</script>

<template>
  <FlowDiagram
    :nodes="nodes"
    :relations="relations"
    :node-types="nodeTypes"
  />
</template>
```

**Resolution order**: `#node` slot > `nodeTypes[node.type]` > default renderer.


# Edge Types (/docs/vue/edges)



Edge Types [#edge-types]

String DSL [#string-dsl]

```vue
<FlowDiagram
  :nodes="nodes"
  :relations="[
    'a->b',           // Solid arrow
    'a-->b',          // Dashed arrow
    'a<->b',          // Bidirectional
    'a->|label|b',    // With label
  ]"
/>
```

Object Form [#object-form]

```vue
<FlowDiagram
  :nodes="nodes"
  :relations="[
    { from: 'a', to: 'b', style: 'dashed', color: '#E91E63' },
    { from: 'b', to: 'c', animate: 'flow', label: 'next' },
    { from: 'c', to: 'd', bidirectional: true },
  ]"
/>
```

Animation Presets [#animation-presets]

| Preset              | Effect                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `"flow"`            | Flowing dashes along the edge  |
| `"pulse"`           | Breathing opacity effect       |
| `"shimmer"`         | Light traveling along the edge |
| `"reverse-flow"`    | Reverse flowing dashes         |
| `"reverse-shimmer"` | Reverse shimmer                |

***

Edge Path Types [#edge-path-types]

Control how edges are drawn with the `path-type` prop:

Bezier (default) [#bezier-default]

Smooth cubic bezier curves — the default and most common style:

```vue
<FlowDiagram
  :nodes="nodes"
  :relations="relations"
  path-type="bezier"
/>
```

Straight [#straight]

Direct straight lines between nodes:

```vue
<FlowDiagram
  :nodes="nodes"
  :relations="relations"
  path-type="straight"
/>
```

Orthogonal [#orthogonal]

Right-angle polylines that follow horizontal/vertical paths only:

```vue
<FlowDiagram
  :nodes="nodes"
  :relations="relations"
  path-type="orthogonal"
/>
```

***

Edge Labels [#edge-labels]

The Vue adapter renders string labels from either the DSL or object relation form:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/vue';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'client', content: 'Client' },
  { id: 'api', content: 'API' },
  { id: 'db', content: 'Database' },
];

const relations = [
  'client->|REST|api',
  'api->|SQL|db',
];
</script>

<template><FlowDiagram :nodes="nodes" :relations="relations" /></template>
```

Decorate the same serializable label with Vue-native content through the `#edge-label` scoped slot:

```vue contract
<script setup lang="ts">
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/vue';
</script>

<template>
  <FlowDiagram
    :nodes="[
      { id: 'client', content: 'Client' },
      { id: 'api', content: 'API' },
    ]"
    :relations="['client->|HTTPS|api']"
  >
    <template #edge-label="{ label }">
      <strong class="protocol-badge">🔒 {{ label }}</strong>
    </template>
  </FlowDiagram>
</template>
```

The slot receives `{ label }`. Keep framework objects out of the relation definition so the same
topology remains valid for JSON, workers and other adapters.

Group Labels [#group-labels]

Keep group definitions semantic and decorate their labels through `#group-label`. The scoped slot
receives the original `group` plus its non-null `label`; derived boundary coordinates remain
internal to DiaX.

```vue contract
<script setup lang="ts">
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/vue';
</script>

<template>
  <FlowDiagram
    :nodes="[
      { id: 'browser', content: 'Browser' },
      { id: 'api', content: 'API' },
    ]"
    :relations="['browser->api']"
    :groups="[{ id: 'backend', label: 'Backend', nodeIds: ['api'] }]"
  >
    <template #group-label="{ group, label }">
      <strong class="boundary-label" :data-group="group.id">◫ {{ label }}</strong>
    </template>
  </FlowDiagram>
</template>
```

Group labels are presentation inside a non-interactive boundary surface. Use them for headings,
badges and icons, not buttons or form controls.


# Vue Guide (/docs/vue)



<InstallTabs packages="[&#x22;@diax/vue&#x22;]" description="Vue bindings (peer dependency: vue >= 3.3)" />

<Callout type="warn">
  **Nuxt / SSR**: `@diax/vue` renders a stable SSR shell and measures pixel edge paths after mount.
  `<ClientOnly>` is optional for application-owned browser-only node content, not a DiaX requirement.
  See [Nuxt & Vue SSR](/docs/vue/nuxt).
</Callout>

Progressive API [#progressive-api]

DiaX provides three levels of control. Choose based on your needs:

| Layer | API                                          | Best for                               |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| 1     | `<FlowDiagram>` / `<Mindmap>`                | Quick usage, AI output, prototyping    |
| 2     | `<FlowDiagram>` + scoped slots / `nodeTypes` | Custom styling with your design system |
| 3     | `useDiagram()` composable                    | Full headless control, library authors |

***

Quick Start [#quick-start]

The simplest way to use DiaX — just pass nodes and relations:

```vue contract
<script setup lang="ts">
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/vue';
</script>

<template>
  <FlowDiagram
    :nodes="[
      { id: 'client', content: 'Browser' },
      { id: 'api', content: 'API Server' },
      { id: 'db', content: 'Database' },
    ]"
    :relations="[
      'client->|HTTPS|api',
      'api->|SQL|db',
    ]"
    density="comfortable"
  />
</template>
```

Density [#density]

Control spacing with the `density` prop:

| Value           | Description                             |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `"compact"`     | Tight spacing, good for inline diagrams |
| `"comfortable"` | Default, balanced spacing               |
| `"spacious"`    | Wide spacing, good for presentations    |

Direction [#direction]

```vue
<FlowDiagram direction="horizontal" />         <!-- Left to right (default) -->
<FlowDiagram direction="vertical" />            <!-- Top to bottom -->
<FlowDiagram direction="horizontal-reverse" />  <!-- Right to left -->
<FlowDiagram direction="vertical-reverse" />    <!-- Bottom to top -->
```

| Value                  | Description                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `"horizontal"`         | Left to right (default)        |
| `"vertical"`           | Top to bottom                  |
| `"horizontal-reverse"` | Right to left (RTL flows)      |
| `"vertical-reverse"`   | Bottom to top (upstream flows) |

Layout Algorithms [#layout-algorithms]

Use the dedicated component for each layout type:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { FlowDiagram, Mindmap } from '@diax/vue';
</script>

<template>
  <FlowDiagram :nodes="nodes" :relations="relations" />  <!-- DAG layout -->
  <Mindmap :nodes="nodes" :relations="relations" />       <!-- Center-outward radial -->
</template>
```



Next Steps [#next-steps]

  <Card title="Custom Rendering" href="/docs/vue/custom-rendering" description="Customize node rendering with scoped slots and nodeTypes" />

  <Card title="useDiagram Composable" href="/docs/vue/composables" description="Full headless control with Vue's useDiagram composable" />

  <Card title="Edge Types" href="/docs/vue/edges" description="DSL syntax, animations, path types, and custom edge labels" />

  <Card title="Advanced" href="/docs/vue/advanced" description="Stagger, highlight, mindmap, namespaces, and template patterns" />

  <Card title="Nuxt 3" href="/docs/vue/nuxt" description="Using DiaX with Nuxt 3 and Vue SSR" />

  <Card title="Props Reference" href="/docs/vue/props" description="Complete props, slots, and composable reference" />
</Cards>


# Nuxt & Vue SSR (/docs/vue/nuxt)



Vue SSR behavior [#vue-ssr-behavior]

`@diax/vue` renders a stable node shell during SSR and starts DOM measurement only after mount. Its
package lifecycle tests execute Vue `renderToString()`, hydrate the result, preserve node identity,
and then render measured edges.

A Nuxt page can therefore use an ordinary Vue diagram component. The following SFC is a host
fragment—it is shown in full, but the current docs gate compiles Vue syntax rather than running a
Nuxt production build:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/vue';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'frontend', content: 'Frontend' },
  { id: 'api', content: 'API' },
  { id: 'database', content: 'Database' },
];
const relations = ['frontend->api', 'api->database'];
</script>

<template>
  <FlowDiagram :nodes="nodes" :relations="relations" />
</template>
```

Final SVG paths are not calculated on the server because pixel rectangles do not exist there. They
appear after hydration without requiring the application to replace the server-rendered node DOM.

When to use `<ClientOnly>` [#when-to-use-clientonly]

Use Nuxt's `<ClientOnly>` or a `.client.vue` component only when application-owned node content
depends on a browser-only SDK, or when you intentionally do not want server HTML for an optional
diagram. It is not the default DiaX integration:

```vue
<template>
  <!-- Nuxt host fragment: use only for an intentionally browser-only feature. -->
  <ClientOnly fallback-tag="p" fallback="Loading architecture…">
    <BrowserOnlyDiagram />
  </ClientOnly>
</template>
```

These Nuxt fragments are deliberately not marked as code contracts. A future Nuxt fixture must
validate the actual module resolver, server bundle, route render, hydration, and framework version;
the existing Vue SFC compiler check cannot honestly prove those host responsibilities.

Verify the adapter contract [#verify-the-adapter-contract]

Run the Vue package lifecycle suite for its current SSR→hydration evidence:

```bash
pnpm --filter @diax/vue test
```

Until a dedicated Nuxt production fixture exists, describe the package as Vue SSR/hydration
compatible rather than claiming independently verified Nuxt parity.

# Advanced (/docs/vanilla/advanced)



DOM ID Namespaces [#dom-id-namespaces]

Use `namespace` to prevent resolved DOM IDs from colliding across independent diagrams:

```html
<div style="display: flex; gap: 32px;">
  <div id="frontend"></div>
  <div id="backend"></div>
</div>

<script type="module">
  import { createDiagram } from '@diax/vanilla';

  // Frontend diagram
  const feDiagram = createDiagram(document.getElementById('frontend'), {
    namespace: 'fe',
    nodes: [
      { id: 'app', content: 'React App' },
      { id: 'gw', content: 'API Gateway' },
    ],
    relations: ['app->gw'],
  });

  // Backend diagram
  const beDiagram = createDiagram(document.getElementById('backend'), {
    namespace: 'be',
    nodes: [
      { id: 'svc', content: 'User Service' },
      { id: 'db', content: 'PostgreSQL' },
    ],
    relations: ['svc->db'],
  });
</script>
```

Node IDs become `namespace::nodeId` in the DOM. Each `createDiagram()` instance measures and draws
inside its own container; it does not create a shared cross-container SVG overlay. Keep connected
topology inside one diagram. DOM-first Connect is public from `@diax/react/connect`, but a Vanilla
Connect adapter is not available yet.

***

Mindmap [#mindmap]

Use `layout: 'mindmap'` to render a center-outward radial layout instead of the default DAG flow:

```js
const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  layout: 'mindmap',
  nodes: [
    { id: 'root', content: 'DiaX' },
    { id: 'core', content: 'Core Engine' },
    { id: 'react', content: 'React' },
    { id: 'vue', content: 'Vue' },
    { id: 'svelte', content: 'Svelte' },
    { id: 'vanilla', content: 'Vanilla' },
    { id: 'layout', content: 'CSS Grid' },
    { id: 'edges', content: 'SVG Edges' },
  ],
  relations: [
    'root->core',
    'root->react',
    'root->vue',
    'root->svelte',
    'root->vanilla',
    'core->layout',
    'core->edges',
  ],
});
```

Mindmap layout places the root node at the center and branches outward. It works well for hierarchical topic maps, brainstorming diagrams, and tree-like structures.

You can combine mindmap with other options:

```js
const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  layout: 'mindmap',
  direction: 'horizontal',
  highlightOnHover: true,
  pathType: 'bezier',
  nodes: [...],
  relations: [...],
});
```


# Custom Rendering (/docs/vanilla/custom-rendering)



Custom Node Rendering [#custom-node-rendering]

Use `renderNode` to customize how nodes look:

```js
const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'client', content: 'Browser' },
    { id: 'api', content: 'API Server' },
    { id: 'db', content: 'Database' },
  ],
  relations: [
    'client->|HTTPS|api',
    'api->|SQL|db',
  ],
  renderNode: (node, el) => {
    el.innerHTML = `
      <div style="
        padding: 8px 16px;
        border-radius: 10px;
        border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1);
        background: linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(94,106,210,0.15), rgba(94,106,210,0.05));
        color: #EDEDEF;
        font-family: Inter, system-ui;
        font-size: 13px;
      ">
        ${node.content}
      </div>
    `;
  },
});
```

TypeScript Generics & Strong Typing [#typescript-generics--strong-typing]

DiaX Vanilla bindings fully support strict generic payloads. Pass your custom type to `createDiagram<T>` to type-check `node.content`:

```ts
import { createDiagram } from '@diax/vanilla';

interface ServerData {
  ip: string;
  uptime: number;
}

const diagram = createDiagram<ServerData>(container, {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'web1', content: { ip: '10.0.0.1', uptime: 99.9 } },
  ],
  relations: [],
  renderNode: (node, el) => {
    // node is DiaxNode<ServerData>
    el.innerHTML = `
      <div>
        ${node.content.ip} - ${node.content.uptime}%
      </div>
    `;
  },
});
```

Node States [#node-states]

The `renderNode` callback receives a third `state` parameter that reflects the current interaction state:

```js
renderNode: (node, el, state) => {
  // state is "highlighted" | "dimmed" | undefined
}
```

Accessibility (`aria-flowto`) [#accessibility-aria-flowto]

DiaX Vanilla gives every node wrapper a stable DOM `id` and injects valid `aria-flowto` references
from parsed relations. Support varies across assistive technologies, so this is supplemental metadata
rather than a guaranteed screen-reader navigation command. Keep node content semantic, place the
diagram in a named region and provide a non-spatial summary when the relationships are essential.

The `renderNode` callback can use its third `state` parameter for visual emphasis without changing
the wrapper's semantics:

```js
renderNode: (node, el, state) => {
  el.textContent = node.content;
  if (state === 'highlighted') {
    el.style.boxShadow = '0 0 0 2px rgba(94,106,210,0.6)';
    el.style.opacity = '1';
  } else if (state === 'dimmed') {
    el.style.boxShadow = 'none';
    el.style.opacity = '0.25';
  } else {
    el.style.boxShadow = 'none';
    el.style.opacity = '1';
  }
}
```

| State           | When              | Suggested style  |
| --------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| `undefined`     | Default           | Normal           |
| `"highlighted"` | On hover path     | Ring/glow effect |
| `"dimmed"`      | Not on hover path | Reduced opacity  |


# Edge Types (/docs/vanilla/edges)



Edge Animations [#edge-animations]

Use object-form relations for animated edges:

```js
// [!code word:animate]
const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  nodes: [...],
  relations: [
    { from: 'a', to: 'b', animate: 'flow' },
    { from: 'b', to: 'c', animate: 'pulse', color: '#4CAF50' },
    { from: 'c', to: 'd', animate: 'shimmer', color: '#5E6AD2' },
  ],
});
```

Animation Presets [#animation-presets]

| Preset              | Effect                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `"flow"`            | Flowing dashes along the edge  |
| `"pulse"`           | Breathing opacity effect       |
| `"shimmer"`         | Light traveling along the edge |
| `"reverse-flow"`    | Reverse flowing dashes         |
| `"reverse-shimmer"` | Reverse shimmer                |

***

Edge Path Types [#edge-path-types]

Control how edges are drawn with the `pathType` option:

Bezier (default) [#bezier-default]

Smooth cubic bezier curves — the default and most common style:

```js
// [!code word:pathType]
const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'Middle' },
    { id: 'c', content: 'End' },
  ],
  relations: ['a->b', 'b->c'],
  pathType: 'bezier',
});
```

Straight [#straight]

Direct straight lines between nodes:

```js
// [!code word:pathType]
const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'Middle' },
    { id: 'c', content: 'End' },
  ],
  relations: ['a->b', 'b->c'],
  pathType: 'straight',
});
```

Orthogonal [#orthogonal]

Right-angle polylines that follow horizontal/vertical paths only:

```js
// [!code word:pathType]
const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'Middle' },
    { id: 'c', content: 'End' },
  ],
  relations: ['a->b', 'b->c'],
  pathType: 'orthogonal',
});
```

***

Edge Labels [#edge-labels]

Use the `label` property on object-form relations to add labels to edges:

```js
const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'client', content: 'Client' },
    { id: 'api', content: 'API Server' },
    { id: 'db', content: 'Database' },
  ],
  relations: [
    { from: 'client', to: 'api', label: 'HTTPS' },
    { from: 'api', to: 'db', label: 'SQL' },
  ],
});
```

You can also use the string DSL shorthand:

```js
relations: ['client->|HTTPS|api', 'api->|SQL|db']
```

Labels are real HTML inside the SVG overlay, so normal DOM styling and content work. Use
`renderEdgeLabel` when a string is not expressive enough:

```ts contract vanilla
import { createDiagram } from '@diax/vanilla';

interface ProtocolLabel {
  icon: string;
  text: string;
}

const container = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#diagram');
if (!container) throw new Error('Missing #diagram container.');

createDiagram<string, ProtocolLabel>(container, {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'client', content: 'Client' },
    { id: 'api', content: 'API' },
  ],
  relations: [
    { from: 'client', to: 'api', label: { icon: '🔒', text: 'HTTPS' } },
  ],
  renderEdgeLabel: (label, element) => {
    if (typeof label === 'string') {
      element.textContent = label;
      return;
    }
    element.className = 'protocol-badge';
    element.append(label.icon, label.text);
  },
});
```

The callback receives a fresh DiaX-owned element whenever the edge layer is rebuilt. Treat it as an
owned render target: append content and classes to that element, and let DiaX retain measurement and
cleanup ownership.

Group Labels [#group-labels]

Use `renderGroupLabel` to apply application-owned DOM presentation without putting elements or HTML
strings into the semantic group definition:

```ts contract vanilla
import { createDiagram } from '@diax/vanilla';

const container = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#diagram');
if (!container) throw new Error('Missing #diagram container.');

createDiagram(container, {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'browser', content: 'Browser' },
    { id: 'api', content: 'API' },
  ],
  relations: ['browser->api'],
  groups: [{ id: 'backend', label: 'Backend', nodeIds: ['api'] }],
  renderGroupLabel: (group, element) => {
    element.className = 'boundary-label';
    element.dataset.group = group.id;
    element.append('◫ ', group.label ?? '');
  },
});
```

The callback receives the original semantic group and a fresh DiaX-owned label element. Boundary
geometry, ResizeObserver invalidation and cleanup stay automatic. Group surfaces intentionally do
not accept pointer interaction; place controls inside nodes instead.

***

Highlight on Hover [#highlight-on-hover]

Enable `highlightOnHover` to automatically highlight connected paths when hovering over a node. Nodes on the hovered path receive the `"highlighted"` state, while all other nodes are `"dimmed"`:

```js
// [!code word:highlightOnHover]
const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'gw', content: 'API Gateway' },
    { id: 'auth', content: 'Auth Service' },
    { id: 'user', content: 'User Service' },
    { id: 'db', content: 'PostgreSQL' },
  ],
  relations: ['gw->auth', 'gw->user', 'auth->db', 'user->db'],
  highlightOnHover: true,
});
```

Combine with `renderNode` to apply custom highlight styles:

```js
// [!code word:highlightOnHover]
// [!code word:renderNode]
const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  nodes: [...],
  relations: [...],
  highlightOnHover: true,
  renderNode: (node, el, state) => {
    el.innerHTML = `<div class="node">${node.content}</div>`;
    const div = el.querySelector('.node');
    div.style.padding = '8px 16px';
    div.style.borderRadius = '10px';
    div.style.border = '1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1)';
    div.style.color = '#EDEDEF';
    div.style.fontFamily = 'Inter, system-ui';
    div.style.fontSize = '13px';
    div.style.transition = 'opacity 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s';

    if (state === 'highlighted') {
      div.style.boxShadow = '0 0 0 2px rgba(94,106,210,0.6)';
      div.style.opacity = '1';
    } else if (state === 'dimmed') {
      div.style.opacity = '0.25';
      div.style.boxShadow = 'none';
    } else {
      div.style.opacity = '1';
      div.style.boxShadow = 'none';
    }
  },
});
```


# Vanilla JS Guide (/docs/vanilla)



<InstallTabs packages="['@diax/vanilla']" description="Vanilla JS bindings (zero framework dependencies)" />

Progressive API [#progressive-api]

DiaX provides three levels of control via the imperative `createDiagram` API. Choose based on your needs:

| Layer | API                                       | Best for                               |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| 1     | `createDiagram(el, { nodes, relations })` | Quick usage, zero config, prototyping  |
| 2     | `createDiagram(el, { renderNode })`       | Custom styling with your design system |
| 3     | `getLayout()` / `getEdges()`              | Full headless control, library authors |

***

createDiagram [#creatediagram]

The `createDiagram` function creates a diagram inside a container element:

```html title="index.html"
<div id="diagram" style="background: #050506; padding: 40px;"></div>

<script type="module">
  import { createDiagram } from '@diax/vanilla';

  const diagram = createDiagram(document.getElementById('diagram'), {
    nodes: [
      { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
      { id: 'b', content: 'Process' },
      { id: 'c', content: 'End' },
    ],
    relations: ['a->b', 'b->c'],
  });
</script>
```

That's it — nodes are rendered with beautiful defaults, edges are drawn as SVG overlays.

TypeScript callers should narrow the container before creating the diagram:

```ts contract vanilla
import { createDiagram } from '@diax/vanilla';

const container = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#diagram');
if (!container) throw new Error('Missing #diagram container.');

const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  nodes: [
    { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'End' },
  ],
  relations: ['a->b'],
});

diagram.getLayout();
```

Configuration [#configuration]

```js
const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
  nodes: [...],
  relations: [...],
  direction: 'vertical',          // 'horizontal' | 'vertical' | 'horizontal-reverse' | 'vertical-reverse'
  theme: 'github',                // 'linear' | 'light' | 'notion' | 'github'
  highlightOnHover: true,         // Highlight connected paths on hover
  pathType: 'bezier',             // 'bezier' | 'straight' | 'orthogonal'
});
```

***

Next Steps [#next-steps]

* [Custom Rendering](/docs/vanilla/custom-rendering) — Custom DOM rendering with `renderNode` callback and node states
* [Lifecycle](/docs/vanilla/lifecycle) — Update, destroy, and inspect diagram instances
* [Edge Types](/docs/vanilla/edges) — Edge animations, path types, and hover highlighting
* [Advanced](/docs/vanilla/advanced) — DOM ID namespaces and mindmap layout
* [API Reference](/docs/vanilla/props) — Configuration options and instance methods


# Lifecycle (/docs/vanilla/lifecycle)



Updating the Diagram [#updating-the-diagram]

Call `update()` with new options to re-render:

```js
// Add a new node
diagram.update({
  nodes: [
    { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'Process' },
    { id: 'c', content: 'End' },
    { id: 'd', content: 'Archive' },
  ],
  relations: ['a->b', 'b->c', 'c->d'],
});
```

Destroying the Diagram [#destroying-the-diagram]

Clean up when done:

```js
diagram.destroy();
// Container is emptied, ResizeObserver disconnected
```

Getting Layout Data [#getting-layout-data]

Access computed layout and edge data programmatically:

```js
const layout = diagram.getLayout();
console.log(layout.nodes); // [{ id: 'a', col: 0, row: 0 }, ...]
console.log(layout.cols);  // 3
console.log(layout.rows);  // 1

const edges = diagram.getEdges();
console.log(edges); // [{ from: 'a', to: 'b', dashed: false, ... }]
```


# API Reference (/docs/vanilla/props)



Configuration Options [#configuration-options]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  nodes: { description: 'Node definitions', type: 'DiaxNode<string>[]', default: 'required' },
  relations: { description: 'Relations', type: 'DiaxRelation<string>[]', default: 'required' },
  groups: { description: 'Nested semantic boundaries derived from direct members', type: 'DiaxGroup<string>[]', default: '[]' },
  namespace: { description: 'Resolved DOM ID namespace', type: 'string' },
  direction: { description: 'Layout direction', type: &#x22;'horizontal' | 'vertical' | 'horizontal-reverse' | 'vertical-reverse'&#x22;, default: &#x22;'horizontal'&#x22; },
  layout: { description: 'Layout algorithm', type: &#x22;'flow' | 'mindmap'&#x22;, default: &#x22;'flow'&#x22; },
  centered: { description: 'Center nodes', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
  highlightOnHover: { description: 'Highlight path on hover', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
  theme: { description: 'Theme preset or custom value', type: 'ThemeInput' },
  pathType: { description: 'Edge path type', type: &#x22;'bezier' | 'straight' | 'orthogonal'&#x22;, default: &#x22;'bezier'&#x22; },
  strokeColor: { description: 'Edge color; inherits currentColor when unthemed', type: 'string', default: &#x22;'var(--diax-edge-color, currentColor)'&#x22; },
  strokeWidth: { description: 'Edge stroke width', type: 'number', default: '1' },
  arrowSize: { description: 'Arrow marker size', type: 'number', default: '6' },
  renderNode: { description: 'Custom node renderer', type: '(node, el, state) => void' },
  renderEdgeLabel: { description: 'Render a semantic edge label into a fresh DiaX-owned element', type: '(label, element) => void' },
  renderGroupLabel: { description: 'Render a semantic group label into a fresh DiaX-owned element', type: '(group, element) => void' },
  nodeTypes: { description: 'Node type renderer registry', type: 'Record<string, (node, el, state) => void>' },
  onRender: { description: 'Called after render', type: '() => void' },
}"
/>

`CreateDiagramOptions<NodeContent, EdgeLabel, GroupLabel>` keeps node content, edge-label data, and
group-label data independent. String DSL labels remain strings, so `renderEdgeLabel` receives
`EdgeLabel | string`. Inference is preferred; the explicit order exists for empty definitions and
reusable renderer callbacks.

Instance Methods [#instance-methods]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  'update(options)': { description: 'Re-render with updated options', type: '(options: Partial<CreateDiagramOptions>) => void' },
  'destroy()': { description: 'Clean up and empty container', type: '() => void' },
  'getLayout()': { description: 'Get current LayoutResult', type: '() => LayoutResult' },
  'getEdges()': { description: 'Get current ParsedRelation[]', type: '() => ParsedRelation[]' },
}"
/>


# SSR & Frameworks (/docs/vanilla/ssr)



Server-Side Rendering (SSR) [#server-side-rendering-ssr]

DiaX intrinsically requires a DOM environment because its layout engine relies on the native `getBoundingClientRect` to calculate precise routing points for SVG edges.

If you are using `@diax/vanilla` within an SSR environment (like Next.js, Nuxt, Node servers, etc.), you must ensure that diagram initialization **strictly runs on the client-side** after hydration:

```javascript
if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
  // Safe to import and create diagram
  import('@diax/vanilla').then(({ createDiagram }) => {
    const container = document.getElementById('diagram-root');
    const diagram = createDiagram(container, {
      nodes: [...],
      relations: [...]
    });
  });
}
```

Cleanup in Framework Runtimes [#cleanup-in-framework-runtimes]

If you are wrapping `createDiagram` inside a framework component (e.g. wrapping Vanilla within an Angular or Web Component lifecycle), make sure to call `diagram.destroy()` when the component unmounts to prevent memory leaks from internal `ResizeObservers`.

```javascript
// Example: Custom Web Component Integration
class DiamondDiagram extends HTMLElement {
  connectedCallback() {
    this.diagram = createDiagram(this, {
      nodes: [{ id: '1', content: 'Node' }],
      relations: []
    });
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    // Critical: Clean up resize observers
    if (this.diagram) {
      this.diagram.destroy();
    }
  }
}
```


# Advanced (/docs/svelte/advanced)



DOM ID Namespaces [#dom-id-namespaces]

Use the high-level `namespace` prop to prevent resolved DOM IDs from colliding across diagram
instances:

```svelte contract
<script>
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/svelte';

const frontendNodes = [
  { id: 'gw', content: 'API Gateway' },
  { id: 'bff', content: 'BFF' },
];
const frontendRelations = ['gw->bff'];

const backendNodes = [
  { id: 'svc', content: 'User Service' },
  { id: 'db', content: 'Database' },
];
const backendRelations = ['svc->db'];
</script>

<div class="flex gap-8">
  <FlowDiagram namespace="fe" nodes={frontendNodes} relations={frontendRelations} />
  <FlowDiagram namespace="be" nodes={backendNodes} relations={backendRelations} />
</div>
```

Node IDs become `namespace::nodeId` in the DOM (for example, `fe::gw`). Each built-in renderer
measures only its own diagram container, so it does not draw edges between these two canvases. Keep
connected topology inside one diagram. DOM-first Connect is public from `@diax/react/connect`, but a
Svelte Connect adapter is not available yet.

***

Reactive Updates [#reactive-updates]

High-level component props follow ordinary Svelte reactivity. For a headless renderer,
`createDiagramStore()` exposes `updateOptions()` so callers can update topology without replacing
the returned stores. See [Headless Stores](/docs/svelte/stores).


# Custom Rendering (/docs/svelte/custom-rendering)



Component Slots [#component-slots]

Customize node rendering while keeping all layout logic. In Svelte, use the `node` slot of the `<FlowDiagram>` component to render custom content:

```svelte
<script>
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/svelte';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'gw', type: 'gateway', content: 'API Gateway' },
  { id: 'auth', type: 'service', content: 'Auth Service' },
  { id: 'db', type: 'database', content: 'PostgreSQL' },
];
const relations = ['gw->auth', 'auth->db'];
</script>

<FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations} highlightOnHover>
  <svelte:fragment slot="node" let:node>
    <!-- Read node.flowState for interaction stylings -->
    <div
      class="px-4 py-2 rounded-xl border"
      class:ring-2={node.flowState === 'highlighted'}
      class:opacity-25={node.flowState === 'dimmed'}
    >
      {#if node.data.type === 'gateway'}
        ⬡ {node.data.content}
      {:else}
        {node.data.content}
      {/if}
    </div>
  </svelte:fragment>
</FlowDiagram>
```

Node States [#node-states]

The `node.flowState` property provides the current interaction state when `highlightOnHover=true` is active:

| State           | When              | Suggested style  |
| --------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| `undefined`     | Default           | Normal           |
| `"highlighted"` | On hover path     | Ring/glow effect |
| `"dimmed"`      | Not on hover path | Reduced opacity  |

Resolving Node Types [#resolving-node-types]

Instead of a big `if-else` block, you can map your node content to dedicated Svelte components conditionally:

```svelte
<!-- In your FlowDiagram usage -->
<script>
  import GatewayNode from './GatewayNode.svelte';
  import ServiceNode from './ServiceNode.svelte';
  
  const typeMap = {
    gateway: GatewayNode,
    service: ServiceNode
  };
</script>

<FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations}>
  <svelte:fragment slot="node" let:node>
    <svelte:component 
      this={typeMap[node.data.type] ?? ServiceNode} 
      {node} 
    />
  </svelte:fragment>

</FlowDiagram>
```

For structured generic content, compose the low-level store and `DiagramEdges` as shown in
[Headless Stores](/docs/svelte/stores). The high-level component currently renders string content.


# Edge Types (/docs/svelte/edges)



Keep relations on the Diagram [#keep-relations-on-the-diagram]

The high-level component parses relations, measures the rendered nodes and draws the SVG edge layer.
You do not compute or render `edgePaths` yourself.

String DSL [#string-dsl]

```svelte
<script>
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/svelte';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
  { id: 'b', content: 'Review' },
  { id: 'c', content: 'Ship' },
];
const relations = [
  'a->b',
  'b-->|changes|a',
  'b->|approved|c',
];
</script>

<FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations} />
```

Object relations [#object-relations]

Use objects for styles, markers, events and AI-generated input:

```svelte
<script>
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/svelte';

const relations = [
  { from: 'a', to: 'b', style: 'dashed', color: '#E91E63' },
  { from: 'b', to: 'c', animate: 'flow', label: 'next' },
  { from: 'c', to: 'd', bidirectional: true, targetMarker: 'diamond' },
];
</script>

<FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations} />
```

Decorate a serializable label with Svelte-native markup through the named slot:

```svelte contract
<script>
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/svelte';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'client', content: 'Client' },
  { id: 'api', content: 'API' },
];
const relations = ['client->|HTTPS|api'];
</script>

<FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations}>
  <svelte:fragment slot="edge-label" let:label>
    <strong class="protocol-badge">🔒 {label}</strong>
  </svelte:fragment>
</FlowDiagram>
```

The current Svelte 4-compatible interface uses a named slot. Keep components and snippets out of
the relation definition; a future Svelte 5-only surface may offer a typed snippet with the same
semantic `label` value.

Group labels [#group-labels]

The Svelte 4-compatible group presentation seam is another named slot. It receives the original
semantic `group` and its non-null string `label`, while DiaX retains boundary placement and
measurement ownership.

```svelte contract
<script>
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/svelte';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'browser', content: 'Browser' },
  { id: 'api', content: 'API' },
];
const relations = ['browser->api'];
const groups = [{ id: 'backend', label: 'Backend', nodeIds: ['api'] }];
</script>

<FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations} {groups}>
  <svelte:fragment slot="group-label" let:group let:label>
    <strong class="boundary-label" data-group={group.id}>◫ {label}</strong>
  </svelte:fragment>
</FlowDiagram>
```

The boundary surface is non-interactive. Keep buttons and inputs in authored node content rather
than inside a group label.

Animation presets [#animation-presets]

Set `animate` on an object relation. `DiagramEdges` injects the required edge styles when it mounts.

| Preset              | Effect                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `"flow"`            | Flowing dashes                 |
| `"pulse"`           | Breathing opacity              |
| `"shimmer"`         | Light traveling along the edge |
| `"reverse-flow"`    | Reverse flowing dashes         |
| `"reverse-shimmer"` | Reverse shimmer                |

Animations follow the shared reduced-motion policy from Core.

Path types [#path-types]

Choose one surface fallback with the component prop:

```svelte
<FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations} pathType="bezier" />
<FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations} pathType="straight" />
<FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations} pathType="orthogonal" />
```

An object relation may override that fallback with its own `pathType`.

Interactive relations [#interactive-relations]

Handlers live on object relations. Add `ariaLabel` whenever endpoint names do not adequately describe
the action:

```svelte
<script>
const relations = [{
  from: 'review',
  to: 'details',
  ariaLabel: 'Open review evidence',
  events: {
    onClick: ({ from, to }) => console.log(from, to),
  },
}];
</script>

<FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations} />
```

See the [shared edge vocabulary](/docs/guide/edge-types) for every object field.


# Svelte Guide (/docs/svelte)



<InstallTabs packages="[&#x22;@diax/svelte&#x22;]" description="Svelte bindings (peer dependency: svelte >= 4)" />

Progressive API [#progressive-api]

DiaX Svelte provides three progressive levels of control, matching the core engine's architecture:

| Layer | API                                      | Best for                                      |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| 1     | `<FlowDiagram>` / `<Mindmap>` components | Quick usage, AI output, prototyping           |
| 2     | Component slots (`let:node`)             | Custom node styling with your design system   |
| 3     | `createDiagramStore()`                   | Full headless control, complex DOM structures |

***

Quick Start [#quick-start]

Use the zero-config `<FlowDiagram>` component for immediate results:

```svelte contract
<script>
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/svelte';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
  { id: 'b', content: 'Process' },
  { id: 'c', content: 'End' }
];

const relations = ['a->b', 'b->c'];
</script>

<FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations} />
```

Density [#density]

| Value           | Description                             |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `"compact"`     | Tight spacing, good for inline diagrams |
| `"comfortable"` | Default, balanced spacing               |
| `"spacious"`    | Wide spacing, good for presentations    |

Direction [#direction]

```svelte
<FlowDiagram direction="horizontal" {nodes} {relations} />         <!-- Left to right (default) -->
<FlowDiagram direction="vertical" {nodes} {relations} />            <!-- Top to bottom -->
<FlowDiagram direction="horizontal-reverse" {nodes} {relations} />  <!-- Right to left -->
<FlowDiagram direction="vertical-reverse" {nodes} {relations} />    <!-- Bottom to top -->
```

| Value                  | Description                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `"horizontal"`         | Left to right (default)        |
| `"vertical"`           | Top to bottom                  |
| `"horizontal-reverse"` | Right to left (RTL flows)      |
| `"vertical-reverse"`   | Bottom to top (upstream flows) |

Mindmap [#mindmap]

```svelte
<script>
import { Mindmap } from '@diax/svelte';

const nodes = [
  { id: 'core', content: 'Platform' },
  { id: 'fe', content: 'Frontend' },
  { id: 'be', content: 'Backend' }
];

const relations = ['core->fe', 'core->be'];
</script>

<Mindmap {nodes} {relations} />
```

***

Next Steps [#next-steps]

* \[Custom Rendering] — custom node styling, nodeType, and state handling
* \[Headless Stores] — full control with `createDiagramStore`
* [Edge Types](/docs/svelte/edges) — DSL syntax, animations, and customize paths
* [Advanced](/docs/svelte/advanced) — Stagger animation, DOM ID namespaces, reactive patterns
* [SvelteKit](/docs/svelte/sveltekit) — Browser checks and SSR guidance
* [API Reference](/docs/svelte/props) — Store return values and configuration options


# API Reference (/docs/svelte/props)

`FlowDiagram` and `Mindmap` accept the following presentation props. Custom generic payloads remain
available through the lower-level store interface below.

# Headless Stores (/docs/svelte/stores)



Use the public rendering primitives together [#use-the-public-rendering-primitives-together]

`createDiagramStore()` owns pure topology state. `DiagramEdges` owns DOM measurement and SVG
rendering. Use both when the built-in `FlowDiagram` wrapper is too opinionated; omitting
`DiagramEdges` intentionally produces nodes without connections.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
import { createDiagramStore, DiagramEdges } from '@diax/svelte';

const diagram = createDiagramStore({
  nodes: [
    { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
    { id: 'b', content: 'Review' },
    { id: 'c', content: 'Ship' },
  ],
  relations: ['a->b', 'b->c'],
  layout: 'flow',
  highlightOnHover: true,
});

const {
  nodes,
  edges,
  layoutMap,
  containerStyle,
  highlightedNodes,
  highlightedEdgeIds,
  setHovered,
} = diagram;

function toCSS(style: Record<string, string | number | undefined>) {
  return Object.entries(style)
    .filter(([, value]) => value != null)
    .map(([key, value]) => `${key.replace(/[A-Z]/g, c => `-${c.toLowerCase()}`)}:${value}`)
    .join(';');
}
</script>

<div class="relative" style={toCSS($containerStyle)}>
  {#each $nodes as node (node.id)}
    <article
      data-diax-node={node.resolvedId}
      style={toCSS(node.style)}
      on:mouseenter={() => setHovered(node.id)}
      on:mouseleave={() => setHovered(null)}
    >
      {node.data.content}
    </article>
  {/each}

  <DiagramEdges
    edges={$edges}
    layoutMap={$layoutMap}
    highlightedNodes={$highlightedNodes}
    highlightedEdgeIds={$highlightedEdgeIds}
  />
</div>
```

The measured edge layer depends on the `data-diax-node` attributes and the same `layoutMap` returned
by the store. Keep them inside one containing block.

Store interface [#store-interface]

| Value                    | Purpose                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `nodes`                  | Bound nodes with resolved IDs and CSS Grid styles            |
| `edges`                  | Parsed relations consumed by `DiagramEdges`                  |
| `layout`                 | Raw rows, columns and layout nodes                           |
| `layoutMap`              | Node lookup used for anchor direction                        |
| `containerStyle`         | CSS Grid container styles                                    |
| `highlightedNodes`       | Current highlighted path or `null`                           |
| `highlightedEdgeIds`     | Exact highlighted relation occurrences or `null`             |
| `updateOptions(options)` | Merges new semantic or layout input into the existing stores |
| `setHovered(id)`         | Updates highlight state                                      |

`updateOptions()` preserves the returned store objects while recomputing their values. Pass complete
replacement arrays for `nodes`, `relations` or `groups`; DiaX does not mutate caller-owned arrays.

```ts contract svelte
import { createDiagramStore } from '@diax/svelte';

const diagram = createDiagramStore({
  nodes: [{ id: 'draft', content: 'Draft' }],
  relations: [],
});

diagram.updateOptions({
  namespace: 'promotion',
  nodes: [
    { id: 'draft', content: 'Draft' },
    { id: 'review', content: 'Review' },
  ],
  relations: ['draft->review'],
});
```

`useDiagram` remains a deprecated compatibility alias during Alpha. New code should use the
framework-native factory name.

Independent payload types [#independent-payload-types]

The store independently preserves structured node content, edge labels, and group labels even
though the built-in Svelte component currently renders strings:

```ts
import { createDiagramStore } from '@diax/svelte';

interface NodePayload { title: string }
interface EdgePayload { protocol: string }
interface GroupPayload { badge: string }

const diagram = createDiagramStore<NodePayload, EdgePayload, GroupPayload>({
  nodes: [
    { id: 'web', content: { title: 'Web' } },
    { id: 'api', content: { title: 'API' } },
  ],
  relations: [{ from: 'web', to: 'api', label: { protocol: 'HTTPS' } }],
  groups: [{ id: 'backend', label: { badge: 'Internal' }, nodeIds: ['api'] }],
});
```

Ordinary non-empty definitions infer these types. Render the bound stores in one wrapper and keep
`DiagramEdges` beside the authored node DOM.


# SvelteKit & SSR (/docs/svelte/sveltekit)



SSR is supported [#ssr-is-supported]

`@diax/svelte` can render through Svelte's server compiler and hydrate through the client runtime.
The server emits deterministic diagram DOM and an empty edge shell; the client preserves that DOM,
measures nodes, and fills in pixel edge paths after hydration.

Use the component normally in a SvelteKit route:

```svelte contract
<script lang="ts">
  import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/svelte';

  const nodes = [
    { id: 'frontend', content: 'Frontend' },
    { id: 'api', content: 'API' },
    { id: 'database', content: 'Database' },
  ];
  const relations = ['frontend->api', 'api->database'];
</script>

<svelte:head>
  <title>Architecture</title>
</svelte:head>

<main>
  <h1>Architecture</h1>
  <FlowDiagram {nodes} {relations} />
</main>
```

The repository test suite uses a real Vite SSR compilation, renders the built Svelte component on
the server, hydrates it in a DOM, verifies stable node identity, and waits for measured edges:

```bash
pnpm --filter @diax/svelte test
```

When to disable SSR [#when-to-disable-ssr]

Disable SSR only when application-owned node content depends on a browser-only SDK, or when an
optional route intentionally has no useful server representation:

```ts title="+page.ts"
// SvelteKit host fragment: this opts the entire route out of SSR.
export const ssr = false;
```

This is not the recommended default for DiaX. It removes server-rendered content and can delay the
first meaningful view. The fragment is intentionally not a DiaX contract; a SvelteKit route fixture
would need to verify the chosen framework version, adapters, server bundle, and navigation behavior.

For one browser-only child rather than the whole route, keep the dynamic import and `{#if browser}`
policy inside an application wrapper. Do not add that complexity merely for DiaX measurement: the
official adapter already defers browser APIs until mount.

Hydration rules [#hydration-rules]

* Keep initial nodes and relations deterministic across server and client.
* Do not branch the first topology on `browser`, viewport width, random IDs, or local time.
* Expect node content and the edge shell in server HTML; expect final paths after client measurement.
* Keep browser-only application widgets behind their own boundary instead of disabling SSR for the
  entire diagram.
* Let adapter updates and observers remeasure content; do not persist DOM rectangles in a store.

Runtime boundary [#runtime-boundary]

The current evidence proves the Svelte adapter's SSR→hydration contract. It does not claim an
independent production fixture for every SvelteKit deployment adapter. If a deployment fails, check
that its resolver honors the package's `svelte` export condition and reproduce with the package test
before adding a client-only workaround.


# Advanced (/docs/solid/advanced)



Mindmap [#mindmap]

Use the `<Mindmap>` component or `layout: 'mindmap'` for center-outward radial diagrams:

Using the Mindmap Component [#using-the-mindmap-component]

```tsx
import { Mindmap } from '@diax/solid';

function TechRadar() {
  return (
    <Mindmap
      nodes={[
        { id: 'platform', content: 'Platform' },
        { id: 'frontend', content: 'Frontend' },
        { id: 'backend', content: 'Backend' },
        { id: 'infra', content: 'Infrastructure' },
        { id: 'react', content: 'React' },
        { id: 'node', content: 'Node.js' },
      ]}
      relations={[
        'platform->frontend',
        'platform->backend',
        'platform->infra',
        'frontend->react',
        'backend->node',
      ]}
      density="comfortable"
    />
  );
}
```

Using useDiagram with Mindmap Layout [#using-usediagram-with-mindmap-layout]

```tsx
import { useDiagram } from '@diax/solid';
import { For } from 'solid-js';

function TechRadar() {
  const { nodes, containerStyle } = useDiagram({
    nodes: [
      { id: 'platform', content: 'Platform' },
      { id: 'frontend', content: 'Frontend' },
      { id: 'backend', content: 'Backend' },
      { id: 'infra', content: 'Infrastructure' },
      { id: 'react', content: 'React' },
      { id: 'node', content: 'Node.js' },
    ],
    relations: [
      'platform->frontend',
      'platform->backend',
      'platform->infra',
      'frontend->react',
      'backend->node',
    ],
    layout: 'mindmap',
  });

  return (
    <div style={containerStyle()}>
      <For each={nodes()}>
        {(node) => (
          <div data-diax-node={node.resolvedId} style={node.style}>
            <div class="px-4 py-2 rounded-xl border border-white/8">
              {node.data.content}
            </div>
          </div>
        )}
      </For>
    </div>
  );
}
```

***

DOM ID Namespaces [#dom-id-namespaces]

Use `namespace` to prevent resolved DOM IDs from colliding when several diagrams share a page:

```tsx
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/solid';

function NamespacedDiagrams() {
  return (
    <div class="flex gap-8">
      <FlowDiagram
        namespace="fe"
        nodes={frontendNodes}
        relations={['gw->bff']}
      />
      <FlowDiagram
        namespace="be"
        nodes={backendNodes}
        relations={['svc->db']}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Node IDs become `namespace::nodeId` in the DOM. Each built-in renderer measures only its own
diagram container, so it does not draw an edge between these two canvases. Keep connected topology
inside one diagram. DOM-first Connect is public from `@diax/react/connect`, but a Solid Connect
adapter is not available yet.


# Custom Rendering (/docs/solid/custom-rendering)



Custom Rendering [#custom-rendering]

Use `renderNode` to customize how nodes look while keeping all layout logic. Both arguments are
Solid Accessors; call `node()` and `state()` inside JSX so highlight and data updates patch the
existing authored DOM instead of replacing it:

```tsx
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/solid';

<FlowDiagram
  nodes={nodes}
  relations={relations}
  renderNode={(node, state) => (
    <div
      class={`px-4 py-2 rounded-xl border ${
        state() === 'highlighted' ? 'ring-2 ring-blue-500' : ''
      } ${state() === 'dimmed' ? 'opacity-25' : ''}`}
    >
      {node().content}
    </div>
  )}
/>
```

Accessor typing [#accessor-typing]

The renderer contract is framework-native and can be named explicitly when you share renderers:

```tsx
import type { DiaxNode } from 'diax';
import type { NodeState } from '@diax/solid';
import type { Accessor, JSX } from 'solid-js';

type NodeRenderer = (
  node: Accessor<DiaxNode<string | JSX.Element>>,
  state: Accessor<NodeState>,
) => JSX.Element;

const renderServer: NodeRenderer = (node, state) => (
  <div data-state={state()}>{node().content}</div>
);
```

Node States [#node-states]

The value returned by `state()` tells you the current interaction state:

| State           | When              | Suggested style  |
| --------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| `undefined`     | Default           | Normal           |
| `"highlighted"` | On hover path     | Ring/glow effect |
| `"dimmed"`      | Not on hover path | Reduced opacity  |

Node Type Registry (`nodeTypes`) [#node-type-registry-nodetypes]

Define reusable node renderers by type, then reference them in the nodes array:

```tsx
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/solid';
import type { DiaxNode } from 'diax';
import type { NodeState } from '@diax/solid';
import type { Accessor, JSX } from 'solid-js';

type NodeRenderer = (
  node: Accessor<DiaxNode<string | JSX.Element>>,
  state: Accessor<NodeState>,
) => JSX.Element;

const nodeTypes: Record<string, NodeRenderer> = {
  gateway: (node, state) => (
    <div class="px-5 py-3 rounded-xl bg-indigo-500/10 border border-indigo-500/20 text-indigo-300">
      ⬡ {node().content}
    </div>
  ),
  service: (node, state) => (
    <div class="px-4 py-2 rounded-lg bg-emerald-500/10 border border-emerald-500/20 text-emerald-300">
      ● {node().content}
    </div>
  ),
};

function Architecture() {
  return (
    <FlowDiagram
      nodes={[
        { id: 'gw', type: 'gateway', content: 'API Gateway' },
        { id: 'auth', type: 'service', content: 'Auth Service' },
        { id: 'user', type: 'service', content: 'User Service' },
      ]}
      relations={['gw->auth', 'gw->user']}
      nodeTypes={nodeTypes}
    />
  );
}
```

**Resolution order**: `renderNode` > `nodeTypes[node.type]` > default renderer.

Stagger Animation [#stagger-animation]

Add entrance animation that staggers nodes layer by layer:

```tsx
<FlowDiagram stagger />        {/* Default 120ms delay between layers */}
<FlowDiagram stagger={200} />  {/* Custom 200ms delay */}
```

Stagger works with both `<FlowDiagram>` and `<Mindmap>`. You can combine it with reactive signals:

```tsx
import { createSignal } from 'solid-js';
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/solid';

function AnimatedDiagram() {
  const [staggerDelay, setStaggerDelay] = createSignal(120);

  return (
    <div>
      <input
        type="range"
        min={50}
        max={500}
        value={staggerDelay()}
        onInput={(e) => setStaggerDelay(Number(e.currentTarget.value))}
      />
      <FlowDiagram
        nodes={nodes}
        relations={relations}
        stagger={staggerDelay()}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```


# Edge Types (/docs/solid/edges)



Edge Types [#edge-types]

String DSL [#string-dsl]

```tsx
relations={[
  'a->b',           // Solid arrow
  'a-->b',          // Dashed arrow
  'a<->b',          // Bidirectional
  'a->|label|b',    // With label
]}
```

Object Form [#object-form]

For more control, use the object form:

```tsx
relations={[
  { from: 'a', to: 'b', style: 'dashed', color: '#E91E63' },
  { from: 'b', to: 'c', animate: 'flow', label: 'next' },
  { from: 'c', to: 'd', bidirectional: true },
]}
```

Animation Presets [#animation-presets]

| Preset              | Effect                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `"flow"`            | Flowing dashes along the edge  |
| `"pulse"`           | Breathing opacity effect       |
| `"shimmer"`         | Light traveling along the edge |
| `"reverse-flow"`    | Reverse flowing dashes         |
| `"reverse-shimmer"` | Reverse shimmer                |

Example with reactive animation selection:

```tsx
import { createSignal } from 'solid-js';
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/solid';

function AnimatedEdges() {
  const [animation, setAnimation] = createSignal<string>('flow');

  return (
    <div>
      <select onChange={(e) => setAnimation(e.currentTarget.value)}>
        <option value="flow">Flow</option>
        <option value="pulse">Pulse</option>
        <option value="shimmer">Shimmer</option>
        <option value="reverse-flow">Reverse Flow</option>
        <option value="reverse-shimmer">Reverse Shimmer</option>
      </select>
      <FlowDiagram
        nodes={[
          { id: 'a', content: 'Source' },
          { id: 'b', content: 'Target' },
        ]}
        relations={[
          { from: 'a', to: 'b', animate: animation() },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Custom Edge Labels [#custom-edge-labels]

Use `renderEdgeLabel` to customize how edge labels are rendered:

```tsx
<FlowDiagram
  nodes={nodes}
  relations={[
    'client->|REST|api',
    'api->|SQL|db',
  ]}
  renderEdgeLabel={(label) => (
    <span class="px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-indigo-500/20 text-indigo-300 text-xs font-mono">
      {label}
    </span>
  )}
/>
```

***

Edge Path Types [#edge-path-types]

Control how edges are drawn with the `pathType` prop:

Bezier (default) [#bezier-default]

Smooth cubic bezier curves — the default and most common style:

```tsx
<FlowDiagram
  nodes={nodes}
  relations={relations}
  pathType="bezier"
/>
```

Straight [#straight]

Direct straight lines between nodes:

```tsx
<FlowDiagram
  nodes={nodes}
  relations={relations}
  pathType="straight"
/>
```

Orthogonal [#orthogonal]

Right-angle polylines that follow horizontal/vertical paths only:

```tsx
<FlowDiagram
  nodes={nodes}
  relations={relations}
  pathType="orthogonal"
/>
```


# useDiagram Hook (/docs/solid/hooks)



Headless Hook — useDiagram [#headless-hook--usediagram]

The SolidJS binding uses `createSignal` and `createMemo` for fine-grained reactivity:

```tsx
import { useDiagram } from '@diax/solid';

function MyDiagram() {
  const { nodes, edges, layoutMap, containerStyle, setHovered } = useDiagram({
    // [!code highlight]
    nodes: [
      { id: 'a', content: 'Start' },
      { id: 'b', content: 'Process' },
      { id: 'c', content: 'End' },
    ],
    relations: ['a->b', 'b->c'],
  });

  return (
    <div style={containerStyle()}>
      <For each={nodes()}>
        {(node) => (
          <div
            data-diax-node={node.resolvedId}
            style={node.style}
            onMouseEnter={() => setHovered(node.id)}
            onMouseLeave={() => setHovered(null)}
          >
            <div class="px-4 py-2 rounded-xl border border-white/8">
              {node.data.content}
            </div>
          </div>
        )}
      </For>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Interactivity & Accessibility [#interactivity--accessibility]

Solid's `useDiagram` return bindings provide explicit properties for interactive styling and
supplemental accessibility metadata:

```tsx
<For each={nodes()}>
  {(node) => (
    <div
      id={node.resolvedId}
      data-diax-node={node.resolvedId}
      style={node.style}
      aria-flowto={node.ariaFlowTo}
      data-flow-state={node.flowState}
      onMouseEnter={() => setHovered(node.data.id)}
      onMouseLeave={() => setHovered(null)}
    >
      <div class="px-4 py-2 rounded-xl">{node.data.content}</div>
    </div>
  )}
</For>
```

* **ariaFlowTo**: Exposes serialized downstream DOM IDs as supplemental relationship metadata. Preserve `id={node.resolvedId}` so every reference resolves; do not assume a screen reader will navigate it as a graph command.
* **flowState**: Matches `"highlighted"` or `"dimmed"` when hover paths are active, allowing easy reactive styling.

Reactive Options [#reactive-options]

Pass an accessor function for reactive options — the diagram re-computes automatically when the signal updates:

```tsx
import { createSignal } from 'solid-js';
import { useDiagram } from '@diax/solid';

const [options, setOptions] = createSignal({
  nodes: [...],
  relations: [...],
});

const { nodes } = useDiagram(options);
// Updates automatically when options change
```

Return Values [#return-values]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  'nodes()': {
    description: 'Bound nodes with style and data',
    type: 'DiagramNodeBinding[]',
  },
  'edges()': { description: 'Parsed edges', type: 'ParsedRelation[]' },
  'layout()': {
    description: 'Layout computation result',
    type: 'LayoutResult',
  },
  'layoutMap()': {
    description: 'ID → LayoutNode map',
    type: 'Map<string, LayoutNode>',
  },
  'containerStyle()': {
    description: 'CSS Grid styles',
    type: 'Record<string, string>',
  },
  'highlightedNodes()': {
    description: 'Highlighted node set',
    type: 'Set<string> | null',
  },
  'highlightedEdgeIds()': {
    description: 'Exact highlighted relation occurrences',
    type: 'Set<string> | null',
  },
  setHovered: {
    description: 'Set hovered node',
    type: '(id: string | null) => void',
  },
}"
/>

All return values suffixed with `()` are Solid **Accessors** — call them to read their current value. Solid's fine-grained reactivity ensures only the affected DOM nodes re-render when data changes.

Reactive themes [#reactive-themes]

Theme selection is ordinary Solid state. DiaX does not add a second state abstraction around
`createSignal`; pass the current value to the diagram and let it own CSS injection:

```tsx
import { createSignal } from 'solid-js';
import { FlowDiagram, type ThemeInput } from '@diax/solid';

function App() {
  const [theme, setTheme] = createSignal<ThemeInput>('linear');

  return (
    <div class="p-8">
      <button onClick={() => setTheme(theme() === 'light' ? 'linear' : 'light')}>
        Toggle Theme
      </button>

      <FlowDiagram nodes={...} relations={...} theme={theme()} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

For a manual CSS-variable object outside a diagram, import `resolveTheme` and `themeToStyle` from
the explicit `diax/themes` leaf instead of loading that policy through the Solid root.

Independent payload types [#independent-payload-types]

The headless primitive accepts `useDiagram<NodeContent, EdgeLabel, GroupLabel>()`. The corresponding
node, edge, and group Accessors retain each payload type without converting them to a universal
value. Prefer inference and use explicit arguments only when an empty definition or a reusable
Accessor cannot provide enough context.


# SolidJS Guide (/docs/solid)



<InstallTabs packages="[&#x22;@diax/solid&#x22;]" description="SolidJS bindings (peer dependency: solid-js >= 1.8)" />

<Callout type="warn">
  **SolidStart / SSR**: `@diax/solid` publishes server and browser conditions. SSR emits stable node
  markup and an empty edge shell; measured paths appear after hydration. See
  [SolidStart & SSR](/docs/solid/solidstart).
</Callout>

Progressive API [#progressive-api]

DiaX provides three levels of control. Choose based on your needs:

| Layer | API                              | Best for                               |
| ----- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| 1     | `<FlowDiagram>` / `<Mindmap>`    | Quick usage, AI output, prototyping    |
| 2     | `<FlowDiagram renderNode={...}>` | Custom styling with your design system |
| 3     | `useDiagram()` hook              | Full headless control, library authors |

***

Quick Start [#quick-start]

The simplest way to use DiaX — just pass nodes and relations:

```tsx contract solid
import { FlowDiagram } from '@diax/solid';

function MyDiagram() {
  return (
    <FlowDiagram
      nodes={[
        { id: 'client', content: 'Browser' },
        { id: 'api', content: 'API Server' },
        { id: 'db', content: 'Database' },
      ]}
      relations={[
        'client->|HTTPS|api',
        'api->|SQL|db',
      ]}
      density="comfortable"
    />
  );
}
```

Density [#density]

Control spacing with the `density` prop:

| Value           | Description                             |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `"compact"`     | Tight spacing, good for inline diagrams |
| `"comfortable"` | Default, balanced spacing               |
| `"spacious"`    | Wide spacing, good for presentations    |

Direction [#direction]

```tsx
<FlowDiagram direction="horizontal" />         // Left to right (default)
<FlowDiagram direction="vertical" />            // Top to bottom
<FlowDiagram direction="horizontal-reverse" />  // Right to left
<FlowDiagram direction="vertical-reverse" />    // Bottom to top
```

| Value                  | Description                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `"horizontal"`         | Left to right (default)        |
| `"vertical"`           | Top to bottom                  |
| `"horizontal-reverse"` | Right to left (RTL flows)      |
| `"vertical-reverse"`   | Bottom to top (upstream flows) |

Layout Algorithms [#layout-algorithms]

Use the dedicated component for each layout type:

```tsx
import { FlowDiagram, Mindmap } from '@diax/solid';

<FlowDiagram nodes={...} relations={...} />  // DAG layout
<Mindmap nodes={...} relations={...} />       // Center-outward radial
```

***

Next Steps [#next-steps]

* [Custom Rendering](/docs/solid/custom-rendering) — Customize node appearance with `renderNode`, `nodeTypes`, and stagger animation
* [useDiagram Hook](/docs/solid/hooks) — Full headless control with Solid's fine-grained reactivity
* [Edge Types](/docs/solid/edges) — DSL syntax, animations, path types, and custom labels
* [Advanced](/docs/solid/advanced) — Mindmap layout and DOM ID namespaces
* [SolidStart & SSR](/docs/solid/solidstart) — Stable server markup and measured edges after hydration
* [Props Reference](/docs/solid/props) — Complete options and return values reference

<TypeTable
  type="{
